articleTitle: Perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and coercivity of Co/Ni multilayers
abstract: It is well known that Co/X multilayers show perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) below certain CO thicknesses, with X being a non- magnetic metal as Pd, Pt, Au, Ir, Ru. The possibility of finding PMA in multilayers, comprising two magnetic elements has so far been overlooked or dismissed. Recently, however, ab-initio calculations predicted a PMA for a Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>/Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> multilayer, which has been experimentally confirmed. This multilayer possesses a saturation induction of 1.0 T and shows a large magneto-optical Kerr effect. Thermo-magnetic writing of reversed domains has shown to be feasible. This paper reports on a detailed study of the anisotropy and coercivity of Co/Ni multilayers as a function of various deposition variables.

articleTitle: Track-edge noise versus erasure state
Effect of added Cu on the Nd-rich phase in hot-deformed NdFeB magnets
abstract: The addition of Cu greatly improve the hot workability of cast Pr(Nd)FeB magnets, which makes possible the production of aligned magnets by hot deformation of the cast structures. Substantial amounts of a liquid phase identified as the Pr (Nd)-rich phase are extruded from these materials during hot deformation. However, we have examined the liquid extruded by hot deformation from the Cu added NdFeB sintered magnets. It consists of three phases, instead of a single Nd-rich phase. We hot pressed sintered NdFeB (Cu) magnets to produce the magnetic alignment. As shown in Fig.1, Cu-free sintered NdFeB shows little ductility; however, the addition of 1.5at %Cu greatly improves the hot workability. Cu-containing sintered NdFeB always shows bumps (extruded liquid) on the sample surface after hot deformation.

articleTitle: Measurement of magnetic fields in axial field motors
abstract: Measurements of the magnetic field in three axial field brushless DC motors (Fig. 1) are described. Three different magnetic materials are used in these motors: rubber-bonded ferrite, Ceramic 5, and sintered neodymium-iron-boron (Nd- Fe-B). A closed form analytical equation for calculating the magnetic flux density, based on a 2-D approximation, is derived in a companion paper by E. Furlani. The measurements of the magnetic flux density are compared with the calculated values. Other authors have shown a variety of techniques for calculating the magnetic flux density, but little information is available on how well the analytical methods agree with measured values. A critical problem in comparing analytical calculations on permanent magnets with measured values is determining the state of magnetization, μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> M, of the magnet. In the present paper, core samples were taken from the center of the pole faces. Using the core samples, the flux density was measured and the state of magnetization was back calculated. This technique approximates the state of magnetization of the magnets.

articleTitle: Demagnetization effect in strip-line cavity measurements
abstract: Strip-line resonant cavities are useful for measuring the effective high frequency permeability (μ) of small samples of high permeability thin-film materials. However, in such an open magnetic circuit device, the effect of sample demagnetization can seriously degrade measurement accuracy unless recognized and corrected when necessary. A correction equation, approximate demagnetization factors, and a demagnetization effect map that aids identification of unreliable measurement results are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of tunneling magnetic force microscopy using a flexible triangular probe
abstract: Rice and Moreland have shown that magnetic data on a hard disk can be imaged with a tunneling microscope by using a flexible triangular probe cut from a thin film of magnetic material. We have assembled a similar device. Our aim is to use this microscope to not only image the microscopic magnetic patterns but to measure the constituent magnetic fields. To this end we have made a complete analysis of the interaction between the probe tip and a typical recorded pattern.

articleTitle: Magnetic circuit analysis of a linear synchronous motor with permanent magnets
abstract: Recently in factory automation, the conveyance using linear induction motors and linear pulse motors has been realized. However, this adopt open loop control in all cases, and due to such difficulties as controllability, efficiency, step-out and so on, there is the limitation in coping with high speed, high precision fields. Therefore, we paid attention to permanent magnet type linear synchronous motor (LSM) which have excellent servo performance as those for high speed, high precision conveyance. And we have investigated the magnetic circuit analysis when LSM was made into servomotor. This paper deals with the theoretical analysis and experimental results of static thrust and normal force of LSM.

articleTitle: Ultrathin Fe-based amorphous ribbons cores
abstract: Yagi et al. have fabricated ultrathin Co-based amorphous alloys which exhibit low loss properties. But ultrathin Fe-based amorphous alloys are not reported yet. We fabricated ultrathin Fe-based amorphous alloys the thickness of which is less than 5μm by single roller method in vacuum.

articleTitle: Shielding studies of electrochemically oxidised La/sub 2/CuO/sub 4/
abstract: Recently, Wattiaux et al induced superconductivity in the as prepeared semiconductor La<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>CuO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> (LCO) by electrochemical oxidation (e.o.) which was confirmed by others. We examine here in detail the shielding properties of the superconductor LCO prepared by e.o. Pellets of LCO were prepared by the usual solid state sintering technique. One part of the pellet (6x6x1.2 mm) was electrochemically oxidised as described before. The reaction was carried out for more than 48 h in 1N NaOH. Real (x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">'</sup>) and imaginary (x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">"</sup>) parts of the ac magnetic susceptibility were recorded as a function of T while warming up the sample in the presence of an applied d.c. field H(< 100 Oe) (i) after cooling the sample in zero H (labelled ZFR) and (ii) (for some fields) after cooling below T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> in the presence of H (FCR). The ac field amplitude (h) used was 0.1 Oe with a frequency f = 1500 Hz. Runs were also made with H = 0, h = 0.2 Oe at f = 150 Hz and 15 kHz. Some data were also taken on a powdered sample. The pellet showed a T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>(onset) of 44 K at H=0 (fig. 1 curve 8) and the width was 4 K. Preliminary results on the powdered pellet indicated a T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, of 40 K and the width increased to around 10 K. Further, x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">"</sup> showed an increase for T < 20 K but no peak was observed. For the pellet, peaks in x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">"</sup> are observed at T <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> in all runs.

articleTitle: Measurement of interaction fields in particulate tapes by linearization of the Henkel plot
abstract: Inter-particle interactions are a major source of noise in particulate recording media and, as such, impose limits on recoding densities. It is well-established that these interactions may be studied by isothermal (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>) and dc demagnetization (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</sub>) remanence measurements. Such measurements are usually analyzed using Henkel plots or the more recently introduced δ-I plots. In the absence of interactions, Wohlfarth's theory predicts that I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</sub> = 1 – 2I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>. Clearly, an experimental (Henkel) plot of I versus I results in a straight line of slope -2 for a non- interacting dispersion. In reality, the Henkel plot in the vast majority of commercial tapes bends below this straight line on account of 'negative' interactions. In this study, the interaction fields themselves have been measured by a process of re-linearization of the Henkel plot into the form of eq. (1) above. This has been done for a wide selection of commercial audio, video and digital tape media by replotting the Henkel plot data points in terms of an effective field which is the vector sum of the applied field and an interaction field which is taken as directly proportional to the tape magnetization.

articleTitle: Magnetic force scanning tunneling microscope imaging of overwritten data
abstract: In most digital recording systems, previously recorded data is not erased but simply written over. The extent of erasure of old data is a complex process that depends upon the recording parameters such as record current, record gap, densities and media parameters including coercivity and hysteresis. In addition, insufficient overwrite can also result from inaccurate electromechanical positioning of the record head during the re-recording process. Slight misalignment of the new data track relative to the previously written track results in incomplete erasure of the previous data, and residual magnetization of the old data persists along the track edges. This could have considerable implications on performance, as well as, on current notions of complete data erasure. To investigate this, we have developed a magnetic force scanning tunneling microscope to image magnetization patterns with sub-micron resolution, and applied it to commercially obtained hard disk media containing rewritten tracks.

articleTitle: First results in numerical simulation of domain structure in thin-film heads
abstract: We have developed a software that we intend to use for simulating the domain structure of thin-film magnetic recording head poles. The main points of this program are: 1. Minimization of the total energy of the material (Anisotropy, Exchange, Demagnetizing and Zeeman) under the non-linear constraint that magnetization keeps a constant norm. This is done by an original descent method: at each step we look for a descent direction that minimize first plus second derivative of total energy. 2. Splitting of the scalar potential used to compute demagnetizing field in order to tackle the problem of integration outside the material. 3. Assumption is made that the material is mono-domain in the thickness, thus we can formally integrate all the equations over the thickness. This leads to a geometrically 2D problem. 4. Use of finite elements for the discretization. The two first results have been computed for a 15 x 5 x 1 μm parallelepiped with easy axis of magnetization along the short axis of the material. We obtain the two structures of almost same total energy according to the initial state (Figures 1, 2, 3 and 4). This fisrt parallelepiped has been discretized with 60 x 20 first order hexahedric elements. Then, we present results for a 130 x 30 x 2 μm parallelepiped with easy axis along the short axis of the material. Under an applied field, we can notice the rotation of the main domains and the expansion or contraction of closure domains. This parallelepiped has been discretized whith 80 x 40 first order hexahedric elements.

articleTitle: Characteristic analysis of surface motor
abstract: Recently, in the X-Y drive system, the direct drive method with linear motor has been introduced and contributed practical use. It is reported that the X-Y plotter, using two linear motors (one to drive the X direction, the other to drive the Y direction), is being marketed. But the direct-drive Surface Motor ("SFM"), which has only one motor and moves in both the X and Y direction, has yet to be practically applied. Therefore, to make such an application a reality, we propose an SFM that drives in two directions using only one motor. However, this SFM has some problems, which require that we analyze its characteristic. To make that analysis, we first have to set UP a method for it. This reports describes the method of SFM analysis. The pattern of SFM's flux distribution is three-dimensional and complex, and a three-dimensional analysis method usable for the SFM have been not yet perfected. Therefore, we examine the three-dimensional approximate of two-dimensional analysis.

articleTitle: Energy considerations in hysteresis models
abstract: It is well known that the energy density lost in a closed magnetization cycle is equal to the area enclosed by the M-H loop. Mayergoyz and Friedman have suggested that the energy lost in a process which does not close upon itself can be computed from the Preisach model. Accurate Preisach models of hysteresis have been recently introduced that describe both reversible and irreversible processes. Comparison with experiment has shown that the locally-reversible magnetization depends not only on the applied field but also upon the state of the irreversible magnetization and the total magnetization. This factor complicates the computation of the energy loss for an open cycle.

articleTitle: Experimental validation and generalized theory of a single boundary eddy-current separator model
abstract: In a recent publication, the principles of a single magnetic field boundary eddy-current separator were delineated and a theoretical model that describes the progress, through the separator, of non-ferrous conducting elements of two basic filamentary geometries (see Fig. 1a) was proposed. Also reported were preliminary separation experiments which demonstrated the ability of the device to separate arbitrarily shaped conducting laminae from similar non-conducting elements. The theory presented allows the conductor penetration, y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>. of the field boundary to be calculated in terms of the system parameters for the filamentary model elements. In this work we report on: (a) the experimental justification of the filamentary theory, (b) the variance between filamentary theory and experimental when non-filamentary elements such as those shown in Fig. 1b are used, (c) a generalization of filamentary theory to embrace the extended element geometry, (d) a comparison of the generalized theory with experiment and (e) a further generalization of the theory to allow for leading edge eddy-current circulation and its effect on the agreement between theory and experiment.

articleTitle: Permeability anomaly of Co-based amorphous thin-film stripes
abstract: As the recording density and data rate of magnetic disk drives increase, magnetic thin film heads with narrow tracks will have to be used at high frequencies. An understanding of magnetization changes at high frequency for soft magnetic films is therefore important in designing high-performance heads. It has recently reported that the permeabilities of unlaminated Ni-Fe snipes decrease at high frequencies and those of laminated Ni-Fe/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> stripes show the flat frequency response. In this study, the permeabilities of laminated and unlaminated Co-based amorphous stripes are measured and the magnetization changes observed using a scanning Kerr effect microscope at high frequencies. It was found that the unlaminated stripes have some peaks in permeability and this phenomenon is related to the 180° wall motion.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties and domain structures in rpimary-recrystallized thin-guage Si_fe with orientation near [110][001]
abstract: This paper introduces the magnetic properties and domain structures of the new thin-gauge, 15-50μm thick, grain oriented Si-Fe. Inductions of these materials are 1.70-1.95T at 800A/m. These values are about 0.1-0.4T higher than those of conventional materials originally invented by M.F. Littmann. Core Losses of 50 μm thick materials are W15/400=9W/kg and W17/400=20W/kg and after laser irradiation they decrease to W15/400=8W/kg and W17/400=15W/kg. These values are about above 40% lower than those of conventional materials. The low core losses depend on the degree of (110) [001] orientation of primary recrystallized grains. That is to say, they decrease with increasing induction (B8). The decrease effects of core losses by laser irradiation is not found in the low B8 materials and increases with increasing induction. The grain size is 40-60 μm.

articleTitle: Measurement theory and experimental research on microwave permeability and permittivity by using the cavity characteristic equation method
abstract: The measurements of microwave permeability and permittivity for ferrite sample are carried out usually by using the cavity perturbation method. In order to avoid the perturbation-approximation error, we have suggested a cavity characteristic equation method (CE-method) and applied it in measuring the microwave permeability in the demagnetized state μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub> = μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub> ' – jμ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub> " successfully. In this paper, the CE-method has been developed for measuring ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub> = ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub> ' – jε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub> ", the theoretical inference, measurement technique, computational analysis and experimental research on μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub> and ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub> of this method are presented.

articleTitle: Partial grooving in vertical bloch line memory
abstract: Partially grooved regions in magnetic garnets, that are used to stabilize minor-loop stripe domains in Vertical Bloch Line memories, have been investigated in previous work using arrays of single 10%-deep grooves in garnets with zero-field stripe-widths of 5 μm. In this work, two 10% grooving steps were used to stabilize stripes in minor loops and magnetic bubbles in the major line in garnets with a zero-field stripe-width of 2.36μm, composition of (YBiGdHoCa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(FeGeSi)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> grown epitaxially on GGG, thickness of 2.26 μm, anisotropy field of 1920 Oe, saturation magnetization of 446 Oe, and characteristic length of 0.28 μm. Rectangular grooved regions, as shown in Figure 1, were used to confine the minor loop stripes, using groove depths of 10% and 20%, and groove widths of 1.25 μm, 1.5 μm, and 1.75 μm. Bias field margins were experimentally measured as well as computed using a two-dimensional, magnetic-domain computer simulation. The simulation assumes that uniform, unichiral stripe domains can be represented by a sequence of wall points whose motion is governed by the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, subject to applied fields, demagnetizing fields, and wall pressure, and a linear mobility subject to coercivity and wall saturation velocity.

articleTitle: Simple model of the high frequency permeability of narrow thin-film structures with eddy currents, walls, and structures
abstract: We report the derivation and experimental verification of a simple model of the high frequency permeability of narrow soft-magnetic thin film structures which includes eddy currents and magnetization rotation, wall motion, and saturation. Magnetic structures, such as mending heads, are modelled as connected sections of width, w, thickness D, resistivity p and magnetic properties: anisotropy H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>, saturation magnetization M, and wall coercivity H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cw</sub>. The easy magnetic axis is aligned perpendicular to the applied field. The model has two permeability terms: (1) from the easy-axis aligned domains, in which the bulk permeability (magnetization nitration) is radical by eddy currents and constricted by closure domains, and (2) from the hard axis regions, in which domain wall motion is described by the standard damping limited theory of wall motion solved for an oscillatory field. Saturation is handled by clipping the total moment change at 4πM, and replacing the wall phase delay with the transit time for a wall to cross the film.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal coupling structure of a ferrite loaded dielectric image guide
abstract: A novel coupled image guide was designed and tested from 26.5 to 40 GHz. The nonreciprocal structure consisted of two dielectric image guides separated by a YIG/GGG ferrite film (Fig. 1). Electromagnetic scattering matrix elements of the device were measured for the magnetic field applied perpendicular to the ferrite film plane. Nonreciprocal behavior in the scattering parameters were observed in agreement with analysis of reference. Our results indicated that various type of millimeter wave passive devices could be realized in a planar geometry, such as: isolators, filters, modulators, switches etc..

articleTitle: Effects of alloy composition and/or casting method on the amount Fe-precipitation in NdFeB alloys
abstract: According to the ternary Nd-Fe-B phase diagram, Fe-precipitation during the solidification of NdFeB alloy is anticipated because the solidification trajectory passes through a region of iron stability. The presence of Fe-precipitates not only causes difficulties in ingot crushing, pulverizing and fine milling but also lowers the magnetic properties and the corrosion resistance of NdFeB magnets. A dilute substitution of Nb, V or Ga for Fe has been known to improve the magnetic properties, in particular the intrinsic coercivity, the temperature coefficient of induction, and the corrosion resistance of NdFeB magnets. However, (the impact of these elements on) the precipitation of Fe during casting has never been discussed in the open literature.

articleTitle: Practical method for heat treating large toroids for pulse compression applications
abstract: To date few studies into the tailoring of the soft magnetic properties of the materials used in pulse compression elements have been published. Currently these cores are made from ferrites or amorphous alloy ship wound into toroids. Sheard showed the best method to treat a cobalt based alloy VAC 6030 was to stress relieve the completed core by heating and rapidly cooling by quenching in water. The important criterion was rapid cooling to avoid induced anisotropy. Whilst rapid cooling is possible with small test samples it is not viable for commercial size cores. Taub proposed a method of stress relieving the material into its final shape during winding, by passing the ribbon over a heated curved surface. This method becomes difficult as the curvature of the core changes during winding. A new method of heat treating cores by ohmic heating as they are wound is presented.

articleTitle: Demonstration of high data density recording on direct overwrite magneto-optical disk
abstract: Next generation Magneto-Optical (MO) disks must support high density recording; 0.5 μm/bit to 0.6 μm/bit which is twice the first generation recording density. They should also support direct overwrite (DOW). With this in mind, we have previously demonstrated that by adding a GdFeCo Readout layer which has no effect on the DOW function, the C/N of DOW-MO disks has been improved by 3 dB and it could be several dB higher than the C/N of first generation MO disks. Using this improved DOW-MO disk, we have achieved 21 % window margin at 0.54 μm/bit recording density using pulse width modulation.

articleTitle: Hysteresis in random collections of isotropic interacting particles
abstract: We find, on the basis of numerical computation, that random monolayers of single domain ferromagnetic spheres exhibit substantial remanence (squareness approximately 0.6) and a small coercivity (approximately 0.16 times the saturation magnetization in Gaussian units). The M vs H loops for such monolayers appear approximately universal, in that they are independent of the details of the sample geometry and packing fraction, provided that the latter is sufficiently high. Three dimensional random collections of single domain ferromagnetic spheres, on the other hand, show very small remanence (squareness less than 0.1). All of our computations are for collections of identical spheres, each having uniform magnetization and no crystalline anisotropy.

articleTitle: Exponential series statistical modeling of track misregistration in magnetic storage channels
abstract: The ability to predict off-track performance and to assess the efficiency or signal processing and coding schemes depends on having a good analytic representation of the track misregistration (TMR) noise. We apply the analytical method or exponential series expansion to empirical frequency distributions obtained from measurement of this noise in magnetic storage head-disk-assembly (HDA) devices. Traditionally, the analytic model used in the industry has been Gaussian distribution. The use of such a model reduces a huge mass or measurement data to a single number, the dispersion or variance, provided the origin is shifted to the mean value. The argument that is used to justify this procedure is the central limit theorem, which is an asymptotic result. Instead we compute analytic expressions that represent the deviation or the TMR frequency distributions from the Gaussian. The latter becomes the first term in a series of orthogonal functions with coefficients determined by the moments of the empirical distributions. This allows for adequately matching the tails or these distributions where the Gaussian fit is poor and there HDA performance predictions are most interesting.

articleTitle: Magneto-resistive head thermal asperity digital compensation
abstract: Thermal asperities, as they relate to Magneto-resistive heads, can modulate the readback signal on a hard dish drive to the point that error bursts will occur that exceed the power of the error correction code (ECC) used in a disk drive. Techniques have been derived that reduce this resultant error burst. This paper describes a technique that greatly reduces the resultant error burst lengths caused by thermal asperities in a disk drive using a sampling detector, and presents data from verification testing of the circuitry.

articleTitle: Hydrogen in ultrafine metal magnetic particles
abstract: The dim of this research is to present the unusual and extremely interesting magnetic properties of metal Co-B powders obtained by the borohydride reduction process using another apparatus for their production. The well known methods are so called “tea” and “Y” methods. Using the new technique of carring out the reduction process, considerably greater with smooth surface and nonporous particles are obtained but their magnetic parameters don't worsen.

articleTitle: CoPtCr composite magnetic thin films
abstract: The demand for increased recording density in hard-disk drives is never-ending. As recording density increases in longitudinal recording, reduction in the media noise becomes pronounced. It is well documented that the segregation of non-magnetic materials at grain boundaries reduces the intergranular exchange coupling between magnetic grains and decreases the media transition noise. To create media with low noise and high coercivity, Co-based magnetic alloy films are usually made on a Cr underlayer under a relatively high Ar pressure, to enhance the segregation of non-magnetic materials such as Cr or O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, at grain boundaries. In our study, we attempted to obtain longitudinal recording media that have high coercivity and low noise without using a Cr underlayer by co-sputtering CoPtCr alloys and non-magnetic compounds such as SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, SiN, ZrO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, or Sic.

articleTitle: Comparison between the mgneization obtained from Faraday balance and VSM or squid
An experimental sector servo system for a rotary head tape recorder
abstract: Reducing track pitch in a tape recorder increases storage capacity with less signal-to-noise ratio penalty than increasing the in-track density, provided head-to-track registration can be reliably maintained during playback. Traditional feedback controllers, which apply a control input based on an error signal filtered by a lead/lag network or PlD control, are ineffective in reducing tracking errors, since they require an impractically large servo bandwidth for effective error rejection. A significant component of the hacking error, which can be attributed to variations in tape guiding due to tape slitting errors and differences in the mechanical alignment on different tape transports, is periodic or slowly changing and can effectively be cancelled with a repetitive controller. An experimental sector servo system using such a compensator structure implemented on a D2 video production recorder significantly reduces tracking errors.

articleTitle: Magnetic orientation of acicular iron particle in recording media
abstract: Metal taps made from iron particles has been widely used as recording media for 8mm video, DAT, and HDTV system. The orientation of metal particle is a problem in the development of superior particle recording media. The magnetic orientation of iron oxide has been discussed in theory and in practice. Very few papers discussing orientation of metal tape have been found for the sake of commercial confidentiality. A. Ohtsubo had researched his MP-LIPS (Longitudinal Inside and Perpendicular Surface) metal tape. The degree of orientation inside the tape was doubtful if only the permanent magnet pairs was used for the alignment of magnetic metal particles. This paper describes the behavior of magnetic metal iron particles in an applied field. The best orientation process was found in order to produce a good metal tape with a high orientation.

articleTitle: Diminution of eddy-current losses in propagation of magneto-acoustic-wave in quasiperiodic multilayers
abstract: In order to reduce the eddy-current losses in the highly magnetostrictive amorphous film for constructing magneto-surface-acoustic wave (MSAW) devices, an effective method was developed with insertion of insulating layers in the film. In this paper, we present the numerical results of the propagation properties of Love-type MSAW in a new type of modulated structures.

articleTitle: High density recording on CoSm/Cr thin film media
abstract: Current research activities in high density longitudinal magnetic recording media are concerned with reducing medium noise and transition width. To lower the medium noise it is necessary to obtain thin films with magnetically non-interacting grains a few nm in size, and to minimize the transition width, a thin medium possessing a high coercivity is essential. A previous study reported that coercivities >2400 Oe could be obtained for 14 nm thick CoSm films grown on a Cr underlayer. Since that time coercitivities approaching 3000 Oe have been attained. We report here the recording results for high coercivity CoSm/Cr hard disks fabricated on glass substrates. The recording results were obtained at a flying height of 7.5 μin using a thin film inductive head which had 9 turns, 0.58 μm gap length and 28 μm pole tip width.

articleTitle: Controlled synthesis of differently textured Sm(Fe,T)/sub 12/ T = Ti, Ti+V, V sputtered films
abstract: We recently showed that ThMn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> type Sm(Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> films could be sputter synthesized for x values as low as zero where the third element T = Ti, V, Ti+V. This was a new result in view of the fact that in bulk form, the Sm-Fe-T 1-12 system does not stabilize for x < 0.1. The films reported exhibited extreme perpendicular anisotropy such that all crystallite c-axes were oriented perpendicular to the film plane. It is only for this texture mode that the remanent flux density can nearly equal the saturation value. We have now studied the texture changes in the 1-12 sputter synthesized films as a function of the third element concentration, sputter gas pressure and deposition temperature. The study was carried out for 0 ≤ x ≤ 0.2, for third elements T = Ti, V, Ti+V, substrate temperature in the range 660 K to 900 K, and sputtering gas pressure of 60 to 160 mTorr of Ar.

articleTitle: New structures for linear displacement sensor with high magnetic field gradient
abstract: This paper presents the design of new permanent magnet structures providing a high magnetic field gradient in an air gap for displacement sensor application. The proposed magnetic configurations are yoked and yokeless 2D structures, made of two units on each side of a rectangular air gap in which one insert a magneto elastic device.

articleTitle: Superior read/write characteristics of asymmetric ring head
abstract: Recently, asymmetric head at large inclination angle has been shown to equip with attractive read/write characteristics highly suitable for high density reading/recording purposes. To qualify for being a good read/write head it is essential that the head exhibits a very sharp head field gradient distribution since the latter means to give rise to a good correspondingly sharp transition width which is larger than the stability versus demagnetization limit has indicated. Further, in addition to having a wide band spectral response function, better still a gap-null free smooth response function, good reproducing efficiency or good SNR is also a pre-requisite. In this paper, we report superior read/write characteristics of asymmetric head at various inclination angles, delineating its essential features for what is required of a high density read/write head for both longitudinal and perpendicular modes of recording.

articleTitle: Non-conflict torque sensor using the difference of maximum induction of amorphous cores
abstract: For the power measurement of rotating machine, dynamic torque measurement is necessary. Amorphous alloy has been used for the development of torque sensor based on its high yield stress and magnetoelastic properties. Non-contact torque sensors using amorphous magnetic materials are economic due to their simple structure. In earlier works, the force sensor, which employs the change of the maximum magnetic induction as measurand, shows high dynamic properties. In this work, we applied this principle to non-contact torque sensor, namely the difference of the maximum magnetic induction of two amorphous cores was used as measurand.

articleTitle: Structure and magnetoresistance properties of Co/Cu multilayers
abstract: Artificially layered metallic materials have attracted considerable attention during recent year. One of the more interesting and potentially significant properties of magnetic multilayers is that of enhanced magnetoresistance. S.S. Parkin et al recently reported giant magnetoresistance for Co/Cu multilayer sputtered onto a silicon substrate with iron buffer layer at room temperation. We have prepared Co/Cu multilayers films on glass substrate with different thickness of buffer layer Fe. The films structure and magnetoresistance have been investigated. We found that giant magnetoresistance still existed in the multilayred films with the more amorphous structure. The buffer layer strongly influence on the structure and on the magnetoresistance of multilayered films.

articleTitle: On evaluation of shielding factor for 60Hz power source component in two-fold shell type magnetic shielding device
abstract: Recently, importance of magnetic shielding in new material fields and biomagnetic fields has markedly increased for the necessity of realizing the space of magnetic field which unlimitedly approches zero. Particularly, shielding to 60Hz commercial power source component is troublesome. For this purpose, two things have to be considered. One is on developments of the magnetic field sensor which is easy to handle and has a sufficient sensitivity of being able to detect a faint magnetic field close to zero, instead of SQUID. The other is dependent on constructions of the shielding system.

articleTitle: High abrasion resistive laminated sendust heads
abstract: Laminated sputtered Sendust (LSS) video heads. whose magnetic core is sandwitched between non-magnetic substrates. are expected to have excellent high frequency read/write characteristics, as well as Low rubbing noise at high relative tape-head speed, because of high saturation flux density, high permiability and low magnetostriction for the Sendust film. Head life depends on the substrate abrasion resistance. Abrasion resistance for conventional MnO-NiO ceramic, which shows good thermal expansion coherence with Sendust film, is not sufficient at high speed rubbing, about 20m/sec. CaO-TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is one of the most popular slider materials, because of its high abrasion resistance and its head processing ease. However, its about 1.1 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> thermal expansion coefficient (α) is too small to be used as a Sendust film substrate. The authors applied NiO added CaO-TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> ceramic, whose α is controlled by the concentration up to 1.5 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>, to the LSS head and suceeded in realizing practical durability and read/write characteristics.

articleTitle: Nitrogenated 1:12 compounds prepared by mechanical alloying
abstract: It was recently discovered that the planar anisotropy Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> compound exhibits a strong uniaxial anisotropy after a nitrogenation heat treatment where nitrogen enters the lattice interstitially and forms a Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> intermetallic compound. A similar behavior was also observed in the R(FeM)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>, compounds (M = Ti, Mo, V) with the tetragonal ThMn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> structure. A very high coercivity was obtained in Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> after mechanical alloying and a solid-state reaction. In this study we report the hard magnetic properties of Nd(FeM)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> powders obtained by mechanical alloying.

articleTitle: A low noise slotless parametric motor being much suited for the uses of quiet environment
abstract: In many places such as hospitals, offices, homes etc., the quiet environment has been required, and the reduction of acoustic noise which is mainly originated from a motor is desired. In the ordinary motor, the higher harmonics of the induced mmfs caused by the slots and teeth give rise to the harmonic distortion such as vibration, electromagnetic noise, rotating fluctuation etc.. The parametric motor has no slot and no tooth in a stator, therefore the noise parametric motor is expected to be lower than that of an ordinary motor. This report provides a comparative study of the acoustic noise of a parametric motor and an ordinary motor.

articleTitle: Effect of surface properties on cobalt modification of iron oxides
abstract: Cobalt modified iron oxides for high density magnetic recording applications have been consistently improved in recent years. However, the factors determining the effectiveness of the doping process are still not well defined. The purpose of this study is to identify in more detail surface properties of the gamma Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> that are important to the cobalt modification process.

articleTitle: Magnetorestive heads for magnetic tape and disk recording
Characterization of magnetic multilayers by grazing incidence x-ray reflectivity
abstract: Since the discovery of giant magnetoresistance in Cr-Fe films there has been a greatly enhanced activity in the study of magnetic thin films and multilayers. There has been particular interest in understanding why in some systems the magnitude of the magnetoresistance is strongly dependent on the growth method. As the interface morphology of layers grown by MBE and sputtering is likely to be markedly different, it is crucial to develop techniques for the measurement of interface roughness as this may have the significant effect on the magnetic behaviour. Grazing incidence X-ray reflectometry is one such non-destructive method for measuring layer thickness, period dispersion and interface roughness in thin films. We have undertaken an experimental and computational study of MBE grown multilayers to assess the sensitivity of the technique to yield interface roughness data on multilayers exhibiting novel magnetic properties.

articleTitle: Iron-alumina nanocomposites prepared by ball milling
Analytic analysis of a dual magnetoresistive head
abstract: A recently proposed dual magnetoresistive (DMR) reproduce head, consisting of two identical, adjacent MR stripes separated by a nonmagnetic spacer and connected electrically in parallel, was shown to have potential in very high density magnetic recording applications. The present work considers the micromagnetics of this coupled layer device, and derives approximate analytical expressions for the expected signal output as a function or in-track recording density. The results are found to be in good agreement with numerical computations based on reciprocity. Comparison with analytical results for other MR head configurations is discussed.

articleTitle: Substrate and process effects on thin Cr underlayer films
abstract: In order to grow hexagonal Co films with the c-axis oriented in the plane of the film a Cr underlayer having (200) crystallographic texture is desired. This (200) Cr texture is obtained by heating the substrate during deposition of the Cr. It has also been found that the coercivity of these films is increased and optimized when the Cr underlayers are thick (>2000 Å). Here we report that high coercivity CoNiCr films can be obtained at room temperature on thin Cr films grown both on single crystal Si and on glass. The crystallographic texture for these Cr underlayers differs.

articleTitle: Preparation of Co ferrite thin films with large perpendicular and in-plane coercivities by facing targets sputtering
abstract: Thin films of a spinel type of cobalt ferrite (CoFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) are very attractive because they exhibit large Faraday rotation angle, magnetocrystalline anisotropy and magnetostriction. They are expected to apply for devices such as magnetic recording media, magneto-optical devices, and SAW transducers and so on. Although Co ferrite has a lot of possibilities as high performance devices in near future, has been very difficult to prepare thin films with (l l l) orientation at low substrate temperature and without post-annealing.

articleTitle: New power supply method for soft magnetic material characterization at high flux density values
abstract: The characterization of soft magnetic material (magnetizing and specific losses W/Kg curves) has to be determinated in sinusoidal supply. Strong constraints are imposed by the International Standard on the total e.m.f. distortion induced in the secondary winding of the device under test (D.U.T.) (Epstein yoke, wound core etc.). When very high flux density values (up to 2.0 T) have to be reached, the possibility to have sinusoidal supply is not a simple task. The non ideality is related to the absorbed current harmonics content, since the magnetic non-linearity of the material under test. As a consequence, the magnetic material makers give the data sheet curves up to 1.8-1.9 T and the extrapolation to higher values is not to a simple problems to solve. The mend to increase the stress in the electrical machines cores for getting higher torque-volume ratio leads to a good knowledge of the magnetic material behaviour at high flux density. In order to supply the D.U.T. by sinusoidal waveform, the outhors in a previous paper used an audio quality power linear amplifier, but in this case the power supply limit of 300-400 VA seems to be not enought to use in this experiment. As a consequence, the authors propose an innovative supply method for having a good sinusoidal waveform. The supply is obtained using a single phase high switching frequency PWM inverter controlled by a voltage loop. In Fig. 1 a block diagram of the supply method is shown.

articleTitle: Domain imaging in magnetic garnets using tunneling-stabilized magnetic force microscopy
abstract: Magnetic domains in low-coercivity magnetic garnets have been imaged, ostensibly for the first time, using tunneling-stabilized magnetic force microscopy (TSMFM). In this imaging method, a triangular, Au-coated, thin-film, Ni-spring tunneling tip, as depicted in Figure 1, flexes in response to the sample's fringing magnetic field. The sample garnet is coated with a 1500 Å thick Au conductor to allow a tunneling current from the tunneling tip to flow and be used to maintain constant separation between the probe and sample. As the probe scans the sample's surface, the response of the spring to the fringing field is measured piezoelectrically and displayed, as shown in Figure 2. The Ni spring is designed to respond primarily to the vertical fringing magnetic field.

articleTitle: Micromagnetic structures of track-center and track-edge transitions recording in thin film media with a thin film head
abstract: Future rigid disk magnetic recording systems require heads with both narrower track widths and lower flying heights. As the recorded track width decreases, side writing and reading effects have a more significant affect on the performance of a system. Lower flying heights will affect the micromagnetic structures of the magnetization transitions at not only the center of the track but also at the edge of the track. Both of these effects will have a significant affect on the signal and noise characteristics of a system. The magnetic structure of recorded transitions have been investigated by several techniques including Bitter colloid technique, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy (TEM), spin-polarized scanning electron microscopy with polarization analysis (SEMPA), and magnetic force microscopy (MFM). Lorentz microscopy was used to study the sawtooth or zig-zag wall structures and magnetic vortices at the center of recorded transitions and the micromagnetic structures near track edges of tracks. The purpose of this paper is to describe a new technique for obtaining clearer micromagnetic structures of track-center and track-edge transitions recorded in high-coercivity thin film media with a thin film head by superimposing the sharp "bright lines" of over-focused and under-focused Lorentz Fresnel TEM images of the same transition.

articleTitle: Domain collapse in amorphous magnetostrictive wires
abstract: Recently magnetic amorphous wires have been widely used in sensor technique. The applications are based on the domain dynamic processes which are characterized by a number of peculiarities caused by a combination of the wire geometry and stress induced anisotropy. Here we have investigated the domain collapse at a collision of two domain walls in Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">77.5M</sup> Si<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.5</sup> B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> amorphous wires under longitudinal tension (up to 1700 MPa). At this process a sharp voltage pulse which is very useful for application is generated. The data obtained have been analyzed on the basis of an ellipsoidal domain model.

articleTitle: Magnetic property and microstructure dependence of CoCrTa/Cr media
Magnetic properties of rapidly quenched RF/sub e7/Si/sub 6/ alloys
abstract: Since the discovery of Sm(Pr)Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> permanent magnet, much effort has been devoted to substituting iron for cobalt in it. Recently, by means of rapidly quenched method, we got some RF e binary and RFeSi ternary alloys, whose x-ray diffraction lines correspond to that of hexagonal CaCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5<sub>-type structure. In this paper, we mainly report the magnetic properties of the GdFe<sub>7</sub>Si<sub>x</sub>, and ErFe<sub>7</sub>Si<sub>x</sub> (0 ≤ x ≤ 2.5) day systems.</sub></sub>

articleTitle: Torque sensor using perpendicularly magnetizing coil
abstract: Various magnetic torque sensors for rotational shafts have been proposed up to now to establish high level torque control systems for automobiles, industrial robots and dining systems. These toque sensors have been classified into two groups: torsional-angle detection type (Δ θ -type, for short) and magnetostrictive λ-type, for short). λ -type sensors are required (Δ θ -type sensors due to their compactness in size. Requisite features for development of reliable λ -type sensor are (i) forming a sensitive and stable magnetostrictive layer (λ -layer, for short) on a steel shaft with extreme strength, (ii) stable detection of the stress-magnetic effect of the λ -layer independently of the steel shaft, and (iii) stable torque detection for the temperature variation of the steel shaft and the λ -layer. For requisite feature (i), me have formed Ni40Fe56Cr4 λ -layer with thickness of 600-1300μm on a carbon steel shaft (S45C) and a stainless steel shaft (SUS304) using a low-pressure plasma spray method. For (ii). we have constituted the Twin-coil which magnetizes the λ -layer perpendicularly to the shaft surface (Fig.1). The twin coil method can avoid the influence of the stress-magnetic effect of the steel shaft compared with conventional ring coil methods in which the magnetizing direction is coincident to the easy magnetizing direction of the shaft. For (iii), we newly constructed a compensation system using a new temperature sensor due to a non-induction coil. The variation of torque sensor output for the temperature variation of the steel shaft can be compensated using a value which changes only with temperature variation independently of the applied torque.

articleTitle: A load cell utilising and amorphous ribbon material as the primary element
abstract: There is an ever growing demand for the development of novel or the improvement of existing transducer technologies that will satisfy the quite hostile environments that common place in todays highly automated world. The widely reported superior soft magnetic and magnetoelastic properties displayed by amorphous materials have been exploited in a number of novel and existing transducer technologies. In the latter cam, the onus is on proving the implementation of the new material as the primary element in the existing scheme of operation provides such benefits as to warrant the subsequent change in technology. The actual composition of a particular alloy dictates the material properties and potential applications. In this investigation a selection of as-cast and annealed alloy compositions were examined under various electromagnetic operational conditions including variation of ambient temperature.

articleTitle: Giant magnetoresistance in Ni-Fe/Cu multilayers formed by ion beam sputtering
abstract: Giant magnetoresistive effects have recently been found in various magnetic multilayered films. In Fe/Cr, CO/Cu and Co/Ru multilayers, the oscillatory magnetoresistance changes were observed as the thickness of the non-magnetic layer was varied. However, Ni-Fe based multilayers to show oscillatory magnetoresistance changes have not yet been reported. This study investigates Ni-Fe/Cu multilayers formed by ion beam sputtering. Ion beam sputtering has not been used much in the formation of the multilayers to show high magnetoresistive effects. We observed magnetoresistance oscillation as the thickness of the Cu layer changes in Ni-Fe/Cu multilayers. The Ni-Fe(1 nm) / Cu(1 nm) multilayer shows magnetoresistance of 18.8% at room temperature.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Fe/sub 3/GeN/sub x/
abstract: Fe <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ge crystallizes in two modifications. The high temperature phase exhibits a hexagonal crystal structure of the Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Sn-type with the space group P6<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/mmc. The low temperature phase crystallizes in the face centered cubic (FCC) Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Au-type with the space group Pm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>m. Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ge absorbs nitrogen under mild conditions of temperature and pressure. A few years ago, Stadelmaier et al. and Boller reported that nitrogenation of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ge results in a change in the crystal structure to the tetragonal (FCT) Cr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>AsN-type with the space group 14/mcm. Magnetic properties of the nitrides of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ge have not been published in the literature. The objectives of the present work are to optimize the conditions for the formation of the nitrides of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ge and examine their magnetic and structural properties. We also propose to extend this work to include other transition metals. In view of the considerable interest of the nitrides of rare earth-transition metal intermetallic compounds, it seemed pertinent to examine pure transition metal-based nitrides.

articleTitle: A magnetorestrictive direct drive rotary motor
abstract: Several concepts based on magnetostrictive drives have been attempted, all with varying degrees of success. In this digest a distinctly different approach using magnetostrictive drive rods and a roller locking principle for clamping is described. Fig. 1(a) illustrates the roller locking concept. Fig. 1(b) shows the proposed design. The drive assembly consists of two concentric races, in which one is circular (drive drum - which is positively connected to output shaft) and other cylinder having cams on its outer rim (drive cam cylinder - which is free to rotate on shaft, and is driven by a pair of magnetostrictive rods) with a roller above each cam. Relative rotation which wedges the rollers between the narrow portion of the cam and the circular surface of the outer race forces both races to rotate together, while dative rotation in the opposite direction frees the rollers. In order to provide dual directional motion two sets of drive rods and a modified drive cam cylinder is incorporated in the design. The top half of the drive cam cylinder has cam oriented in such a way as to generate counterclockwise motion. The bottom half of the drive cam cylinder has cam oriented in reverse fashion to facilitate motion in clockwise direction. The performance of the motor can be evaluated by number of benchmarks like torque, speed, and wear etc. Torque capacity for a given geometry of the motor is established by three considerations: Hertz contact stresses, hoop stresses and deflections. The frequency response of the motor depends on the inertia of the motor.

articleTitle: Orientation and angular dependence of magnetic properties for Ba-ferrite tapes
abstract: It has been demonstrated that Ba-ferrite tapes have excellent high frequency response, in spite of the fact that their coercivity and saturation magnetization are rather smaller than those for metal particulate tapes. This paper discusses the reason why Ba-ferrite tapes have such excellent high frequency responses, by investigating angular properties, squareness and switching field distribution (SFD) for Ba-ferrite tapes with different orientations. In this study, Ba-ferrite tapes with non-orientation. perpendicular orientation, and longitudinal orientation were prepared, using Ba-ferrite particles with about 50nm average diameter and about 3.5 diameter-to-thickness ratio.

articleTitle: Magnetoresistance and galvanomagnetics in bias sputtered Co/Cu multilayers
abstract: Recently Parkin et al reported oscillatory magnetic exchange coupling through thin Cu layers and giant magnetoresistance ΔR/R of more than 65% at 300K in Co/Cu multilayers sputtered onto a silicon substrate with Fe buffer layer. For magnetoresistive sensor application, the larger differential magnetoresistance (ΔR/R . ΔH) is desirable, where ΔH is the field value at half maximum of ΔR/R. Giron et al reported the value of 1.4 kOe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at room temperature in Co/Cu multilayers sputtered on Si(100) wafers. Here, we report on the giant magnetoresistance and extraordinary Hall effect in Co/Cu multilayers sputtered on glass substrates with negative bias voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>.

articleTitle: Low temperature magnetization behavior in nanocrystalline materials: spin waves
abstract: The low temperature magnetization behavior of the ferromagnetic samples can be explained by means of the spin waves excitation theory. In this work we tray to explain the behavior of the saturation magnetization applying the usual spin wave model in nanocristalline materials.

articleTitle: Effect of azimuth angle and bias field on second harmonic distortion in differentially biased MR heads
abstract: The magnetoresistance effect in a thin permalloy film is a quadratic function of the applied field until the onset of saturation and is often written as R = Ro + dR cos<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>A where A is the angle the internal field B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> makes with the sense current direction due to an externally applied field. Ro the resistance at zero applied field and dR is the magnetoresistance. As saturation approaches, the gradient of the MR characteristic begins to reduce a t which point a quasi-linear region exists for small inputs. This point also is the point of maximum gradient and is often called the optimum bias point as it delivers the maximum output per unit input current. A DC bias field. Bb, is normally applied to operate close to this region. In the purely quadratic region of the characteristic the use of opposing bias fields and differential sensing from two indentical (half) elements eliminates the second harmonic terms by perfect cancellation. The equations governing the read response for each half element below the onset of saturation derived from equation 1, V1 & V2 are:- V(1,2) = I Ro 2 (dR Ro) Bt<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (dBy<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sup> ± 2Bb dBy) dBy is the input field, Bb the bias field applied in the + or - direction and B1 the internal field. As can be seen for differential sensing the dBy<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> term would disappear if they were equal. However, this cancellation is only "perfect" under the following conditions (a) each half element carries the same bias current, (b) each half element is magnetically identical or (c) the input flux to each half element is the same. Condition (c) is not met when there is some azimuth angle between the MR element and the recorded data on a tape or disk. For even a small azimuth angle the value of dB, for each half would differ as the sinusoidal wavefront would arrive at the element at slightly different times. The effect of azimuth angle.

articleTitle: Observation of the antiferromagnetic resonance in dicalcium ferrite
abstract: Submillimeter spectra (10 - 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) were investigated in Ca<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> by Fourier spectrometry in zero magnetic field at temperatures 4.2 - 350 K. Two modes of magnetic origin have been observed which are supposed to be antiferromagnetic resonance modes. It was found that effective anisotropy fields in the planes ca and cb of the orthorhombic antiferromagnet differ more than in an order. Dicalcium ferrite Ca<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> is an orthorhombic antiferromagnet (space group - D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2h</sub> Pcmn, T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sub> = 725 K) with the spins alined along the c axis and slightly canted towards the a axis. The Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions occupy two different sites (octahedral and tetrahedral coordination) in the layers parallel to ac plane which alternate along the b axis. The two nonequivalent layers are antiferromagnetic and interlayer interaction is also antiferromagnetic.

articleTitle: Planar imperfections in th Pr/sub 3/Fe/sub 14/B ribbons with Cu, A1 and Zn substitutions
abstract: The coercivity of melt-spun Pr-Fe-B ribbons has been found to increase with small additions of Cu, Al and Zn. The enhancement in coercivity was attributed to grain size reduction and the modification at the grain boundary regions. High resolution electron microscopy on substituted samples showed "disturbed lattice' regions at most of the grain boundaries and secondary phases rich in the added elements mostly at triple grain boundaries. In the present work we report on some defects observed in the 2:14:1 grains. Imperfections in the form of extrinsic atomic layers and distorted layers were encountered in the grains of the 1.5 at % Cu specimen. Steps of defects parallel to the (001) planes of the 2:14:1 phase are shown in fig. 1. The areas under stress were revealed iby their different contrast at the ends of each defect and at the grain boundaries. Extrinsic lattice layers are seen clearly in fig. 2. The sharp contrast at the defect areas indicates stress concentrations caused by these extrinsic layers.

articleTitle: A method for assessing eddy current effects in pulsed magnetometry
abstract: The magnetic properties of emerging rare-earth permanent magnets are beginning to exceed the limits for which their hysteresis loop can be measured to an acceptable accuracy in systems employing iron-yoked electromagnets, eg. the dc permeameter. However the most widely used alternative, which is capable of producing magnetic fields far in excess of those obtainable with iron-yoked systems, is the superconducting vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM), which suffers from the drawbacks of having high capital and running costs and a limited peak field capability. Therefore, there is a growing interest in developing a more economic and flexible method based on the production of pulsed fields by the discharge of capacitors into a conventional resistive solenoid. Although pulsed field magnetometry for material characterization is well established in basic materials research, when magnetic fields in excess of 40T are now commonly employed, at present their use for the routine characterisation of rare-earth permanent magnets, which are produced in a wide range of geometries, is limited.

articleTitle: Effects of high temperature creep on magnetic properties of steels
abstract: It is known from the work of Kersten and Neel that the magnetic properties of various steels are sensitive to the total volume of inclusions. These inclusions can be precipitates of interstitial or substitutional solutes, or microscopic voids in the material. Neel has shown that when a domain wall intersects a spherical void for example, there is a reduction in magnetostatic energy of ΔE = Πμ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sup>/9 where M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> is the saturation magnetization of the material and r is the radius of the void. When a material is subjected to stress at elevated temperatures for extended periods it is likely to suffer what is known as creep damage, which amounts to a very slow plastic flow of the material. The plastic flow leads to a build up of dislocations within the material and this leads eventually to microscopic voids, cavities and finally macroscopic cracking of the material. This whole phenomenon has been dealt with in detail by, among others, Evans. The problem is currently a major cause for concern in power plants in which high pressure high temperature pipelines are susceptible to failure.

articleTitle: Inhomogeneities and coercivity of soft permalloy thin films
abstract: Coercivity mechanisms in thin permalloy films due to inhomogeneous distributions of in-plane uniaxial anisotropy me investigated numerically, utilizing a two-dimensional domain wall model. The distribution of anisotropy could be attributed to the polycrystalline grain structure of thin films, as well as magnetostrictive stress.

articleTitle: Environmental 50Hz magnetic fields measurements
abstract: Exploration of environmental 50Hz magnetic fields is of value because of several reasons. On one hand it probably enables identifying regions where the 50Hz magnetic fields are often and for relatively long periods of time of dangerous levels. Anther application of such exploration is in enabling an identification of locations where the fields are usually small, and as a result, such locations are useful for ELF receiving stations. The latter are valuable mainly in geophysical investigations. The present work is related to a relatively narrow band of measured frequencies. As a result, there is no need to resort to complicated methods of magnetometry, and a relatively simple instrumentation based on a tuned search coil is adequate.

articleTitle: Domain wall dynamics in TbFeCo thin films
abstract: Experiments on thermomagnetic bit recording in RE-TM films have shown that bit formation takes place in two stages: an initial nucleation followed by domain wall motion process [1,2]. The final size and shape of the domain as well as a the possibility of direct overwriting strongly depend on domain wall dynamics [3,4]. The present work deals with the domain wall dynamics in amorphous TbFeCo films with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in external magnetic fields up to 13 kOe at room temperature. The Tb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>(Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B5</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</sub> films with 15 <x <30 were obtained by method of magnetron RF-sputtering of composite target in an argon atmosphere. Thickness of films used in experiments was ˜ 800 A. All the films were protected on both sides by layers of silicon nitride.

articleTitle: Microstructure characterization of Sm-Fe-Zr melt-spun hard magnetic systems
abstract: The high intrinsic coercivity (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">CImax</sub> = 12.8kOe) of some of the melt-spun Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">73</sub>-Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">27-x</sub> Systems, along with the identification of a new hard magnetic phase in the mechanically alloyed materials with high Sm content, sparked interest in the study of the microstructure of melt-spun Sm-Fe-Zr systems. Several batches of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">73</sub>-Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">27-x</sub> melt-spun at v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>=50m/s and v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>=30m/s were considered in the present work, with x=14 and x=20, and with respective intrinsic coercivities of 3.4kOe and 12.8kOe.

articleTitle: Structure and magnetic properties of hot pressed Dy/sub 3-x/R/sub x/Al/sub 2/ system
abstract: Thirty years ago it was recognized that Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>A1<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> possessed some interesting permanent magnet properties such as large energy product of 73 MGOe and an almost square loop (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ci</sub>=21 koe). However, the Curie temperature is low (105 K) and the magnetic properties diminish rapidly as the temperature is increased from 4.2 K. Utilization of Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>A1<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> as a permanent magnet material would require an improvement in the Curie temperature as well as an improved temperature dependence of the remanence, coercivity and energy product.

articleTitle: Effect of biaxial stress on magnetoacoustic emission from nickel
abstract: When magnetization changes by the motion of non-180° domain walls, magnetostrictive strains also change, giving rise to magnetoacoustic emission (MAE). Since the presence of structural defects and residual stresses modify the magnetic domain configuration and hence alter the MAE signals, MAE has been under development as a non-destructive testing technique for the monitoring of defects and stresses in magnetic materials. The possibility of measuring biaxial stresses in mild steel by MAE has recently been studied. In this paper we report the effect of biaxial stress on MAE measurements from nickel.

articleTitle: Micro-annealing studies of Pt/Co multilayers for magneto-optic recording applications
abstract: Pt/Co multilayer films are currently generating substantial interest as possible 'next-generation' magneto-optic recording films. This is due primarily to the fact that they exhibit a Kerr rotation which increases with decreasing wavelengths. The Pt/Co layers are also expected to be much more stable to oxidation than typical rare-earth/transition-metal (RE-TM) media presently available, resulting in improved ageing properties. However, little work has so far been carried out to assess in detail the ageing behaviour of these films. Of particular concern might be the integrity of the layer interfaces when subjected to thermal fatigue induced by repeated write cycles; since it is the quality of these interfaces which many workers believe determines the degree of perpendicular anisotropy. A few bulk annealing studies have been performed, but these reveal some contradictory effects, identifying both cross-boundary atomic diffusion and crystallite growth as significant ageing mechanisms. Such bulk annealing studies, although undoubtedly of great value, do not truly mirror the thermal processes present in a real recording situation. In this paper we present the results of micro-annealing studies of a range of Pt/Co multilayer structures in which the magnetic, structural and recording properties of microscopic regions were monitored whilst subjecting the samples to up to 400 million write cycles.

articleTitle: The origin of crystallographic texture produced during hot deformation in rapidly-quenched NdFeB permanent magnets
abstract: The texture produced by hot deformation ("die-upsetting") of rapidly-quenched NdFeB permanent magnets greatly enhances the energy product of the material. Considerable effort has been made to understand the mechanism of this orientation, which remains controversial in spite of extensive microstructural studies by saved research groups. Our previous work has shown that the texture forms mainly by the preferential growth under compressive stress of favorably-oriented grains by means of mass transport through a liquid phase at the grain boundaries. A quantitative model is to support this suggested mechanism. This paper presents a calculation based on a liquid diffusion model and shows that the calculated results are consistent with the experimental data.

articleTitle: Characterization of nitrogenation of Sm/sub 2/Fe/sub 17/
abstract: Newly developed Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>Nx intermetallic compounds have been gathering interest as new permanent magnets. Energy products of 21 MGOe of compressed body made from Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> powder has been reported. We focused on the gas-solid reaction of nirogenation of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>.
