The relation of conditions of nitrogenation and the nitrogen phase in Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, especially distribution of nitrogen in nitrogenated particles was carefully evaluated.

articleTitle: An inductor/capacitor hybrid made of ferrite only
abstract: Ferrite is magnetic as well as dielectric and the specific permittivity and the resistivity are 10-20 and more than 1M Ω m, respectively in N1-Zn ferrite. By using these properties of N1-Zn ferrite a new type inductor/capacitor hybrid resonant component (L/C hybrid, hereafter) is developed. This paper describes the construction of prototype L/C hybrid and its characteristics.

articleTitle: Effect of nitrogen content in magnetic properties of Sm/sub 2/Fe/sub 17/N/sub x/ and SmFe/sub 5/N/sub y/ alloys
abstract: The nitrogenization of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> enhances the Curie temperature and magnetic anisotropy and induces uniaxial anisotropy. They are thus potential permanent magnet materials and have extracted extensive attention. However, they were found to decompose at high temperatures, hence sintering is less possible. In this study, Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> alloys with different nitrogen contents were explored, those with nitrogen less than a certain level was found to be stable at high temperatures. The possible stabilization effect of nitrogen on the Sm-Fe 1:5 phase, and its high temperature stability are also presented.

articleTitle: Maskless patterning of ferrite films by laser-enhanced ferrite plating in aqueous solution
abstract: Ferrite plating facilitates the formation of polycrystalline spinel ferrite films in an aqueous solution below 100 °C. This enables the use of heat-sensitive materials such as plastics as substrates, and allows the deposition of ferrite films on devices (e. g., GaAs IC) degenerated by exposure to high temperature. In the conventional ferrite plating, the film deposition rate is -15-30 nm/min, which is insufficient for the practical production of ferrite film devices. To solve this problem we have recently developed "light-enhanced ferrite plating" in which the substrate is heated by a Xe-lamp and the deposition rate is increased to -320 nm/min, by factor of -10. By substituting the Xe-lamp with an Ar-laser, we have further increased the deposition rate up to -2350 mm/min, and successfully drawn ferrite film pattern by selective growth of the film without using masks. We call this "laser-enhanced ferrite plating". In this paper, we describe the experimental method of laser-enhanced ferrite platin and the maskless patterning, and report the deposition rate and magnetic properties of the plated films.

articleTitle: Magnetic and thermomagnetic analysis of 4 megabyte barium ferrite flexible disks
Implantable soft heating device using temperature-sensitive amorphous metal flakes and prptotype heating system
abstract: The SOFT AEATING method is a kind of induction heating method which utilizes temperature sensitive magnetic materials implanted Inside a body or tissue. In this method, the maximal temperature Is controlled automatically by the Curie temperature, therefore temperature control system is not necessary. In this paper, as a SOFT HEATING device, temperature sensitive amorphous metal flakes consisting of Fe-P-C-Cr were prepared. We have measured the generation of heat in phantom and discussed the performance of the prototype system.

articleTitle: Giant magnetoresistance with low saturation field in Co/sub x/Fe/sub 1-x//CU multilayers
abstract: Magnetoresistance (MR) of magnetic multilayers has been actively investigated by many research group, and giant MR has been observed for Fe/Cr and Co/Cu multilayers, which have a potential to be applied for magnetic sensor devices. MR ratio, however, under the small magnetic field is quite small, because the saturation field (H-) of these multilayers is very large up to 10 kOe or more, and this will limit its application for the magnetic sensors. In this study, we report that giant magnetoresistance at room temperature up to 62% with low saturation field of 0.9kOe can be attained in (Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>/Cu)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> multilayers. A set of (Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>/Cu)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> multilayers was prepared by the ion beam sputter deposition method from Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub> and Cu targets on MgO (110) single crystal substrates. Base pressure was 5 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> Torr and sputtering was carried out using 1.3 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> Torr argon Ions. Acceleration voltage (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> for sputtering was changed from 300V to 1kV in order to change the interface state. Structure was investigated by X-ray diffraction measurements. Magnetoresistance was measured using conventional four-point geometry with magnetic field in the films. The magnetic properties of the films were investigated by vibrating sample magnetometer.

articleTitle: New organic ferromagnet of pyrolysed polyvinylchloride
abstract: After the first report of the organic ferromagnet (poly-BIPO) quite a number of works devoted to a ferromagnetism in organic substances has appeared (see the review articles). At present the intensive search are being carried on of new organic ferromagnets with the high saturation magnetization. Here we first report of obtaining the new organic ferromagnet by the pyrolysis of a polyvinylchloride (PVCH). A technical PVCH (-CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>CHCH1-)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub>, having the molecular mass of about I.2xIO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> was used for pyrolysis in vacuo. The temperature in- crease was realized in the descrete steps on IOOK with the delay of I h on each reached value. The obtained product was crushed by the ultrasonic disperser into a powder with the average grain size of about 80 μm. The ferromagnetic phase formation versus the PVCH pyrolysis temperature (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>) was studied by two independent methods such as the electronic spin resonance (ESR) and the vibromagnetometer.

articleTitle: Microtrack profiling technique for narrow-track tape heads
abstract: Microtrack properties of magnetoresistive (MR) heads are particularly useful for predicting the off-track performance as well as the domain structure and stability of the sensors. Conventional microtrack profiling techniques used on DASD heads involve stepping the head in small increments on a narrow track written by partial erasure of another track. This method is difficult to apply to narrow tape heads due to the required precision with which the tape must be guided through the transport. We present a new technique for rapid and dynamic measurement of microtrack profiles for tape heads as narrow as 5 μm. The method uses a narrow track written in a serpentine trajectory down a length of tape as shown in Fig. 1. A 5 μm videocassette head is sinusoidally translated perpendicular 10 the tape travel direction by a voice coil actuator. The write current is enabled only in the linear portion of one direction of the sinusoid. The written pattern is a square wave in the density range of 500-2000 fr/mm. The read head of interest is then mounted on a linear translator and is positioned roughly at the center of the area of the serpentine pattern. The peak-to-peak amplitude of the readback signal is digitized in real time as the narrow wandering track crosses the read head. The time axis is converted lo position along the track by using the zero crossing slope of the serpentine trajectory. Successive traces can be averaged to produce a high signal-to-noise microtrack profile; and can also be individually used to monitor the repeatability of the microtrack profile to test for domain stability.

articleTitle: Remanence curves and interaction plots in Tb/Fe magneto-optic multilayer films
abstract: Thin multilayer files offer new opportunities to study fundamental magnetic behavior, as well as being of technological interest, where novel properties not obtainable in bulk materials can be exploited. In this paper we present data on remanence curves, and calculate interaction effects in Tb/Fe multilayer films of constant period (one period is Tb = 14.3Å, Fe = 12.6Å) but with varying numbers of periods and hence different total thicknesses.

articleTitle: Magnetostatic volume wave in multilayered magnetic structure with non-collinear magnetizations
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical investigation of magnetostatic volume wave (MSVW) propagation in multilayered magnetic structure (YIG/GGG/YIG/GGG), in which the static magnetizations in the two YIG layers are not collinear. It is assumed that there exists an arbitrary angle between the two static magnetic magnetizations for a given applied field. Therefore, the effect of the relative orientation between the magnetizations in the different YIG layers on the dispersion and time delay can be explored.

articleTitle: A torsion pendulum magnetometer for determination of the magnetization reversal under various orientation angles
abstract: Using the torsion pendulum method the first-order-anisotropy field H’<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub> and the magnetization of textured permanent magnets can be obtained. In the past, however, this method was restricted to measurements with the texture axis parallel to the applied field. In this paper the determination of the irreversible magnetization reversal in dependance on the angle θ between texture axis and external magnetic field is reported.

articleTitle: Giant magnetoresistance; a primer
abstract: In 1988, Babich et al reported that the application of a magnetic field to multilayer ultrathin films in the (Fe/Cr)n family produced very large changes in the electrical resistance of the film, changes in Δρ/ρ approaching 100% at low temperatures. This is to be contrasted with the Δρ/ρ values on the order of 1% arising from normal bulk magneto-resistance. The Fe films in the multilayer structure had been previously established to be exchange coupled antiferromagnetically through the Cr layer (in itself a very interesting phenomenon); application of sufficient magnetic field overwhelmed the exchange interaction and rendered the magnetization of all Fe layers parallel. The large change of resistance accompanied the change of magnetic structure from successive layers magnetized antiparallel to parallel. This discovery triggered an avalanche of studies on transition metal/non-magnetic metal multilayers, and it was found that giant magnetoresistance was a widely occurring, but not universal, phenomenon. Values of Δρ/ρ as large as 65% at room temperature (in Co/Cu multilayers) have been reported.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional magnons and domain wall dynamics in Ytrium iron garnet
abstract: The problem of a dynamics of domain walls (DWs) and Bloch lines (BLP) is of large interest now due to their promising use in the new type of solid state memory. The microscopic origin of the wall dynamic properties deals with the processes of interaction of different types of elementary and nonlinear excitations. Results of the investigation of the excitation spectrum of the moving wall and its nonlinear dynamics in YIG are presented in this note.

articleTitle: Development of trapezoid shaped Nd-Fe-B die-upset magnets by preform method
abstract: Nd-Fe-8 die-upset magnets possess an inherent advantage in that they may be produced in several shapes with high anisotropy. However, the die-upsetting process needs to be optimized individual shapes. For example, the bulging phenomenon which occurs during hot plastic deformation causes severe problems in the finished magnets. When the mechanically applied tensile stress approaches the maximum tensile stress of the material, cracks generate in the magnets. To circumvent this problem, we have employed a new method called 'the Preform Method'. The total reduction in height during compression exceeded ˜ 72% and the finished magnets were free from cracks. By this method we have fabricated trapezoid die-upset magnets with high energy products of >320 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: The effects of different demagnetisation processes on interactionseffects in thin film media
Magnetic properties of a novel iron carbide film, Fe/sub 7/C/sub 3x/ formed in a glow discharge
abstract: Plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition offers considerable promise for producing unique metal and ceramic structures. Notable features of this deposition technique include low temperature processing, ease of reproducibility, the preparation of unusual phases, the production of either amorphous or oriented crystalline films, and the alteration of film properties by using different process conditions and post production thermal treatment. The iron-carbon-oxygen system has been used to deposit a number of unique films, some of which may have useful magnetic properties. This paper describes magnetic and Mössbauer effect studies of plasma deposited Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, thin films. Thin film coatings of iron carbide deposited on glass microscope cover slips were made by introducing Fe(CO)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>, with H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> carrier gas into a plasma reactor. X-ray diffraction showed the resulting films to be Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. Hysteresis loops and magnetization curves, obtained by using a SQUID magnetometer, gave film coercivities ranging from 280Oe at 300K to 1130Oe at 10K. In contrast, the coercivity of bulk Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> is about 35 Oe.

articleTitle: Observation of floquent higher-order modes in magneto-acoustic interactions
Transistor logic-memory module using high T/sub c/ superconducting core
abstract: The authors have found that oxide high transition temperature superconductor (YBCO and BSCCO: HTcSC for short) disk core shows nonlinear inductance characteristics at 77K due to the flux penetration phenomena. These HTcSC inductors operate at high frequency up to at least 100 MHz because of small energy losses. Utilizing these nonlinear inductance characteristics of HTcSC cores, we have constructed various high frequency magnetic devices. In this paper, a transistor logic memory module based on the Royer oscillator type magnetic multivibrator is presented, in which a HTcSC thin disk core having six coils tightly set around it is connected with two switching transistors.

articleTitle: Correlation between the microstructure and recording properties of CoNi multilayer thin films
abstract: As the recording density is increasing rapidly in magnetic recording devices, media noise is becoming one of the dominant noise sources. Multilayer structured magnetic films have been reported to reduce the media noise by weaking intergranular magnetic coupling. However, the correlation between the magnetic and recording properties and the microstructure of the multilayer films is still not understood very well, which is thought to be crucial for the future design of the multilayer films. In this paper, studies of the magnetic properties, recording performance and microstructure of single (CoNi/Cr/NiP/Al), double (CoNi/Cr/CoNi/Cr/NiP/Al), and triple (CoNi/Cr/CoNi/Cr/CoNi/Cr/NiP/Al) layered thin films are reponed. All the films were deposited on circumferentially textured NiP/Al substrates by dc-magnetron sputtering. Magnetic properties and recording charateristics of the media were measured using vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) and metal-in-gap head, respectively. Plan and cross-section view and local composition of the films were studied using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDXS), respectively.

articleTitle: Intrinsic critical current densities in YBCO superconducting film
New size magnetoelastic effects in thin films
abstract: An excitation of coupled magnetoelastic (ME) waves in thin plates (films) by uniform a.c. field is studied theoretically with taking into account the effects of spontaneous magnetostriction and boundary conditions for surface magnetization and clastic strains. A new type of ME microwave resonance in thin FM and AFM films is predicted. We call this resonance the Joint Ferromagneto-Acoustical Resonance (JFAR) in case of FM or Joint Antiferromagneto-Acoustical Resonance (JAAR) in case of AFM. It occurs when one of the descrete quasi-acoustic eigenfrequencies, with a wave-vector parallel to the normal of the plate, coincides with the frequency of the uniform FMR (AFMR). The possibilities for observing the JFAR (JAAR) are discussed, and the shape of the resonance curve is calculated. An exciting fiture of the ME effects under consideration consists in strong dependence of the shape of resonance curve on the film thickness. The splitting of the resonance curve into two would allow independent determinations of the phonon damping and parameter of ME interaction. Contrary to the usual magneto-acoustic resonances, those considered here rely on the breaking of the translational symmetry, due to the surfaces, and they therefore do not require the wave-vectors of two modes to be equal. The JFAR (JAAR) is the simplest realization of a resonance which does not conserve the total momentum. The observation of predicted ME resonance depends on boundary conditions for spins and elastic displacements and therefore can be powerful instrument for investigation of film surfaces. In spin-wave region, the transmission factor for elastic waves equals zero with neglect of damping, if the sound frequency is close to the one of the descrete quasi-magnon eigenfrequencies. The latter effect has analogy in optics (the total internal reflection) and seems to be promising for applications.

articleTitle: Sm/sub 2/Fe/sub 12/N/sub x/ films with in-plane anisotropy deposited by sputtering
abstract: Permanent-magnet films have attracted much interest in resent years. The nitride and carbide of the Fe-based rare-earth compounds seem very promising for permanent magnets. In this work Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> films were deposited by d.c. magnetron sputtering. They have the Th<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Zn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> type of rhombohedral structure. Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> films with the same structure were made by heating the Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> films in-situ in a low-pressure nitrogen atmosphere. The hysteresis loops for a Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> film and a Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> film are shown in Fig. 1, measured at a temperature of 5 K on a SQUID magnetometer. It was observed that the lattice parameters increase by 2.4% for a and 2.5% for c with nitrogenation. The fractional volume increase is about 7%. Besides the unit cell expansion, the transition from perpendicular to in-plane anisotropy with nitrogenation was observed along with an increase of Curie temperature. The Coercivities with applied filed in the easy directions are 9.7 kOe for Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> and 5.2 kOe for Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> film respectively. The fact that the coercivity for Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> is less than the value for Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> is thought mainly due to the different microstructure. Under an Atomic Force Microscope, the Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> film shows smaller grain size of about 300 nm, while the grain size for the nitride film is about 1 μm, presumably caused by the higher annealing temperature.

articleTitle: Magnetostrictive amorphous sensor for biomedical monitoring
abstract: In biomedical engineering, increased attempts are made to develop sensors for the monitoring of various physiological functions. Besides of being sensitive and reliable, these sensors should be compact and light, thus not disabling the patient (or testee) in a considerable way. These requirements are encouraging the application of amorphous ferromagnetic ribbons with very low thickness. Their effectiveness already has been demonstrated by K. Mohri et al., who applied ribbons of high permeability in connection with a small permanent magnet for the monitoring of heart functions On the other hand, the present paper proposes the use of ribbons of high magnetostriction for the monitoring of articular movements (being relevant, e.g., for sports medicine) and of ventilation, respectively, making use of strain effects.

articleTitle: Macrophage invasiveness and geomagnetism
abstract: We reported previously a modulation by the geomagnetic field of t e invasion of inert, vertical surfaces by oral bacteria growing in vitro. Here, we describe an analogous modulation of the invasion of horizontal surfaces by guinea-pig (gp) cells (macrophages). Macrophages multiply and crawl over inert surfaces.

articleTitle: Spatial mapping of the sensitivity function of magnetic recording heads using a MFM as a local flux applicator
abstract: The response of a magnetic recording head to applied magnetic flux is a function of where the flux is applied. This technologically important "sensitivity function" is usually inferred solely from measurements of the recording process itself. We have developed a technique for applying a localized flux distribution to recording heads using an etched ferromagnetic wire. This wire "flux applicator" can be scanned over the head while the induced signal is monitored. This technique should prove useful in studying such as the asymmetric response of magnetoresistive heads and the sensitivity of both inductive and magnetoresistive heads to off-track magnetization. It can also be used to determine whether a magnetoresistive element returns to it original domain state after being subjected to the stray fields of a neighboring write head.

articleTitle: Asymmetric hysteresis loops in Co-rich ferromagnetic alloys
abstract: We have discovered that after certain annealing treatments, some magnetic materials display a markedly asymmetric hysteresis loop, as shown in Fig. 1. A similar loop was reported without comment by Fujimori et al. in 1981. The asymmetric loop develops easily and readily in materials made of amorphous alloys near the zero magnetostriction composition (Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.94</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.06</sub>)x(S1B)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>, but is not limited to these compositions. The measurements reported here were carried out on ribbons made from Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">70.5</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4.5</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sub>, rapidly solidified and subsequently processed, and measuring about 1.2 mm wide by 20 to 25 pm thick. Most of our samples are 7.5 cm long. To produce the single asymmetric magnetization reversal (AMR) of Fig. 1. a ribbon is treated by annealing for several hours at a temperature of 350 to 400°C, in an applied magnetic field of about 100 mOe directed parallel to the ribbon axis. This field is comparable to the earth's field, which means that to obtain reproducible results the earth's field must be cancelled or measured.

articleTitle: Excitation of propagating dipole-exchange spin waves in ferromagnetic double-film
abstract: The aim of this work is to present a theory of excitation of propagating spin waves (SW) in perpendicularly magnetized double-film structure by microstrip transducer. The theory is based on the dipole-exchange SW spectrum. To solve the boundary problem, we write the equation for the magnetization M (r, t) within each ferromagnetic film (numbers I = 1, 2). The effective field H (r, t), being part of the equation of motion, corresponding to each film, is considered to be equal to the sum of the constant internal magnetic field H, the variable dipole field, the "driving" microwave magnetic field, and exchange field. To find the joint solution of the equations of motion and Maxwell's equations (in magnetostatic limit) we apply earlier elaborated technique: Green's tensor function defining the dipole field and spin wave normal mode expansion technique. As a result we obtain the dispersion equation defining dipole-exchange spin wave spectrum of perpendicularly magnetized double-film structure and the solution for the excited magnetization.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Sm/sub 2/Fe/sub 17/N/sub x/ compounds
abstract: Excellent intrinsic magnetic properties of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> were first reported in an academic paper in 1990 by J.M.D. Coey and H. Sun. We have also proposed these magnetic materials in patents since the discovery of R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> in 1987. We emphasize that the nitrogen content x amounts to 6, in contrast to x <3 reported by other research groups. This report is concerned with the effects of nitrogen content and crystal structure on the magnetic properties of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Nd/sub 2/(Fe,Co,Ni)/sub 14/B single crystals
abstract: It has been revealed that double substitution of Co and Ni atoms for Fe atoms in Nd-Fe-B sintered magnets improves their corrosion resistance while keeping their magnetic properties/l/. The objective of this study is to clarify the magnetic properties of the Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>(Fe, Co, Ni)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sub> B phase.

articleTitle: Mechanisms of the giant magnetoresistance in magnetic multilayers
abstract: The giant magnetoresistance (GMR) or spin valve effect was first observed in the Fe/Cr system. In the Cr thickness ranges where the interlayer exchange coupling is antiferromagnetic (AF), the resistivity drops when an applied field overcomes this coupling and aligns the magnetic moments of all the layers. Similar MR effects have now been found in many multilayered magnetic structures, primarily in multilayers with AF interlayer exchange and also in systems, such as Co/Cu/NiFe or NiFe/Cu/NiFe/FeMn, where the AF arrangement arises from some difference in the coercivity of neighbor magnetic layers. Recently MR effects have also been found with the current perpendicular to the layer and they are even larger in this configuration. Finally, other transport properties are also affected by the flip from antiferromagnetic (AF) to ferromagnetic (F) arrangement. Recently a "giant magnetothermoelectric power, a large field induced change of the thermoelectric power, has been found in Co/Cu, Fe/Cu, Fe/Cr and CoCu/NiFe structures. The GMR is ascribed to spin dependent electron scattering in the magnetic layers (spin dependent scattering, i.e. different scattering rates for the majority and minority electrons, is a wellknown property of the itinerant ferromagnets).

articleTitle: Domain wall velocity measurements by dark field method
abstract: Magnetooptical methods made it possible to reach substantial progress in investigations of dynamics of ferromagnetics. Among these methods important role play methods based on high speed phothography techniques, using which for the first time were observed quasirelativistic motion of the domain wall (DW). Mononedimensionalities of the DW, soliton like behavior of vertical Bloch lines. But high speed photography methods have also a number of limitations. It is difficult to use them in infrared region - in the region of the best transparency of garnets and orthoferrites. They also carry few information about the structure of the DW since the observed width of the DW reflects the resolution of the optical system and by order of magnitude exceeds the real width of the DW. On the other hand, in investigations of Bloch lines dynamics dark field methods demonstrated their wide capabilities. Taking these factors into account the new modification of Sixtus-Tonx method, combined with the dark field techniques, has some advantages and can be considered as supplementary to high speed photography methods.

articleTitle: Magnetic stability of Fe9.0wt%Si/permalloy multilayered films in high temperature processes
abstract: High saturation magnetization films are required to possess stability against high process temperature. For Fe alloys, it is Difficult to obtain high initial permeability, μ, and high Ms simultaneously because of its large magnetocrystalline anisotropy and magnetostriction. Takashi and Shimatsu reported on the origin of the high μ. They made it clear that reduced grain size and moderate lattice strain are necessary to obtain a high permeability. In this method, however, it is difficult to have high μ against high temperature processes. We reported on the magnetic properties of Fe alloy/permalloy multilayered films. It was clarified that polycrystalline orientation plays an important role in getting a high initial permeability value. However, the μ decreases by over 400<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C annealing processes because of diffusion at the boundaries.

articleTitle: Angular dependent recording behaviour of ME tapes
Magnetic properties of Sr-Zn system w-type hexagonal ferrite magnets prepareed by new manufacturing method
abstract: The preparing method of W-type hexagonal ferrite magnets was very complicate it seems to impractical for industrial production at present. The magnetism of Sr-Zn-Co system W-type hexagonal single crystal ferrite has reported by Graetsch et al, but there is little about the magnetic properties of sintered Sr system W-type hexagonal ferrite magnets. This experiment was carried out to suggest a new manufacturing method for stabilizing W-type crystal structure and to investigate the preparation conditions about Sr-Zn W-type hexagonal ferrite magnets, and the physical properties of those magnets were examined.

articleTitle: Theory of low-field loss in partially magnetized ferrites
Suppression of intra- and intergranular properties by transport current in Bi-based ceramic superconductors
abstract: The behaviour of granular superconductors in wide and magnetic field ranges has been experimentally studied and described theoretically. The situation is complicated when the specimen, in the presence of an external field, carries dc-transport current. This problem has two aspects: the induced resistance to the direct transport current by ac magnetic field, and the influence of dc-transport current on the ac susceptibility. In this paper the in-phase and quadrature signals of diamagnetic response of a slab carrying dc-transport current I in a direction normal to the magnetic field H have been studied. A strong suppression of intra- and intergranular properties by transport current observed. The Single- phase Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Ca<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>, ceramic sample had the dimensions 8 ⋅ 8 ⋅ 0.8 mm. The susceptibility was measured using inductive technique at 2.45 kHz. The resistance of the contacts used in this study was less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> Ohm. In the sample carrying the transport current no temperature gradients were detected.

articleTitle: Improved quality factor of thin film inductor by application of multilayer film
abstract: Recently, thin film inductors are reported by many authors (1-3). These thin film micro inductors are investigated in the point of design of exciting coil and magnetic core. The most difference of electric properties between the thin film inductor and chip inductor is that quality factor (Q) of thin film inductor is lower than that of chip inductor using ferrite magnetic core in same inductance (L). To get the high quality factor, it is important to use the magnetic core in which iron loss is small in high frequency. On the other hand, it is well known that in multilayer magnetic films, generally, the permeability is high and iron loss is small. In this paper, it is proposed that the multilayer magnetic core is useful to increase Q in thin film inductor. The experimental inductor shows L of 100nH, Q=18 at 50 MHz in its size of 0.5x2mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Hysteretic magnetic forces calculation for type II superconductors
abstract: In superconducting accelerometer and magnetic beating applications, the precise control of these devices requires the precise understanding of the interactions between superconductor and the applied magnetic field. We will report the complete hysteretic levitation forces calculation for type II superconductors by using the Bean's model. To our knowledge, this is the first time which show the complete hysteretic forces calculation. We will show that the precise prediction of the behaviors of type II superconductors in an magnetic field can be made with reasonable accuracy. Stiffness of a magnetic spring system can also be obtained using the current method.

articleTitle: MÖssbauer study on the distribution of iron in high coercivity chromium dioxide particles
abstract: High coercivity Chromium Dioxide particles have been made available by a modified hydrothermal process. In a recent paper we have suggested, on the basis of magnetic measurements that the enhanced coercivities are due to a higher level of iron doping in the CrO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> lattice which can be reached with the new process. It has not been possible to determine the exact amount of iron atoms incorporated into the crystal because in all particles a secondary phase is present in small concentrations which also includes some of the iron doping. If the concentration ratio between the two iron species were known for different doping levels there might be a possibility to extrapolate the solubility limit of iron in CrO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> more precisely and also to estimate the highest coercivities which can be reached with the new process. Therefore, MÖssbauer spectroscopy has been applied as an experimental technique which is capable to quantitatively analyse the amount of iron in different crystallographic environments even if very small crystal sizes are present.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of permanent-magnet properties of zinc-bonded Sm/sub 2/Fe/sub 17/N/sub z/
abstract: Zinc-bonded permanent magnets based on Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> (x ≲ 3) have been prepared by crushing and milling a Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>17 ingot, nitrogenation, pressing with Zn powder (5 - 15 vol %) in a magnetic field, and a subsequent heat treatment, as described elsewhere. Microprobe analysis showed that after the optimum heat treatment almost all zinc is consumed. The texture degree was adjusted varying the magnetic field during the compacting process, resulting in a ratio of remanence perpendicular and parallel to the texture axis B⊥/B║= 1 - 0.3. At room temperature these magnets exhibit a coercivity μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oJ</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 0.5 - 1.9 T and a remanence B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 0.5 - 0.8 T, where <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">J</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> is very sensitive to particle size (after milling), N content, Zn content, annealing temperature and annealing time.

articleTitle: A self consistent generalized model for the calculation of minor loop excursions in the theory of hysteresis
abstract: In previous work it has been shown how to calculate the magnetization curve from a simple theory which invokes a constant energy loss per unit change in magnetization in a ferromagnet. The energy loss, which is therefore proportional to the change in magnetization, leads to hysteresis loops which are obtained from first principles. In this paper it will be shown how the model has teen generalized to provide completely self consistent minor hysteresis loop excursions. By minor loop we mean any excursion for which either the range of magnetizations ΔM or the range of magnetic fields ΔH is not symmetric about zero. The resulting model solutions show that both crossing and partially coincident minor loops emerge naturally from the theory. This is known to occur in experimental observations and has been noted by Mayergoyz. The generalization of the theory of hysteresis to cover the minor loop excursions has resulted from the use of an effective volume fraction of active domains determined from the location of reversal points on the M.H plane. Such a concept is well known in the use of Preisach models for describing hysteresis.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of geothite in radulae of limpets
abstract: Acicular goethite ∝-FeOOH) is the well-known starting material of acicular γ-Fe203 in industrial processes. Interestingly, acicular goethite is also grown in radulae of limpets (Mollusca: Gastropoda) via a matrix mediated process. Around the acicular goethite is silica in mature teeth. The structure and magnetic properties of limpet radulae are discussed here.

articleTitle: Structural studies of rare earth-iron nitrides by neutron powder diffraction
abstract: New high performance permanent magnets have been found as the result of nitrogenation of rare-earth-iron-based phases, including RE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> and REFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12-x</sub>TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> where TM is a transition-metal such as Mo, V, Al, Ti. We have used neutron diffraction to study the changes which accompany the nitrogenation in a number of these compounds, including Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>, Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>, NdFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>Mo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and NdFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>V2. In the RE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> systems, the nitrogen atoms are found to occupy the largest interstitial site, the h site in Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> and the equivalent e site in Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>. There are indications of a second interstitial site with a low nitrogen occupancy. The primary sites are found to be less than fully populated, perhaps due to steric constraints, since the Fe-N bonds are relatively short. In Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x'</sub> there are clear indications of variable nitrogen filling. In the RETM<>12 systems, the nitrogen is found only in the large interstitial site at 0 0 ½, and depending on preparation, this site may approach full occupancy. The cell volume is found to vary with the nitrogen filling, and intermediate nitrogen occupancies are observed. The change in interatomic distances has been examined across these compounds. We find that the Curie point follows a nearly linear relationship with the average Fe-Fe bond length for the Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub> compounds investigated including Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sub>B. A relationship between anisotropy direction and average Nd-Fe bond length is also noted.

articleTitle: Permeability of ferromagnet in light field
abstract: The effective magnetic fields may be appeared in the transparent ferromagnet as a result of nonlinear interaction of the electrical component of the intensity light wave with the magnetic subsystem. Influence of these fields, because of thier weakness, will be considerable near by instability points, where sucseptebility is anamal large. Magnetic phase transitions under the action of the light field were studied earlier. In this paper the permeability and spectrum of the spin waves in presence of the light field are investigated.

articleTitle: Deviation on induction dependence in the statistical model power losses: the case of 3.2% SiFe N/sub x/O/sub x/ electrical steels
abstract: This work was intended to clarify the exact induction dependence of hysteresis losses P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">hys</sub> and the internal coercive field V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> - which characterize the excess loss behavior - of 3.2 wt% N.O. SiFe electric steel evaluated by the statistical loss representation. It was also investigated in which sense and measure are these dependencies perturbed by the texture of the material at a given size distribution of grains. Careful loss measurements were performed between 10 and 100 Hz in the 0.3T-1.6T induction range on Epstein samples cut both parallel and perpendicular from 0.5 mm thick sheet. For both samples lose separation procedure were performed on 22 level of the induction evaluating the P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">hys</sub> and the V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> field values as fitting parameters of the excess loss data in the n (M.0.) magnetic objects vs. H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">exc</sub> excess field representation.

articleTitle: Oriented barium haxaferrite thin films prepared by pulsed laser deposition
abstract: Oriented thin films of barium hexaferrite, BaFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19<sub>, were grown in situ on (0001) sapphire substrates utilizing a pulsed laser deposition technique for the first time. X-Ray diffraction (XRD), elastic backscattering (EBS), ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) and vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM) confirm the structure, composition and magnetic parameters are consistent with films prepared by other techniques such as liquid phase epitaxy (LPE).</sub></sub>

articleTitle: Nd(Fe,Mo)/sub 12/Nx compounds and magnets
abstract: The nitrogen induced hard magnetic material is getting interest for the potential application of permanent magnet. A lot of efforts are carrying out to make the magnets for the Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>Nx<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> and NdFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> TiNx<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> compounds. The NdFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> TiNx has a large saturation magnetization and Curie temperature comparable with the Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>Nx compound, though the anisotropy field is lower than that of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>2Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>Nx. However, the NdFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> TiNx has an advantage, because the cost of Nd is lower than Sm. In this study, the magnet fabrication art tried for the Nd(Fe,M)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>Nx compounds by the mechanical alloying method. The ThMn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> crystal structure can be formed for the Nd(Fe,M)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>Nx (M=Ti, V, Mo and W) compounds, and the magnetic properties of these compounds are not investigating yet except for the M=Ti case. The purpose of this study is clarify which elements are suitable for the magnet fabrication of Nd(Fe,M)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>Nx within Ti, V, Mo and W.

articleTitle: Polyphosphate surface treatment of γFe2O3 for enhanced coercive force
abstract: The coercive force of partially reduced, acicular γFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> particles has been reported to substantially increase following surface treatment with sodium polyphosphate. This phenomenon is of interest because the polyphosphate/ γFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> system may provide a model for understanding the origins of surface anisotropy in iron oxide particles and films. Extensions of our previous studies on large acicular particles (˜6000Å length, length-to-width ratio ˜6) to particles having dimensions more representative of those found in particulate recording media (˜2000Å, aspect ratio ˜8) are discussed in this digest.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of the magnetization of ultrafine particles of nickel
abstract: The temperature dependence of the magnetization of bulk iron and bulk Nickel at lower temperature can be explained by the ideas of spin wave theory and stoner excitment theory. Because of its size effect and surface effect of ultrafine particle (UFP), the magnetic properties of CFP were usually considered to be different from bulk’s. The spontaneous magnetization of Ni fine particles with the average diameter of 35A has a temperature dependence closely following that of bulk material; the temperature dependence of the spontaneous magnetization of fine iron particles with the average diameter of 19A obeys T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2</sup> -law at temperature above 150K, but the spin-wave constant R of the Fe particles are larger than that of the bulk. In this paper, we present the temperature dependence of magnetization of Ni UFP with the average diameter between 100A and 300A.

articleTitle: Displacement eddy currents in magnetic laminates
Transverse correlation length in thin film media
abstract: Reducing the bit length and track width to increase storage density in magnetic recording is limited by media noise associated with the size or granularity of the micromagnetic features of the recording medium. For a given medium, the scale of the micromagnetic features can be characterized by a correlation length. We have proposed a pseudo-microtrack concept to interpret experiments that measure the transverse correlation of media noise in dc saturated thin film media. We now extend our experiments to the study of transverse correlation of transition-written thin film media. The results of our experiments and a simple statistical analysis are interpreted in terms of a transverse correlation length for several media that differ in their noise characteristics.

articleTitle: Ionic exchange effects and magnetic properties of nanocrystalline BaFe/sub 12/O/sub 19/ ferite dispersions
abstract: Magnetic oxide powders suspended in a liquid spontaneously agglomerate unless they are suitably deflocculated by creating mutually repelling charged double layers or by physically preventing the close approach of particles due to the steric hindrance of absorbed molecules. For hexagonal barium ferrite powder the problem of particles separation is extremely difficult. In processing of materials for magnetic recording, several different additives must be incorporated in the final product to establish the behavior and properties required for the coating. These additives may be categorized conveniently as follows: 1) liquid / solvent medium, 2) surfactant (wetting agent), 3) deflocculant and 4) binder / plasticizer and/or pigment. Although most of these substances are added in a relatively small amount and some may be eliminated or do not appear in the final product, from a manufacturing perspective they are essential. The selection and control of these substances are often the key to successful processing or the development of an improved process. The proper selection is based on chemical characteristics and functions of the additive and empirical experience. For all possible applications of Ba-ferrite particles in magnetic recording, the formation of particle stacks must be prevented. Up to now some experiments that attempt to control agglomeration and surfactant screening for -0.1 μm particles in organic solvents have been reported. A variety of ionic and nonionic surfactants were checked for their ability to provide wetting and particle separation. However, all surfactants used, while offering good particle wetting, failed to deliver relatively stable suspension.

articleTitle: The effects of Ni/sub 3/P sublayer on the properties if CoNiCr/Cr media using different substrates
abstract: Cr and magnetic films have been shown to grow differently on nonmetallic substrates. Consequently, sputtered glass and canasite(glass-ceramic) disks suffer lower Hc, lower HF amplitude and greater bit shift than conventional textured NiP/AI disks. A new process using a sputtered Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> sublayer beneath the Cr-underlayer has been developed. Previously, CoPt-based media with a sputtered Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>P underlayer were reported to exhibit coercivity enhancement and noise reduction. In the present work, a sputtered Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>P sublayer was applied to a system of Co-30%Ni-7.5%Cr medium with a Cr underlayer. The effect of the Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>P sublayer on the magnetic and recording properties of the disk was found to depend on the substrate used.

articleTitle: The effect of cluster size on media noise in Co-Ni-P thin films
abstract: The microstructure of thin-film media is known to have a major effect on media noise, and control of the microstructure is the goal of much process development to produce such media. Grain size is an important characteristic of the microstructure, but the manner in which individual grains interact is even more important. Decreased coupling of adjacent grains leads to more regular domain structure of the recorded transition, the position of the transition is less affected by this magnetic microstructure, and the media noise attributable to variation in position of the transition is thereby reduced.

articleTitle: Improvement of measuring method of DC magnetization curve using ring specimen
abstract: When the dc magnetization (B-H) curve is measured using a ring specimen, the magnetic field strength corresponding to the average flux density should be calculated using the mean magnetic path length L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub>. However, the mean geometric path length L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> is used instead of L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub>, because L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> is unknown. Therefore, the B-H curve obtained has an error, and it is affected by the ratio γ of the outside to inside radii of the specimen. In this paper, a new measuring method of the accurate B-H curve using a ring specimen is proposed. The effectiveness of the method is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Improvement of servo robustness for digital sector servo system
Computerized DC bridge of thermistor measurement or localised power loss in magnetic materials
abstract: It has been reported that a dc bridge circuit with a thermistor as a temperature sensor can be used to measure localised power loss (LPL) by observing the rate of rise of temperature in magnetic cores. In recent years advances in precision electronic components have made simpler circuits feasible for accurate temperature measurement applications. The presented study describes a new design of a thermistor circuit with a dc bridge where simplicity, repeatability, reproducibility and accuracy were the main features. The bridge auxiliary circuit consisted of; two instrumentation amplifiers, a AD524 chip was used with preset gains of x1, x10, x100 and x1000, and two fourth-order Butterworth low pass filters which display a cut-off frequency less than 0.5Hz as shown in Fig. 1.

articleTitle: Power efficiency of eddy current shielding of structural steel in transverse magnetic field
abstract: In industrial plants structural elements, which are magnetic and are reasonably good conductors, are often exposed to the magnetic field produced by the nearby cables carrying large currents. The resulting power loss, especially in large plants, may be substantial. It is often essential to reduce the power loss by shielding the structure from the magnetic field. One possible method of shielding is eddy current shielding in which the element to be shielded is enclosed in a squirrel cage of a good conducting material such as copper. In such a case, it is the total power loss that should be compared with the power loss in the element without the shield. Because of restrictions such as accessibility, then is limitation on how close the shield can be placed to the element to be shielded. In this paper we discuss the effect of the closeness of the shield i.e., the radius of the shield, on the aggregate power loss. A configuration, where a cable is running parallel to element thus producing a transverse magnetic field, is considered. A two dimensional geometry is used for illustration.

articleTitle: Modeling of multilayer thin film recording media
Indcutive absolute angular position sensor
abstract: The need for angular position sensors is not to be proved: it is general in industry. But for some applications, like tools machines, they have to be very precise, whatever the mechanical plays are. We propose a structure insensitive to every kind of play: radial, axial and precession play. The rotor has no windings and is ferromagnetic. The stator is non magnetic, except for a U shaped ferromagnetic core supporting a coil and straddling the rotor (fig 1). The reluctance of the magnetic circuit varies through the rotation of the rotor, depending on the shape of the rotor. The inductance of the coil also varies. The shape of the rotor depends on the way we want to make the measurement and on the form of signal we want to have.

articleTitle: Control of interlayer magnetic coupling and magnetoresistance in magnetic multilayers by insertion of very thin magnetic layers
abstract: Currently multilayer systems such as Fe/Cr, Co/Cu and Co/Cu/NiFe/Cu have attracted much interest because of their large magnetoresistance (MR) effect. In Fe/Cr and Co/Cu systems, large MR effect is attributed to the antiparallel alignments of the magnetic moments in adjacent magnetic layers which arise from the interlayer antiferromagnetic coupling between magnetic layers acoss Cr or Cu. In Co/Cu/ NiFe/Cu system including two magnetic components, the antiparallel alignments of the moments are realized in the magnetization process because of the difference of the anisotropy of Co and NiFe layers. In this system large MR effect is induced by relatively small magnetic field (-50Oe) which is needed to switch the magnetization of NiFe layer. However, interlayer magnetic coupling exists even in this system, and this coupling prevents the independent magnetization switching of two magnetic components especially for the Cu layer thickness smaller than -50A. Therefore, it is important to control interlayer magnetic coupling to obtain large MR change. The interlayer magnetic coupling strongly depends on the kinds of magnetic layer and non-magnetic spacer layer. In this paper we have examined the possibility of the control of interlayer magnetic coupling by insertion of very thin different magnetic layer into spacer and magnetic layer interface.

articleTitle: Read/write characeristics for laminated high moment Fe-Ta-N film heads for HDTV VTR
abstract: Fe-Ta-N films have high saturation magnetization 4πMs (14-17kG), high permeability (>3000 at 10MHz), high Vickers hardness (>900) and are expected to be high density magnetic recording head core materials for high coercivity media, such as metal tapes. Yet, few reports have been published on Fe-Ta-N alloy video head application in contact with the tapes at high relative velocity. The authors have developed laminated film video heads using the Fe-Ta-N films. This paper reports the read-write and wear characteristics for the heads.

articleTitle: Phases of NdFe/sub 10.7-x/Ti/sub 1.3/ alloys and magnetic properties of their nitrides
abstract: Recently, Yang et al reported that nitrification of NdFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>Ti compounds with ThMn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> type structure increases considerably its magnetization, magnetocrystalline anisotropy and Curie temperature. In this work, we report the phases existed in the NdFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10.7-X</sub> Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.3/sub> alloys which have nearly single phase of ThMn<sub>12</sub>-type structure and the effects of nitrification treatments on the magnetic properties of them.</sub>

articleTitle: Light-weight type linear induction motor(LIM) and its characteristics
abstract: At present, study is being made to improve the thrust characteristics of LIM. The thrust per unit weight of motor can be improved either by increasing the thrust of the motor itself or by reducing the weight of the motor. Recentry, we have manufactured a light-weight type LIM on an experimental basis. This paper is intended to report the outline of the light-weight type LIM.

articleTitle: Acicular γ-Fe2O3 particulate surface-coated with barium ferrite
abstract: In the past few years, barium ferrite (BF) particulates have undergone Intensive development in magnetic recording applications due to their high coercivity of up to 5000 Oe and the unique perpendicular recording characteristics. In general, BF particulates are hexagonal platelets. Recently, acicular BF particulates with coercivity of about 2000 Oe were made possible by reacting acicular a-FeOOH with coated BaCO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. In this presentation, novel acicular γ-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> particulates surface-coated will be disclosed. These particulates have coercivity of up to 2700 Oe and saturation magnetization of greater than 60 emu/g, and much improved thermal stability.

articleTitle: The study of recessed MR sensors with un-laminated and multi-laminated flux-guides
Magnetic viscosity in the magnetic fine powders
abstract: Givord et al. found that the activation volume is proportional to the cube of the domain wall width for Sr-ferrite. Carmona et al. suggested that the viscosity mechanism in Ba-ferrite is the strong pinning of domain walls. In this paper, we investigate the temperature dependence and size dependence of the magnetic viscosity of Ba-ferrite and γ-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> fine powders in order to reveal the coersivity mechanism in these materials.

articleTitle: Coercivity mechanism and microstructure of Co/Pt multilayers
abstract: Despite of voluminous work on magnetic properties of Co/Pt multilayers, very little understanding has been achieved as to the coercivity mechanism in connection with the microstructure. This is a critical issue for optical storage applications, since the coercivity affects domain stability which in turn influences recording performance. (Co/Pt) multilayers were fabricated by sputtering in Ar pressure of 2 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> Torr onto various substrate conditions (Fig. 1). Measurements of magnetic properties were carried out by VSM, AGFM and Torque magnetometer. Structural analysis was made by X-ray, XPS and high resolution electron microscopy.

articleTitle: Magneto-optical measurement of interactions in thin-film media
abstract: There is much utility in finding simple magnetic characterization methods that can be used to predict media noise without having to resort to actual recording measurements one easily measured parameter, the coercive squareness. S*, has been snown to correlate with noise, but this correlation may not hold when s* is low due to orientation effects. There has been much recent activity in using δM measurements to characterize interactions and thus noise in various types of media<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,3</sup>, but this measurement, typically done with VSM on coupons cut from disks, is both time-consuming and destructive. We report here for the first time a magneto-optical technique which allows for spatial, non-destructive δM measurements on full disks, and compare it to VSM results.

articleTitle: New procedures for in Situ measurement of the magnetic properties of materials: applications of the magnescope
abstract: The measurement of magnetic properties of materials in situ has received link attention in the past but is now becoming an important issue, particularly in the area of nondestructive evaluation or materials assessment. In merit work we have developed a new instrument known as the Magnescope and here we discuss some of the procedures which have been incorporated in the control and data analysis software in order to give a wide range of magnetic properties calculated from a few simple measurements. These procedures have been used to identify specific magnetic parameters from the hysteresis loop which are affected by applied stress, residual stress, fatigue damage and grain boundary segregation. It has been found that the magnetic properties as measured by the Magnescope are sensitive to all of these effects, and that Magnescope inspections can therefore be used to assess material condition.

articleTitle: Dynamic domain wall observation in amorphous materials subjected to bending stress
abstract: The dynamic Kerr magneto-optic effect is a powerful tool for surface domain observation on various types of magnetic materials. It is essential to make dynamic magnetic domain observations during an a.c. magnetisation cycle in order to understand the magnetisation process. This has been done using different techniques, most commonly by stroboscopic means, ie. by capturing data over a number of cycles of magnetisation. It has been verified that, this technique is feasable as the domain motion in repeatable up to a flux density level of 0.8T in the case of Metglas 2605SC. The dynamic domain motion was observed using a stroboscopic Kerr bench system which also incorporates a mechanism to apply external bending stress. The sample preparation was performed in the following manner; both surfaces of the samples were polished, annealed at 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C for 2 hours under vacuum and then bloomed. The domain studies were carried out when the sample was energized with induction magnitude up to 0.8T within the frequency range 50Hz to 150Hz.

articleTitle: An accurate measuring system for VTR magnetic track
abstract: A new design has been presented and the corresponding measuring system has been built, which is used to calibrate the servomechanism of a video tape recorder (VTR), to test the assembling errors of the video head drum assemblies of a VTR and to determine exchangeability of a VTR. This design is based upon the principle of the method of Bitter pattern, the digital image processing technology and the precise electromagnetic micromotion device (PEW). The accuracy of the former system lies on the location accuracy of the specimen stage of a measuring microscope and that is about 0.5-1 um. And in our system the measuring precision depends on the amplification of system and the resolution of the digital image processing interface, so it is possible to improve the measuring accuracy of the system to deep submicrometer. As a result, the distance measuring precision of our measuring system has attained to 0.2 um.

articleTitle: The magnetic domain structure of monocrystalline Co/sub 2/Y
abstract: Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Y (Ba<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sub>) is a magnetic oxide with hexagonal structure and a pronounced easy plane (basal plane) of anisotropy. The anisotropy field required to rotate the magnetization into the c-axis is 28 kOe: by comparison the anisotropy field within the c-plane is only 155 Oe. Very little prior work has been reported concerning the domain structure of single crystal planar ferrites and as far as we know nothing at all on Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Y. Flux grown platelets of Cozy easily cleave on the basal plane and so provide ready specimens for microscope examination. Other platelets were lapped with diamond paste such that the polished surface contained the c-axis. The domain patterns were studied with the Bitter technique.

articleTitle: Anomalous thermal expansion of Sm/sub 2/Fe/sub 15/Si/sub 2/
abstract: The low Curie temperature of R<>2Fe<>17 compounds is usually attributed to the small Fe-Fe nearest-neighbour distance at the dumbbell site and the concomitant antiferromagnetic exchange interaction between corresponding Fe atoms in the structure. The negative exchange interaction also leads to an anomalous thermal expansion in these compounds. The substitution of Si for Fe results in an increase in T<>c although unit cell volume decreases. The T<>c increase could be attributed to a preferential substitution of Si atoms into the dumbbell Fe sites. But Mossbauer studies on Nd-, Er-, and Tm-compounds and neutron diffraction on Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> indicate no preferential substitution of Si among the four crystallographically different Fe Sites. We investigated the magnetic properties of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17-x</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> and measured the anomalous thermal expansion of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> by high temperature x-ray diffraction.

articleTitle: Magnetization cross track correlations and transition noise of longitudinal thin film media
Preparation and some properties of sputtered Co/U-As multilayers
abstract: We previously reported the "giant" magneto-optic and magneto-transport properties of amorphous U-pnictide (Bi, Sb, As) films at low temperatures prepared by magnetron sputtering. Polar Kerr rotations as large as -3.5°, anisotropic magnetoresistance of 26%, and Hall angles as large as 17° were measured. However, the maximum Curie temperature (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>) is only 130-140K which is too low for practical device applications.
