Alloy additions of up to 20 at% of Co, Mn, Cu, or Ti did not raise T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>. Another possible method to increase T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> is by coupling a strong magnetic material directly to U-As through a multilayer structure. In this paper we describe the preparation and structural characteristic of Co/U-As multilayers. A Comparison of the magnetooptical properties of a multilayer film and alloy film of similar overall composition are presented.

articleTitle: Dependence of magnetic properties of Fe/Al multilayers on layer thickness and annealing temperature
abstract: It is well known that the magnetic and electrical properties of Fe film is strongly dependent on their crystal structure and the grain size. Fe/AI multilayered films deposited by ion beam sputtering have exhibited soft magnetic properties. In this study, the relationship between the Crystallographic and magnetic characteristics and the thickness of Fe and AI layers and post annealing temperature has been investigate for the multilayers deposited by using Ar and Kr as sputtering gas. Ar and Kr pressures in the ion source a t a 0.1 and 0.05 mTorr, respectively. The planar targets of Fe and AI with purity above 99.99% were sputtered by the ions extracted at acceleration voltage of 500V from the source. The layer thicknesses of Fe and AI layers 1<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</sub> and 1<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Al</sub> were in the range of 20 - 120 and 3 - 50 Å, respectively. Post annealing process were performed at the temperature of 150 and 300<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C in a evacuated chamber during 1 hour. Crystallographic and magnetic characteristics were analysed by X-ray diffractometry and determined by VSM, respectively. The relative permeability μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> were evaluated by shunt core method at frequency of 4 MHz.

articleTitle: The effect of V or W additives to microstructure and coercivity of Nd-Fe-B based magnets
abstract: Insufficient temperature stability and corrosion resistance are factors limiting further applications of sintered Nd-Fe-B magnets. It is known that partial replacement of Fe by Co reduces the corrosion sensitivity but decreases the coercivity force. Recently different groups reported on the influence of V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, Mo<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> on the microstructure and magnetic properties of Nd-(Dy)-Fe-Co-B magnets and showed that the addition of small amounts of refractory elements like V or MO lead to magnets with improved corrosion resistance and high coercivity force even at elevated temperatures.

articleTitle: Rare-earth transition metal carbides
abstract: The intrinsic magnetic properties of rare-earth transition-metal compounds have been found to improve dramatically with nitrogen and carbon additions which are made through the gas-phase interstitial modification proceess. In this work, we have obtained rare-earth transition metal carbides with the 2:17 and 1:12 structures using methane and ethane. They intrinsic magnetic properties of these compounds have been studied and the results will be reported.

articleTitle: Metallic glasses as acoustic transducers
abstract: We have previously reported results on the piezomagnetic properties of scrolls of METGLAS 2605SC. There we reported an optimum effective magnetomechanical coupling coefficient. k-ƒ ƒ of 0.75 in air. In this paper, we report the extension of the study to include measurements in water. As before we have chosen a consolidated scroll geometry, and the performance has been analysed using ultrasonic complex plane analysis. A maximum k-ƒ ƒ of 0.68 was achieved with Q=4.5. We believe this to be the first report of a metallic glass acoustic transducer in a practical device configuration.

articleTitle: /sup 67/Fe Mossbauer investigation of R/sub 2/(Fe/sub 1-x/Co/sub x/)/sub 17/N/sub y/ (R=rare earth, X /spl le/ 0.4 and y /spl le/ 2.2)
abstract: Binary rare earth-transition metal compounds are numerous but the R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>17 compound type is the moat iron-rich. It crystallises in the rhombohedral Th<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Zn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> structure for R lighter than Gd and in the hexagonal Th<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> structure for heavier R. Despite the low of the values of the Curie temperature (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>) - maximum of about 470 K for R=Gd, the 2:17 compound exhibit very interesting magnetic properties. Recently a new series with nitrogen R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub> (y=2+6) has been prepared and studied by J.M.D. Coey et al. They showed that nitrogen strongly increases T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and room temperature magnetization, resulting a large increase of the Fe-Fe exchange interaction due mainly to the lattice expansion.

articleTitle: Influence of the control signal input in pinhole device
abstract: Miniaturization of magnetic devices is very important in miniaturizing electronic devices. We have studied various types of micro-thin film inductors and transformers. These inductors and transformers are now being prepared by thin film techniques. Miniaturization and integration of magnetic devices make high frequency operation possible. We have proposed a new type of thin film transformer made using a strip line and an amorphous CoNbZr film and it was called a "pinhole device". The output voltage of thin film transformer could be controlled either the center hole current, an external magnetic field. In this paper, the change of the output voltage when the control signal was applied to the center hole will be described.

articleTitle: Barium ferrite particulate tapes for high band 8MM VCR
abstract: Barium ferrite particulate media are of much interest for their advantage of high density recording characteristics, chemical stability and volume productivity. The barium ferrite recording media already have applications such as large capacity floppy disks and DAT duplication tapes. Further applications for the barium ferrite media to various high density magnetic recording systems are expected. In this study, we have applied the barium ferrite recording media to a high bad 8mm VCR which has the highest recording density among practical use VCRs. Coercivity adjustment to relatively loner value to increase chrominance recording level and longitudinal barium ferrite particle orientation have made the high band 8mm VCR recording characteristics fully compatible with high band 8m particulate metal tapes, despite the fact that the magnetic characteristics are quite different.

articleTitle: Antiferromagnetic exchange coupled and soft adjacent layer biasings for an MR head by triode sputter deposited films
abstract: This paper will investigate the effect of grain size on NiFe/FeMn exchange coupled films. This will be done through deposition methods (diode vs triode deposited films) and thermal treatment of films. Longitudinal biasing at the ends of a magnetoresistive (MR) element is required for Barkhausen noise free response. One approach is to pattern the ends of the ferromagnetic NiFe MR element with FeMn antiferromagnetic film. NiFe/FeMn antiferromagnetic exchange coupled films have been studied by Howard et el using a diode sputtering system. Here we investigate such properties on triode deposited films. Plasma is confined only in the target area away from the substrate in the triode system. Therefore, this is a cooler sputtering process as compared to the diode sputtering system. In the diode sputtering system electron bombardment beats up the surface of the substrate. This will affect siren and grain size in the film. Thus a triode deposited film is expected to exhibit different properties from that of the coventionally diode deposited film. Figure 1a shows exchange shift and hysteresis loop of a 200 Å NiFe film etched back to 150Å NiFe/100Å FeMn/50Å Ta triode deposited sheet films. Figure 1b is the loop on corresponding diode sputtered films. They have different exchange shifts and coercivities. Figures 2a and 2b are the TEM micrographs of films deposited in triode and diode sputtering systems respectively, showing their grain sizes. Variation in properties of these films will be associated with the grain size in this paper. Experimental results and physical arguments will be presented to show improvement in ordering temperature due to increased grain size in the antiferromagnetic film either through deposition method or through thermal treatment. Barkhausen noise was studied on triode sputtered films of antiferromagnetic exchange coupled (AEC) MR element in combination with soft adjacent layer (SAL) transverse biasing.

articleTitle: Origin of magnetoresistance in Co/Cu multilayers
abstract: The discovery by Parkin et al of a "giant" magnetoresistance (MR) in multilayer Co/Cu films has resulted in many studies of this effect. We report on several features of multilayer MR which may help interpretation. Our films are on glass substrates with the structure Cu(50Å)/[Co(10Å)/Cu(t)]32/Cu(50Å) where the Cu thickness t varies from t = 0 to 21Å with 32 layers of each element. The layers are deposited by magnetron sputtering in a 3 mTorr Ar atmosphere using computer control. The substrates, at ambient temperature, are moved sequentially over each gun to deposit the Co or Cu layer. Film resistivities (ρ) are all measured by the van der Pauw method (Fig. 1) except for the t = 9Å film which is also measured (Fig. 2) on a narrow bar specimen. Figure 1 shows ρ at 77K for H = 0 field and H = 18 kOe where Δρ is obtained from the separation of the two curves. Figure 2 shows both the 77K resistivity and magnetization (4 πM) as a function of H comparing the films t = 9Å and t = 21Å.

articleTitle: Exchange anisotropy in a phase-decomposed Fe-12% Mn alloy
abstract: Magnetic hysteresis curves (major loops) shifted from their symmetrical positions about the origin are observed in a limited number of materials having exchange anisotropy, such as Co/CoO, Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Mn, and Cu-Mn. Such shifted loops are usually obtained only at cryogenic temperatures (except for some thin films), and after cooling in the presence of high magnetic field. As the exchange anisotropy is primarily an interface phenomenon, it is essential to create as many interfaces as possible (between the two phases, e.g., ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic) to enhance the effect in bulk materials. We have successfully created a bulk, "room-temperature" exchange anisotropy material from an Fe-12% Mn alloy by suitable microstructural control as shown schematically in Fig. 1. The alloy was phase-decomposed into submicron two-phase structure, severely wire drawn to elongate the interfaces parallel to the field direction, and heat treated. The complicated step of field cooling heat treatment was eliminated, and instead, a simple magnetization of the sample was employed to make use of Br as an internal field. A shifted major B-H loop with "unidirectional" (rather than uniaxial) characteristics (Fig. 2) is obtained after magnetizing with H = ± 14,000 Oe. The shitted loop is not observed in the alloy if the material is in the as-annealed or (annealed + wire drawn) condition.

articleTitle: Magnetic and magneto-optical properties of Fe/sub x/Co/sub 1-x//Pd multilayer thin films
abstract: Co/Pd multilayer thin films have been the subject of numerous recent studies because of their unusal properties, and also, their potential application to magneto - optical recording which enables erasable high-density data storage. So far the studies have been focused Co-based systems and little attention has been paid to FeCo-based systems. The purpose of this study is to investigate the effects of Fe-doping on magnetic and magneto-optical properties in Co/Pd multilayer thin films.

articleTitle: Magnetic resonance studies on CdCr/sub 2-x/InSe/sub 4/ thin films
abstract: Recently, two of us have developed the technology for preparing homogeneous thin films of the spinel CdCr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Se<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> with varying amounts of In impurity. Ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) and spin wave resonance (SWR) measurements at 10 GHz at temperatures (T) varying between 4 and 300 K were used to elucidate the magnetic state -- ferromagnet (FM) re-entrant (REE) or spin glass (SG), of the material as a function of In content. However, it is realized that a thorough understanding is not possible without making resonance measurements at several frequencies. For instance, it is impossible to delineate various contributions to the peak-to-peak linewidth (Γ <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PP</sup>) without knowing its frequency dependence. The present report is based on magnetic resonance data on thin films of CdCr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-x</sub>In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Se<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> at several frequencies between 3 and 36 GHz and at 77 < T < 200 K. We will also report on the remarkable sensitivity of the resonance parameters to exposure, of the sample, to modest (-1 mW) amounts of light from a tungsten lamp over a period of a few seconds.

articleTitle: Preferredrystalline orientation of As-melt-spun Nd-Fe-M-B flakes (M =Ti/Zr/Hf/V/Nb/Ta)
abstract: Anisotropic flakes of R-Fe-B magnet alloys (R= Nd/Pr) are of great industrial importance as high performance resin bond magnets, thus much attention had been paid on the attainment of anisotropic ribbons by single-roller melt spinning (SRMS). However, except for the successful report in Pr-Fe-B alloys or by twin-roller melt spinning in Nd-Fe-B alloys, other trials on varying Nd/B contents and casting velocities were failed. Nowadays, the anisotropic powders are obtained by crushing the die-upsetted and hot deformed compacts (MQ3) of melt spun ribbons. It is time and energy consuming this way. A preliminary success of anisotropic Nd-Fe-M-B flakes by SRMS was reported by our group recently. In this paper more details will be presented.

articleTitle: Transitions between intra-wall structures in permalloy thin films
abstract: LaBonte wall structure was found for 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> domain walls in Permalloy thin films by numerically solving Brown's equations. Magnetization distribution inside the wall forms a vortex structure which significantly reduces the magnetostatic energy over the expense of the exchange energy. For very thin films, the vortex wall structure results in large exchange energy. Neel wall structure becomes more energetically favorable if the film thickness is sufficiently small. Here, we present a micromagnetic study of stable equilibrium 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> wall structures in Permalloy thin film IS a function of film thickness. The main results of this study are that for a film within certain range of thickness, there exist two stable equilibrium structures for a 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> wall, corresponding to two local energy minima. A wall structure can be either one of them, depending on the initial conditions. Irreversible transitions between these two equilibrium structures can occur with externally applied temporal pulse field. In this study, the geometry modeling a 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> wall in a Permalloy film is taken to be exactly the same as in ref. 1. Micromagnetic theory is utilized to calculate the free energy inside the wall. Coupled Landau-Lifshitz equations with a damping ratio (λ/γ) = 0.1 are used to determine magnetization field distribution. In the presence of an external field, magnetization rotations in the domains adjacent to the wall were considered. Magnetic material parameters used in the calculations are the same as in ref. 1 for a standard permalloy film material.

articleTitle: A non-enwrapping, single yoke on-line system magnetic testing system for use in the steel industry
abstract: The standardised method of measuring and verifying magnetic properties of electrical steel is currently the Epstein test. This method has a few well known disadvantages such as the waste of material, cutting of strips from wide sheets and it is not a true indication of the magnetic properties along the length of a steel core. These problem can be overcome by use of an On-Line Test system by which the magnetic properties of electrical steels can be monitored during the manufacturing process. There are two different types of on-Line testers whose magnetizing and measurement systems either enwrap or do not enwrap the moving steel strip. All present systems employ magnetising windings which enwrap either the steel or part or all of the yoke being used. This paper describes a new method of magnetisation for a single sided or non-enwrapping system which has potential benifits over existing methods. A non-enwrapping is easier to maintain and has the capability of measuring properties transverse to the rolling direction of the strip. Investigations on the surface of the strip are also much easier to carry out as there are no obstructions to hinder direct access.

articleTitle: Fractal domain structures in thin amorphous films
abstract: The remagnetization processes in thin films of rare earth - transition metal amorphous alloys were theoretically and experimentally investigated. Domain wall motion are known to play a key role in the decay of the metastable state via nucleation. Considering Bloch domain wall we can reduce magnetostatic equations to Laplace equation for magnetostatic potential φ Δφ = 0 The domain wall motion in an external magnetic field which slightly exceeds the coercive force is determined mainly by the fluctuations of magnetic parameters and cannot be treated as continuous one. The jump probability between neighbouring stable states of domain wall is characterized by the difference of the local free energy of stable and metastable phases P <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">˜</sup> exp (-ΔF/T) Monte Carlo simulation based on the (1) and (2) yields us that the domain structures can be interpreted as Laplace fractal with fractal dimension d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub>, determined by the factor z = M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>/T, where M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> is saturation magnetization, and T is the temperature.

articleTitle: Hot pressed FE-ND-B/Al permanent magnets
abstract: Fe-Nd-B magnets are currently being processed via three routes: sintering, melt-spinning and mechanical alloying. The highest energy products and coercivities achieved by any of these approaches are ˜ 50 MGOe and ˜ 25 kOe. Still superior performance may be achieved by utilizing an idealized microstructure of 2-14 grains completely isolated from one another by a non – magnetic phase. In this work, hot isostatic pressing of 2-14 powders mixed with AI-Mg powders followed by additional heat treatments is being used in an effort to attain this ideal microstructure.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties and structure of nitrogenated La(Co/sub 1-x/Fe/sub x/)/sub 13/ compounds (x = 0-0.4)
abstract: The effects of nitrogen on the magnetism of compounds R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> and RFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>Ti have been extensively studied by several groups. The significant improvement of magnetic properties, especially anisotropy, by nitrogenation has led us to extend our study to La(Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sub> systems. LaCo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> "absorbed a considerable amount of nitrogen" at low pressures at temperatures around 300 C. LaCo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sub> has the largest 3d metal content of any known rare earth intermetallics and, accordingly, is of potential applications interest, except for the fact that it has cubic symmetry and hence lacks anisotropy. In the present study, several nitrides, La(Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-xFe<sub>x</sub>)<sub>13</sub> (x = 1-0.4) were synthesized. The effects of nitrogenation temperature on the phase formation, magnetic properties and structure of La(Co,Fe)<sub>13</sub> compounds have been investigated.</sub>

articleTitle: Low-field loss in ferrites-relevance to broadband circular design
Digital magneto-optical sensor
abstract: The magnetic materials are successfully used in the design of fiber optical sensors, which are of great current interest in many fields of application in spite of their high reliability and unsensitivity to external interferences. The progress in the improvement of accuracy and reliability of fiber optical sensors is suppressed by the defect which is characteristic to any analog fiber optic channel - unstability caused by the action of vibration, humidity, radiation etc. upon optical fibers and opto-electronic components. This problem can be solved by digital fiber optical sensor (DFOS), e.d. sensor which is able to measure physicals quantity and to transmit the result in the form of digital code. But at present time successful DFOS resolutions are found for the position and angular frequency measurements only. The effects of external fields on the domain structure in the transparent ferromagnetic materials give rise to exciting possibilities for DFOS design.

articleTitle: The dependency of coercive force Hc value on reciprocal thermal diffusion of Cr and Co for ion-beam-deposited films
abstract: We arrived at a conclusion that the key factor for coercive force Hc increasing was preferring orientation (PO) HCP CoNi(110)/Cr(200) deposition after we had examined the dependence of Hc value on structure. We also determined there that some small amount of disoriented HCP CoNi phase was nessicity to obtain maximum Hc value. The investigation of such films profiles by SIMS analyze method to determine the thermal diffusion mechanism in the films on substrate temperature was the aim of present work.

articleTitle: Dynamic flux trapping in a ceramic superconductor carrying alternating current
abstract: In this paper we report the result of magnetic flux measurements made on a superconducting slab carrying alternating current in the plane of the slab. The behavior of inphase and quadrature components of the voltage induced in pick-up coil as well as higher harmonic signals are discussed. The sample of single-phase Bl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Ca<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub> ceramics with dimensions 8.5⋅7⋅0.9mm was placed inside a cylindrical coil consisting of about 2000 turns of 0.06mm cooper wire with internal and external radii of 20 and 22mm respectively, and height of 12mm. The plane of the slab was perpendicular to the coil axis. Electrical contacts (1mm width indium strips) were attached to the sample along the longest border. The contact resistance was less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> Ohm. A 250 Ohm resistor was connected in series to the sample to provide a constant value of current throughout the superconducting transition. All measurements were made at 130Hz during the cooling of specimen while carrying a current of certain magnitude from above T to 77K.

articleTitle: Nitrogen diffusion patterns on Re/sub 2/Fe/sub 17/ compounds, R=Pr, Nd, Sm and Gd
abstract: We did some experiments on nitriding of the 2:17 phase of the systems Fe-R, R= Pr, Nd, Sm and Gd in order to get information about the kinetics of the nitrogenation.

articleTitle: New type micro cloth-inductor and transformer with thin amorphous wires and multi-thin coils
abstract: The inductor in cloth structure woven of magnetic amorphous wire and copper wire has been reported by a part of authors. In an inductor using magnetic cores, it is important to reduce loss due to eddy currents in high frequency. Therefore, it is required that thinner amorphous wires are bounded by the copper wire without contact each other in wire cloth inductor. On the other hand, effective diameter of exciting copper coil is determined by skin depth. It is important to prepare the inductor and transformer with thin amorphous wire and copper wire in which diameter is lower than skin depth. In this paper, it is proposed new type cloth inductor and transformer with ultra thin amorphous wire and multi thin coil and then reported these inductor and transformer are useful to miniaturization in size, to increase frequency operation of wire cloth inductor and to get high coupling constant and current capacity of cloth transformer.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Sm/sub 2/(Fe/sub 1-x/N/sub x)/sub 17/N/sub y/ alloys
abstract: Recently, a new intermetallic compound with the composition Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-δ</sub> has been found. Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-δ</sub>3-δ has a rhombohedral structure related to that of Th<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Zn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>. The three intrinsic magnetic properties related to permanent magnets are a high Curie temperature of 470°C a strong uniaxial anisotropy field of 14T and a high temperature magnetization of 1.5T. This paper aims to study magnetic properties of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>(Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>Ny alloys.

articleTitle: Optomagnetic amplifier
abstract: A new type of devices is offered for amplification and transformation of signals in the form of Electromagnetic radiation of optical band primarily. The amplification devices of the offered type are schematically simple, highly reliable, highly resistant to radiative and thermal effects. They can be supplied directly from a.c. mains (without intermediate transducer), this possess high efficiency (about 0.95). The devices offered for amplification of optical signals include neither electronic (semiconducting) nor vacuum amplification elements and nevertheless they permit to obtain estremely high (about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>) values of power amplification factor one cascade. A new type of amplifier is named an optomagnetic amplifier. An optomagnetic amplifier is a promising one to be used in the systems of power electronics (especially in the switch-mode power suppliers) and management with automatization of various production processes in metallurgy, machine-building, mining, chemical and other industries as well as in the devices for visualization and control of the state of objects of different physical nature. Powerful optically coupled pair for control systems, transducers-modulators of optical signals, photo-relay of various kinds, photo-sensors with high levels of an output signal, recorders of signal light pulses etc. can be done on the basis of an optomagnetic amplifier. An optomagnetic amplifier can be especially effectively used for communication systems (board systems for example), as the high photoelectric, mass and size indexes of the offered amplifier permit to make lower demands of other elements of an optoeletronic system such as fibre-optical communication cables, optical disconnect, radiation sources etc.

articleTitle: 3D-CAD of a magnetostrictive amorphous sensor for movements of human spina
abstract: Amorphous ferromagnetic alloys show both, good mechanical properties but also excellent soft magnetic and magnetoelastic properties; therefore increased attempts have been made to construct new types of sensors, e.g. in the life sciences. Here, a sensor arrangement was developed, which allows monitoring of articular movement of the human spinal column.

articleTitle: Investigation of coil geometry for transcutaneous energy transmission for artificial heart
abstract: Transcutaneous energy transmission for a totally implantable artificial heart system has been considered and we have already reported the non-contact electric energy transmission by means of the spiral coils with the amorphous magnetic fiber. In this paper we investigated the coil design for higher transmitting efficiency and less temperature rise of the coil.

articleTitle: The excitation of spin wave exchange resonances in implanted YIG film layer
abstract: Ion implantation of YIG film was used in a number of works to provide conditions for spin exchange wave excitation. The excitation of both standing and travelling exchange waves was observed experimentally. The ion implantation was assumed to fix spins on a film surface and Kittel's mechanism or spin wave excitation was anticipated to be realvzed in experiments. P. E. Silberman's calculation for excitation efficiency with this mechanism has given a negligible transformation coefficient even at the whole surface spin attachment not matching the experiment evidently. This condition makes to remember that implanted ions do not lie on the very surface but in its depth, in some laver with the thickness being though small, but finite. The thickness of implanted layer can be comparable with the length of excited wave. The last statement follows immediately from the calculation of concentration profile n for helium ions with a living depth level n from the surface of experimental sample.

articleTitle: Direct measurement of the sensitivity distribution of magnetoresistive heads by the SXM technique
abstract: Magnetoresistive (MR) heads have been used in tape devices, and are now coming to be used in hard disk files with high recording density. Their advantage over inductive heads is that the readback signal is high and independent of the head-medium relative velocity. However, their across-track sensitivity is different from that of inductive heads and has different profiles on the two track edges because of the microscopic magnetic nature of the MR element, which affects the off-track performance and cross-talk characteristics. Therefore, it is important to investigate the microscopic sensitivity profiles in the MR element for various methods in order to achieve high track-density recording. In this paper, we present a technique for obtaining the two-dimensional magnetic sensitivity distribution of an MR head with submicron resolution using a scanning probe microscopy (SXM) together with a simultaneous topographic image taken in a conventional SXM mode.

articleTitle: Influence of the tension and torsional stress on the magnetic parameters of a Co-rich stress annealed amorphous wire
abstract: Magnetic anisotropy can be induced in a Co-rich amorphous wire (trademark name AC-20 from UNlTIKA Co. Japan) subjected to stress annealing such as has been recently reported in (1). The evolution of this anisotropy as a function of the annealing time, for isothermal treatments, shows a similar behavior to that widely repoted in amorphous ribbons (2). On the other hand, the magnetic parameters obtained from the hysteresis loop (reduced remanence 3 and coercive field H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> show a strong dependence both with th thermal treatment as with the tensile stress applied in metallic glasses as a consecuence of the internal stresses present in the sample which are given rise during the casting process.

articleTitle: Quadratic frequency dependence of spinwave instability thresholds from fast-relaxing ions
abstract: The influence of ions with short spin-lattice relaxation times, typically rare earth (RE) ions in iron garnets and Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions in garnets or spinels, was investigated extensively during the earlier years of microwave ferrite development. Schloermann et al. reported linear increases in the spinwave linewidths ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> of garnets with ions from several members of the lanthanide series. In later work, Dionne and West employed the theoretical results of Van Vleck to demonstrate a positive linear relation between ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> and the rare earth ion concentration, according to ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> = ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RE</sub> = ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</sub> where ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RE</sub> = CΔh, C is the ratio of fast-relaxing ions to the "net" Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions in the opposing ferrite sublattices (i.e., C is approximately proportional to the rare earth concentration divided by the magnetization, x/4ΠM), and Δh is a parameter that is dependent on frequency ω, exchange frequency ω<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</sub>, temperature, and relaxation time. ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</sup> is the linewidth associated with the iron sublattices.

articleTitle: Nd-Fe-B-Cu HD processed sintered magnets: up-graded properties and microstructure
abstract: Cu as an addition is known to improve the hot-workability of Pr - Fe - B magnets where good magnetic properties have been achieved in hot-deformed material. The same behaviour was also shown for Nd - Fe - B - Cu alloys. All early reports on adding Cu to Nd - Fe - B sintered magnets revealed a deterioration in magnetic properties (e.g.). Recently however, Kianvash and Harris report on a successful production of up-graded sintered Nd - Fe - B - Cu materials due to an optimised heat-treatment. The results obtained so far on optimisation of the processing and the related microstructure is described in the following.

articleTitle: Transverse susceptibility of uniaxial multidomain particles
abstract: The reversible susceptibility tensor of single-domain particles with uniaxial anisotropy was calculated earlier. Recent experimental work shows the influence of multidomain particles on the reversible transverse susceptibility (X<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub>) of isotropic barium-ferrite powders. In our investigation we calculate X<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> as a function of applied field for a multidomain single crystal with uniaxial anisotropy energy. Basis of the study is the phase theory as used by Stewart and Lawton to calculate magnetization curves. Measurements performed on a barium-ferrite single crystal are given for comparison.

articleTitle: Direct experimental study of behaviour of bloch points in oscillating neel line
abstract: Research on the properties of various elements of the domain structure of ferromagnets - domain walls, Neel (Bloch) lines, and Bloch points - has recently been attracting increasing Interest. Methods for observing and experimentally studying the dynamic properties of domain walls and Neel lines were developed a fairly long time ago [1 to 3]. The problem of visualizing Bloch points and of developing methods for studying their dynamic properties, on the other hand, has yet to be solved. In present paper we report the results of the first experimental study of Bloch points.

articleTitle: Direct overwriting and super resolution using exchange-couples magnetic multilayer disks
abstract: Direct overwritability and higher density am desiderata for the next generation of magnetooptical disks. Overwriting by light intensity modulation, which is possible using an exchange-coupled magnetic multilayer disk, is more suitable for modulation at a high frequency than overwriting by magnetic field modulation. In fact, light intensity modulation is the only way to record on a double-sided disk and to use a multibeam optical pickup. Magnetically induced Super Resolution (MSR) using a magnetic multilayer disk is a very promising technique for increasing recording density, because the current optics can be used. This paper reports multilayer disks capable of overwriting and super resolution.

articleTitle: Effect of Co content o magnetic properties of hot-worked Nd-Dy-Ce-Fe-Co-B magnets
abstract: In a previous study, the authors reported the effect of cerium in improving the hot workability of Nd-Fe-Co-B magnets; also dysprosium was found to improve the heat resistance temperature of the hot worked magnets. In this study the effect of cobalt content on the magnetic properties of hot worked Nd-Dy-Ce-Fe-Co-B magnets are reported.

articleTitle: Magnetization reversal mechanism evaluated by rotational hysteresis loss analysis for the thin film media
Coercivity development from annealing PtCoB melt spun ribbons
abstract: Large increases in coercivity of binary Pt-Co magnets have been obtained by the addition of boron and the application of rapid solidification by melt spinning with subsequent vacuum annealing. The coercivity for Pt-Co-B ternary alloys is more than double that of the highest coercivity observed for the Pt-Co binary system. Increased coercivity coupled with special properties such as corrosion resistance and ductility may expand the potential applications for these alloys. An alloy of Pt<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">42</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">45</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sub> (at. %) (Pt-Co-B) has been rapidly solidified by melt Spinning. The specimens were then annealed at 650<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C for 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 minutes to study the magnetic hardening mechanisms. The coercivity was measured using a vibrating sample magnetometer. Microstructural characterization (optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, analytical electron microscopy and Lorentz electron microscopy) was used to elucidate the mechanism responsible for the increases in coercivity. The magnetic domain structure was investigated by Lorentz phase contrast imaging.

articleTitle: On the YIG waveguides
Microwave characteristics of YBCO coplanar waveguide resonator
abstract: The discovery of high-T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> superconductor oxides has made it possible for a new class of microwave devices operating at temperatures considerably above liquid helium temperatures. Passive microwave components are among the first practical devices fabricated from these high-T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> materials in which the surface resistance R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub>, is a measure of the device performance at any frequency. Also, knowledge of the London penetration depth λ of a superconductor provides further information about microscopic properties of the superconductor state. In this paper a formalism in which R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and λ may be deduced from microwave reflection data of as superconducting resonator has been developed. The object of this paper is to demonstrate the technique of this analysis in deducing fundamental parameters of superconducting films and obtaining circuit parameters of the device. The analysis involves incremental inductance method. We believe that the analysis will serve as a future guide into the design of passive linear devices. Although a coplanar waveguide (CPW) resonator is considered here, our calculations may be applied to other linear resonators, for example, stripline, microstrip line, slot line, etc. One advantage of a CPW resonator over a microstrip or stripline is that both the ground and conducting planes are in the same film plane. A CPW resonator was fabricated from YBCO thin film deposited on MgO substrate by laser deposition techniques. The deduced λ at 0 K was 0.179 μm and R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> was 10.3 mΩ, which is about one third of that of copper at 14.6 8Hz at room temperature.

articleTitle: Soft magnetic FeAlN/Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ multilayered films
abstract: FeAlN has been proposed as a magnetic recording head material because of its high saturation magnetization, low coercivity and low magnetostriction. The soft magnetic properties have been further improved by making multilayer films with SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> interlayers. Two important concerns about the practicality of multilayer films are: (1) film stresses induced during fabrication, due to differential thermal expansion of the magnetic and interlayer materials: and (2) possible deterioration of the soft magnetic properties under heat treatment, due to interdiffusion between the layers. Compared with SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, AI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> has a thermal expansion coefficient closer to that of Fe and so should give less stress. We have deposited FeAIN/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> multilayers with good soft magnetic properties which are stable to annealing at temperatures up to 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C.

articleTitle: Observation of macroscopic quantum effects in high T/sub c/ thin film weak link rings
abstract: Thin film "weak link" rings were constructed using high T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> ceramic YBCO superconductors. The weak links were biased with a Faraday law voltage from an external magnetic flux applied through the ring. The resulting electron pair charges on the weak links were monitored by an output voltage (coupled through a transformer). The charge stored on the link (as a function of the input bias voltage) is consistent with that of a "macroscopic quantum pendulum".

articleTitle: Bias effects on magnetic anisotropy of sputtered Co/Pt multilayers
abstract: Co/Pt multilayers have been investigated extensively for application to magneto-optical recording. The morphology of the sputtered Co/Pt multilayer depends on the sputtering conditions; type and pressure of the sputtering gas, or negative bias voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> applied on the substrate during sputtering. The change in the morphology influences on the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>, and the coercivity. This paper reports the perpendicular anisotropy in the Co/Pt multilayers sputter-deposited with modulated substrate bias voltage.

articleTitle: Magnetic force microscopy: techniques and applications
abstract: This talk will review the techniques and applications of magnetic force microscopy (MFM). Magnetic force microscopy is a relatively new technique for observing magnetic microstructure on surfaces. Magnetic information is acquired by sensing the force acting on a sharp magnetic tip due to the magnetic field emanating from the sample. The magnetic tip is attached to a weak cantilever spring and the interaction force causes both a small deflection of the cantilever and a frequency shift of the cantilever's mechanical resonance frequency. Either of these effects can be used form MFM images. MFM images are formed by sensing one of these two effects while scanning the tip relative to the sample in a raster pattern. In our apparatus, the cantilever motion is detected using a fiber-optic interferometer. Shift in resonant frequency is detected directly using a sensitive frequency demodulation technique.

articleTitle: Nitrogenation effect of the reduction-diffusion Sm/sub x/Fe/sub 1-x/ powders
abstract: Many papers have already reported the excellent magnetic properties of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>Nx (X=2-3) powders, which are suitable for making good metal composite magnet. Up to now, the starting Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> alloys that reported are mostly produced by vacuum induction melting (VM) process, the ingot usually consists of many free iron inside due to insufficient cooling rate during chilling process. Subsequent long homogenization treatment (24 hrs-1 week) 1 before nitrogenization is necessary to dissolve the free iron, it seems to be uneconomic for commercial production. In this study, we tried to prepare the Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> powders by Reduction diffusion (RD) method followed by rapid quench to eliminate the free iron, with the benifit of omiting homogenization treatment. The proper way of nitrogenation of these RD Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> powders has been studied to compare with the effect of that in VM Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>17 powders.

articleTitle: Vibration reduction in electric machine by magnet interlacing
abstract: A principal source of vibration in permanent magnet motors and generators, typically shown in Fig. 1, is the induced travelling forces from the rotating permanent magnet (PM) poles acting on the stator. Sabonnadiere and Lefevre predicted such dynamic reactions of motors using a variety of analytical techniques. Rahman and Jang showed that the driving frequencies could be characterized by Fourier decomposition of the magnetic traction, and demonstrated that the vibration levels may be reduced by shaping the magnets. To avoid coincidence with structural resonances of the machine, it is desirable to reduce both the number of frequency components of the magnetic force and their amplitudes. In this current research, it is demonstrated that vibration levels may be significantly attenuated, without reduction in radial magnetic flux, by altering the magnetic orientation and increasing the magnetic energy product near the pole transitions.

articleTitle: Optimization of gradient coils for magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: The system for generating the gradient magnetic field in Magnetic Resonance Imaging usually consists of three separate coils wound on a cylindrical surface. The most basic design, producing a gradient in the direction of the main field, has the configuration of appropriately spaced circular loops. This design is relatively easy to analyze, as the field pattern is two-dimensional. The design of the two transverse gradient mils, which are identical but rotated by 90 degrees, is much more difficult, because the field distribution is truly three-dimensional. The simplest transverse coil has four turns arranged in a double saddle-type configuration. This design can be treated as the first approximation to a more generalized class of transverse gradient coils.

articleTitle: A novel approach for magnetocardiagram analysis
abstract: The inverse problem is one of the most important problems in medical applications because most of the medical diagnosis can be reduced to solving the inverse problems. It is well known that any neural activity in the biological systems accompanies the electric charge movements, and this leads to a magnetic field distribution on the surface of a biological body. Particularly, the magnetic field distribution measured over a heart surface is called the magnetocardiodiagram (MCG). Depending on the heart operating conditions, the MCG exhibits the Distinct patterns so that the MCG analysis is intensively studied for the heart diagnosis. Furthermore, the relationship between the operation and activation current flows in the human heart has been measured and confirmed by a group of anatomists. This paper demonstrates that the defect of a heart, not detected by the electrocardiodiagram, can be found by the MCG analysis.

articleTitle: Magnetism of intermetallic nitrides: a review
abstract: Zijlstra and Westendorp observed that exposure of high energy magnets composed of SmCo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> to hydrogen resulted in a diminished coercivity. From this, they concluded that SmCo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> was absorbing hydrogen. Following this, Van Vucht, Kuijpers and Bruning observed that LaNi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> absorbed copious amounts of hydrogen. During the past two decades the effect of hydrogen on the magnetism of compounds between the rare earths and the 3d transition metals has been exhaustively studied. Reviews of this work have been published by Wallace and his associates. In 1979 Soga, Sato, Sano and Ikeda tested rare earth intermetallics and discovered that LaCo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> "absorbed a considerable amount of nitrogen" at low pressures and at temperatures around 300 C. In 1987 Higano, Yamagata, Tokoro, Fukuda and Kamino studied nitrogen absorption by the systems RT<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, RT<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, Rt<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> and R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> in which R is a rare earth (usually Sm) and T is either Fe or Co. In many instances their heat treating was so high that nitrogen was lost via combination with R (vide infra). However, in one instance their work is of value even today. Upon treating Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> at 500 C for 15 hours, they found that its σ value (emu/g) increased from ∿ 110 to ∿ 165. We now know that they formed the nitride of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>.

articleTitle: Improvement of core loss by chemical thinning in a thick amorphous alloy ribbon
abstract: Usual domain refining method, in general, does not greatly improve the core loss of amorphous magnetic alloys, because of their eddy current loss fraction much smaller than that of silicon steel. Then in this study we deal with the effect of chemical thinning, which is likely to be effective for core loss improvement through hysteresis loss reduction.

articleTitle: Effect of magnetic dissipation on propagation of dipole spin-wave envelope solitons in yttrium iron garnet films
Magnetic properties of Sm/sub 2/Fe/sub 17/(C/sub 9/N)/sub x/ and its hardening by rapid quenching and mechanical alloying
abstract: Since the first report on the high uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy of Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17<sub>N<sub>3 by Coey and coworkers in 1990 significant progress has been made in the understanding of the magnetism and the magnetic hardening of this interstitial compound. This contribution describes the variation of the intrinsic magnetic properties with a) the nitrogen content, b) the substitution of Fe by Co and c) that of Sm by Nd. The principles of magnetic hardening by non-equilibrium 1echniques will be discussed. Sm<sub>2Fe<sub>17</sub>N<sub>x</sub> forms a complete series of solid solutions for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3 and the direction of easy magnetization changes from easy plane (for x = 0) to easy cone (for x - 0.4) and finally to easy axis (for x > 0.5). Only complete nitrogenation to x = 3 results in optimum magnetic properties, i.e. an anisotropy field, H<sub>g</sub>, of 21.4 T, a saturation polarisation, J<sub>g</sub>, of 1.52 T and a Curie temperature, T<sub>c</sub>, of 473 °C. These properties can be further improved by Co-substitution showing maxima in the dependence on the Co-content x within the series Sm<sub>2</sub>(Fe<sub>1-x</sub>Co<sub>x</sub>)<sub>17</sub>N<sub>3</sub>. Contrary to Sm<sub>2</sub>Fe<sub>17</sub>N<sub>3</sub> the T, of Co-rich compositions is reduced by nitrogenation. For (Sm<sub>1-x</sub>Nd<sub>x</sub>)<sub>17</sub>N<sub>3</sub> the anisotropy field decreases linearly with Nd-content while T<sub>c</sub> and J<sub>g</sub> are only slightly changed.</sub></sub></sub></sub>

articleTitle: Variation of loss per cycle with pause time at the maxims flux density in electrical iron sheets
abstract: Power losses of electrical iron sheets have been measured under magnetizing condition in which magnetic induction was controlled to change with a constant time rate for a fixed time and to pause at the highest induction for a varied time in each half magnetizing cycle, to be trapezoidal, and a interesting result that losses in each magnetizing cycle increase with the time of pause period have been found and the increase of losses is considered to be from several magnetic relaxation phenomena.

articleTitle: The disproporationation of Nd/sub 2/Fe/sub 14/B under hydrogen in NdFeB alloys
abstract: The HDDR process route involves heating NdFeB under hydrogen to 600-750°C causing the Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>2Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sub>B phase to disproportionate to Fe, NdH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sub>, and Fe <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>B, and then cooling under vacuum to cause recombination. Under optimum conditions, the recombined material has an extremely fine microstructure, which exhibits appreciable coercivity (around 1000kAm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) thus enabling the material to be bonded. The exact processing conditions have been discussed by McGuiness et al, and Takeshita and Nakayama.

articleTitle: Magnetoresistive properties of spin valves
abstract: We describe the magnetoresistive properties of spin-valve sandwiches comprising Substrate/U/F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>/M/F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/AF/C, where U is an underlayer (e.g. Cu, Ru, Ta), F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, and F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> are ferromagnetic metals or alloys (e.g. Fe. Co, Ni, Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</sub>Fe <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub>), M is a nonmagnetic metal (e.g. AI, Cu, Ag, Au, Cr, Pd, Ta, Pt), AF is an antiferromagnet (e.g. Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub>) and C is a protective capping layer (e.g. Cu. Ag, Au, Ta). The thicknesses of F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and M are smaller than or comparable to the electron mean free paths. The resistance of layers U, AF, and C is typically an order of magnitude larger than that of F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>/M/F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, so that shunting by the former layers is small. The role of the antiferromagnet is to constrain, by exchange anisotropy, the magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> of ferromagnet F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Since the magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> is nearly decoupled from M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> by applying a small field H ≤ 100Oe, one can vary the relative angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> between the two magnetizations. When a rotating field is applied in the plane of the structure, as θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> varies between 0 and 2 Π, both F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, and F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, are in single-domain states. The change in resistance ΔR/R relative to parallel alignment is linear in cos θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> and was termed the spin-valve effect. At its origin lies spin-dependent scattering within the bulk of the ferromagnetic layers and/or at the F/M interface. We have shown that the spin-valve effect (or giant magnetoresistance) is fundamentally unrelated to the antiparallel coupling seen in some multilayers.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of a novel 5Ba0.4Fe/sub 2/O/sub 3/ compound
abstract: In the Bao-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>o<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> binary system, a novel compound whom chemical formula being identified to be 5Bao 4Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2o</sub>3 was synthesized by a hydrothermal method by our group. It shows different structure and properties from other compounds known in the binary system, and exists as hexagonal plate of 0.5 um in diameter. The crystal structure and magnetic properties of these fine particulates are presented.

articleTitle: A nondispersive bandwidth tunable magnetostatic wave filter
Low-temperature magnetic excitations in quasiperodic superlattices
abstract: Due to the discovery of icosahedral point-group symmetry in AI-Mn alloys, great interest has been drawn recently in a new kind of layered systems, quasiperiodic superlattices, which are formed from two kinds of films (layers), arranged according to the Fibonacci sequence. Many experimental and theoretical works have been done on these quasiperiodic superlattice systems. Here we study theoretically the low-temperature magnetic excitations of quasiperiodic superlattices for both the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interface-coupling cases. A unified formulation of the problem for both cases is given. The spectra and some related physical quantities of these systems are discussed.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of a granular thin film media AGFE
abstract: Magnetic granular solids are of great interest in magnetic recording and their applications derivated. In this work, fine particules of iron are prepared in Ag matrix by radio frequency sputtering from a AgFe target. The AgFe binary system is one with a solubility wich is less than 1% in both the liquid and solid states. Tthe usual metallurgical process would not yield FeAg alloys. In this paper we report the making of granular FeAg samples, and their magnetic studies after annealing.

articleTitle: Deconvolution of magnetic force images by Fourier analysis
abstract: Magnetic Force Microscopy (MFM) provides excellent spatial resolution of qualitative magnetic features from surface micro-fields. However, quantitative information is difficult to interpret from magnetic force images due to the long range nature of magnetic interactions and poorly defined magnetic tip properties. For example, magnetic images using two different MFM probes may result in images that appear very different, even though the same sample is used. Figures 1a and 1b show images of the same sample obtained with two different Ni tips. This result is due to the inherent nature of the interaction between the tip and sample, which greatly depends on the tip's moment orientation, the shape, and size of the active magnetic volume of the MFM tip. In the past, MFM image interpretation has been limited to numeric calculations, which model the force response between the tip and sample as a function of position. However, inherent to these calculations is a required a priori knowledge of the tip geometry and its magnetic properties. Therefore, it is desirable to realize experimentally an impulse response which possesses the specific details of the interaction between the tip and sample micro-field. This is critically important to fully deconvolve MFM force images into a mapping of magnetic features which are independent of the specific magnetic and geometric properties of the tip.

articleTitle: A novel preparation route for the Nitromag alloy
abstract: The Nitromag alloy is a had magnetic alloy represented by the formula Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+∂</sub> with ∂-0.7 first proposed by Coey in 1990. We have investigated the processing of this alloy with respect to increased industrial viability and specifically with regard to the removal of the long homogenisation period usually associated with the material. To this end, the addition of niobium up to 10% in the cast alloy has been investigated. We have also examined the subsequent nitriding characteristics and magnetic properties of the alloy. The parent compound of the Nitromag alloy, Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> forms through a peritectic reaction between alpha iron and a Sm rich liquid. The large quantities (-25%) of free iron thereby produced in the cast state can be removed by long high temperature homogenisation treatments e.g. 950°C for 10 days. However such treatments can involve the progressive loss of the volatile Sm component. In this work we have succeeded in producing a cast alloy which requires no homogenisation and contains in its cast form <0.1% free iron. This has been achieved through the addition of between 3% and 5% Nb to the melt; the Nb reacts in the molten state with iron to form a paramagnetic phase NbFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (figure 1) and the resultant alloy is free of α-Fe. No evidence has been found to date to indicate that the NbFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> phase effects adversely the magnetic properties of the nitrided alloy. Mossbauer and thermomagnetic analysis have been used to analyse the material for additional ferromagnetic phases such as SmFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, whilst scanning electron microscopy has been used to analyse the interface between NbFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>.

articleTitle: Numerical implementation of the feedback Preisach model
abstract: Magnetostrictive and piezoelectric materials are currently widely used in fine positioning applications. To reduce detrimental effects of hysteretic properties of these materials on the accuracy of positioning, various feedback controllers can be used. This poses an interesting problem of investigation of Preisach-type models with feedback. The feedback Preisach models also naturally arise as a result of demagnetizing field phenomena. This is because hysteretic materials usually "feel" not applied field8 but the fields which are superpositions of applied and demagnetizing fields. Since demagnetizing fields are proportional to the resulting magnetization (output), the feedback connection is thus formed.

articleTitle: Double disc alternators with hybrid excitation
abstract: Some previous papers describe the concept and performance of double disc alternators (refs.1-3). These machines carry the excitation and armature windings on the stationary assembly. Fig 1 shows the general arrangement. The rotor is constructed from solid steel and comprises a cylindrical hub which is coaxial with the shaft and which connects together two rotor paddles. The stator core is a strip wound laminated annulus. It carries a Gramme-ring ac winding, The solenoidal field coil is coaxial with the hub and attached to the stator assembly. In the previous alternators (refs.2 &3) this field coil was the role means of excitation. In the new machines with hybrid excitation described in this paper the main excitation is provided by rare-earth magnets attached to the rotor paddles as seen in Fig 1; the field coil is designed to provide voltage control only. A 5kW 4 pole test machine has been constructed which can be used to provide three test configurations: a hybrid machine (Type A); a small gap machine in which the permanent magnets have been replaced by mild steel pole pieces of the same dimension as the magnets (this is used for comparison purposes) (Type B); a large gap machine without either pole pieces or permanent magnets (this is used to find the reactances of the hybrid machine) (Type C).

articleTitle: Electronic structure and magnetic properties f R/sub 2/Fe/sub 17/N/sub x/
abstract: The discovery of a remarkable improvement in the magnetic properties oi nitrogenated R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> compounds has been a source of considerable excitement in the field of hard magnets. This paper will review the study of magnetism in these compounds based on self-consistent, spin-polarized electronic-structure calculations. These studies have been carried out on Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe11 compound, a prototype R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> system. The first calculation for rhombohedral Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> was carried out by Coehoorn, who found saturation magnetization in very good agreement with the experimental data. Beuerle et al. studied hexagonal Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> as well as its expanded form due to nitrogenation but without nitrogen atoms. Jaswal el al. carried out the spin-polarized calculations for hexagonal Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> and Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. Their magnetization results before and after nitrogenation are in very good agreement with the experimental data. Based on the spin-fluctuation theory of Mohn and Wohlfarth, their band-structure results correctly predict more than doubling of the Curie temperature upon nitrogenation as observed experimentally. The calculated results and their comparison with the experimental data will be reviewed.

articleTitle: Relation of eddy current losses with domain wall movement of very thin 3%Si-Fe strip-wound cores
abstract: We have already reported an observation method for the dynamic domain pattern of grain oriented very thin 3% Si-Fe strip-wound cores by using a SEM and discussed the relation of the measured eddy current losses with the calculated ones qualitatively. In order to discuss such a relation quantitatively, the wound strip is expected to have uniform magnetic characteristics and domain wall bowing should be examined because the domain observation is available only at the core surface, although the eddy current loss is generated at everywhere in the core.

articleTitle: YIG tuners for RF cavities
abstract: Tuning of RF cavities in electron storage rings is needed to maintain accelerating gap voltage under varying beam load conditions. Conventionally, this has been done using motor driven capacitive posts or inductive loops. Under conditions of fast injection, the need exists for a different type of tuner in which the mechanical movements of the tuning elements are eliminated.

articleTitle: A prototype of mass storage bloch line memory
abstract: Since the proposal of vertical Bloch line (VBL) memory, extensive studies on chip architecture as well as investigation on the device functions have been conducted. We already developed a VBL memory using a ring-shaped domain structure as a minor loop, and confirmed minor loop VBL round propagation as well as transfer gate operation and major line bubble propagation, although multi minor loop initialization was not yet examined. In order to demonstrate the feasibility of this device structure, a 0.3 kbit VBL memory with major/minor loop architecture has been developed using partially milled multi ring-shaped domains for minor loops. The chip was fabricated on a 5 um bubble garnet fil m of which composition is (YSmLuCa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>3 (FeGe)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>0<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>. Principal device functions such as ring-shaped minor loops, R/W gates and major line are composed of partially milled grooves on the film surface and tri-layer conductor patterns.

articleTitle: Physical interpretation of induction and frequency dependence of power losses in soft magnetic materials
abstract: Improvements in the physical interpretation of the dependence of power losses on induction, frequency and microstructure in soft magnetic materials are playing an increasingly important role, in favoring improvements of the quality of electrical steels at the production stage and a more effective optimization of their operating conditions. At the same time, a detailed comprehension of loss mechanisms is needed whenever loss measurements are exploited as a non-destructive tool to obtain microstructural information on grain size, texture, internal stresses, and so on.
