Progress in this direction has been achieved in recent years by a statistical loss theory, which provides a physical justification for the separation of losses into the hysteresis, classical, and excess contributions, each of which has a characteristic dependence on B, f, and the microstructure, which should be separately considered and characterized. In particular, the theory shows that the origin of the excess loss P, can be well understood by describing the magnetization dynamics in terms of a random distribution of magnetic correlation regions (i.e., groups of interacting domain walls), often termed magnetic objects (MO), and by assuming that P, is governed by the statistical distribution of the local threshold fields at which different MOs become magnetically active.

articleTitle: Magnetics of NiFe and Ti composites-effect of annealing
abstract: NiFe thin films, with an adjacent Ti layer for magnetic separation, are used as the magnetoresistive (MR) sensors in tape and disk applications. Annealing studies were reported on NiFe thin films. The present work involves studying the magnetic property changes of 65 nm thick NiFe/20 nm thick Ti (Ti over NiFe) and Ti/NiFe composite films annealed at 300<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>9 C for two hours in air or vacuum. Each film layer was exposed to ambient in order to understand the effect of air passivation.

articleTitle: Phases and magnetic properties of mechanically milled Pr-Fe-B-X alloys during heat treatment
abstract: Amorphous alloys have been prepared mainly by the rapid solidification method. The amorphous alloys by a solid state amorphization reaction have been studied since Schwarz and Jonhson's discovery. Schultz et al. reported that the mechanical alloying with pure elements as starting materials was a effective method for preparing the isotropic rare earth permanent magnets and the magnetic properties are comparable to those of rapidly quenched flakes. Recently we reported that mechanical milling of pre-alloyed Pr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">79.85</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</sub> and subsequent annealing showed good magnetic properties iHc˜19.7 kOe, (BH)max˜10.2 MGOe. In this paper, structural changes caused by mechanical milling and subsequent heat treatment were studied and the effect of additive elements on magnetic properties of Pr-Fe-B alloy was investigated.

articleTitle: Anistropic epoxy bonded magnets from NdFeBZr
Giant magnetoresistance of narrow stripes
abstract: A simple model for magnetoresistance in thin magnetic sandwiches was developed. Giant Magnetoresistance (GMR) was measured using the resistances of etched narrow stripes of magnetic sandwiches having two magnetic films and thin conducting interlayers while varying magnetic fields applied to this sandwich by passing current through the stripes and by external fields. The magnetic layers were sputtered (80-20) NiFe films and CoFe films in the thickness range of 20A to 160A. The conducting interlayers were sputtered Cu films and sputtered non-magnetic alloy films of CuNi in the thickness range of 10A to 60A. The range of observed GMR was from 0.2% and more than 4%. The experimental results agree well with the model.

articleTitle: Measurement of transient temperature during thermomagnetic writing in magneto-optical recording media
abstract: Thermomagnetic (TM) recording is a thermal interaction between the applied Laser energy and magnetic thin films occurring in about a hundred nsec or less which writes and erases magnetic domains in magneto-optical (MO) media. Analytical approaches have been used to derive temperature profiles during TM writing. Beside the complicated calculations, the approaches use thermal properties of given thin films whose values are often those of bulk materials which may be significantly different from those of thin films. The results yield limited success to quantify TM recording processes. Measuring temperature profiles occurring in a sub-μm scale within Iess than a hundred-nsec is, nevertheless, a fairly difficult task. Consequently, few experimental results have been reported on TM writing. We have built a time-resolved microscope system to measure temperature profiles and to monitor the recording process visually during TM writing. The temporal and spatial resolutions of the system are better than 5 nsec and sub-μm, respectively. Using a measured temperature dependence of the Kerr effect of a given MO film, the Kerr contrast is used as a sub-μm scale thermometer distribution during TM writing. In this paper, we report on the measurement of transient temperature profiles in MO films and comparison with analytical results.

articleTitle: In-plane anistropies in polycrystalline Ni films induced by Xe bombardment during deposition
abstract: Uniaxial magnetic anisotropies in thin films can be induced in several different ways. For example, an applied magnetic field or oblique incidence deposition are two well known methods to orient the anisotropy axis of the growing film. We have extended our earlier studies and show that in the case of pure Ni films oblique incidence secondary ion bombardment during film growth induces a uniaxial anisotropy within the film plane, whose orientation and magnitude is determined by the plane of incidence, by the flux rate, and the energy of the secondary ions.

articleTitle: Assessment of surface texture on thin-film magnetic rigid disk for estimating the mechanical durability of head-disk interface
abstract: Asperity tip geometry as well as spatial distribution of peak height and peak interval over a sample surface of texturized disk is indispensable information to analyze the tribological behavior of head-disk interface. In the previous paper, we proposed a successful method for extracting the relatively high peaks by rolling a virtual circle over a profile. However, it is required to choose an appropriate value for its radius R depending on the contacting conditions and the mechanical properties of head slider and disk surfaces. For an assessment of spatial distribution of the extracted peaks, standard deviation of peak height σ <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>, mean peak interval t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> and its standard deviation σ were selected as the representative parameters. As an amplitude parameter, mean height of valley between two adjoining peaks δ <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> shown in Figure 1(a) was taken into account instead of Ra (center line average roughness). It should be avoided to calculate the asperity tip radius straight forwardly due to its extremely short arc. An alternative way to evaluate the tip geometry is to quantify the segmental area S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> shown in Figure 1(b) and its standard deviation σ <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>. This is a simple calculation and free from round-off error.

articleTitle: Spin-wave envelope solitons in periodically modulated magnetic films
abstract: Spin-wave (SW) envelope solitons have previously been observed in yttrium-iron garnet (YIG) films with strong surface pinning. The solitons are formed in the spectral regions of strong dispersion near the dipole gaps in the dipole-exchange SW spectrum of the film. In the present work we show that another possibility to create regions of strong dispersion, where envelope solitons can be formed, is to put the film in the periodically modulated external bias field. In this case the gaps in the spectrum are created due to the bias field periodicity. For application to YIG with suitable choices of modulated field strength and spatial period, we predict that SW envelope solitons are formed near the gaps in the spectrum. The soliton duration is also estimated.

articleTitle: Author index
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: 1992 Digests of INTERMAG'92 [Front Matter and Table of Contents]
abstract: Presents the front cover, front matter, and table of contents from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: High density overwriting in exchange-coupled magneto-optical multilayer films
abstract: Direct overwrite by light intensity modulation in an exchange-coupled multilayer film has been investigated because many advantages are inherent. The high density overwriting is essential for next generation. We reported the edge jitter on pulse width modulation (PWM) got to be smaller than conventional ones, due to self-sharpening-effect, that is peculiar to the light intensity modulation method. In this paper, we examined the effect of self-sharpening-effect and the possibility of the high density overwriting in the multilayer film.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Fe-Ta-(B)-N films
abstract: A high performance magnetic head for high-density magnetic recording requires soft magnetic materials with high saturation magnetization to cope with high coercivity media. The authors have already reported that Fe-(Ta,Nb,Zr)-N films near the eutectic composition with fine grain structure have good soft magnetic properties and high saturation magnetization, and among these films, Fe-Ta-N films prepared by r.f. reactive sputtering method, after without magnetic field annealing, exhibit isotropic high permeability (μ ≥ 5000 at 1 MHz), small saturation magnetostriction (| λ <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> | < 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>) and high saturation magnetization (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> ≥ 1.6 T). In this study, keeping application to magnetic head devices in mind, film thickness dependence of soft magnetic properties and variations in anisotropy for Fe-Ta-N films annealed in rotating, static and no magnetic field were investigated in detail. Moreover, in order to improve thermal stability of soft magnetic properties, boron was added to Fe-Ta-N films and their magnetic properties and structures were studied.

articleTitle: Geometrical characterization of high-precision coated abrasive tape and its machining conditions for texturizing rigid disks
abstract: Coated abrasive finishing tape is widely used for texturizing magnetic disk substrates. Two types of coated abrasive tapes shown in Figure 1 were prepared, i.e. (I) uniformly distributed structure and (II) Benard cell structure. The nominal grain size is 3μm in diameter for both types. The highly projecting abrasives may be concerned with the actual cutting of rigid disk surface. A three-dimensional diamond stylus instrument whose tip radius is 5μm was adopted for measuring the surface irregularity of coated abrasive tape. The topographic data were quantified at the points of cross stripe intersection as shown in Figure 2. Summits or local maximums were extracted by the nine points smoothing and differentiation method and their relative heights and positions were stored in a microcomputer for the consequent calculations. Figure 3 depicts the locations of projected summits on a regression plane about tape (II) . As an amplitude parameter of all the summits we treated the standard deviation of summit height σ <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub>. In order to select projecting abrasives which can be related to the cutting into rigid disk surface, a virtual cylinder with radius R was rolled over the topographic data repeatedly as shown in Figure 4. Figure 5 shows the relationship between the cumulative number of selected summits N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub> and repeated times N under the condition of R = 500μm and also the variation of σ <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> for the selected summits against N for both tapes. The experimental data in Figure 5 were obtained at three different locations and a little dispersion can be seen. Apart from grain size and its shape, the tapes can be distinguished by N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub> and σ <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub>U in connection with R and N.

articleTitle: Three dimensional finite element analysis of high power microwave devices
abstract: There has recently been a great deal of interest in antennas and scatterers fro high power microwave applications. These devices have been analyzed in two dimensions but are inherently three dimensional in nature. In three dimensions we must deal with a vector function which means in general, three unknowns at each point. The large size of the system of equations as well as the difficulty of dealing with the open boundary nature of the problem has dissuaded many researchers from attempting finite element solutions although lately there has been renewed interest in this method. We present here a three dimensional formulation in terms of either the electric field or magnetic field vector. The open boundary is modeled using the Engquist-Majda absorbing boundary conditions. A sample problem showing the radiation pattern inside and outside the wave launcher will be shown.

articleTitle: Investigation of the stability of AC repulsive-force levitation systems for low-speed Maglev
abstract: Electrodynamic suspension (EDS) maglev system utilizes repulsive forces between onboard superconducting magnets and eddy currents induced in guide way-mounted conductors. The system requires a speed of 20 m/s to achieve lift-off from mechanical support wheels. In the paper, an alternative scheme incorporating repulsive forces between ac excited magnets and conductors is investigated in the case where the conductors are at rest or moving slowly relative to the magnets. Stable levitation at rest or at slow speeds is achieved if the conductor geometry is properly selected. A new secondary conductor design can achieve higher levitation and guidance forces than that provided by the boat-sharped secondary conductor design used in previous work. A small-scale induction-type maglev model has recently been built at Argonne National Laboratory for the verification of several low-speed suspension concepts. The model consists of a 4-m-long guideway and a 10-kg vehicle. The vehicle can be levitated, guided, and propelled back and forth at a low speed by magnetic forces. Several preliminary tests have been conducted on the model and they are in good agreement with theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Effect of silver on mechanical and superconducting properties of YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 7-x/ (123) system
abstract: High-Tc oxide superconductors are required in bulk form in various shapes and sizes to understand the basic mechanisms involved and to develop superconducting materials for useful applications. YBa<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>/Ag composites were prepared by sol-gel method, by adding 0, 10, 20, and 30 wt % and at different sintering temperatures 910, 945, and 975 respectively, in an oxygen atmosphere followed by a soaking of 20 hrs at 450<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C in flowing Oxygen. Samples have been characterised by XRD, electrical resistivity, bulk density, porosity and microstructure studies. Oxigen content was estimated using lattice parameter values. The compressional (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>) and shear (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>) velocities of all the YBa<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7-x</sub>/Ag composites have been carried out by pulse transmission technique. As the ceramic oxides are porus, the elastic moduli are corrected to zero porosity using the Mackenzie's formula. It has been observed that the youngs modulus and rigidity modulus are found to increase with silver content. As such, it can be understood from the experimental values that the atomic binding between the various atoms of 1-2-3/Ag composites, increases with increasing Ag content. Debye temperature (θ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</sup>) of all the samples have also been calculated using Anderson's formula.

articleTitle: An analysis of the magnetization reversal process
abstract: This paper describes the interaction mechanism between magnetic particles of recording media. This interaction has been observed experimentally by studying the deviation from the linear relation of Henkel plots. However, the physical meaning of these plots is not always clear. This paper clarifies the plots by analysis using a mathematical model. We define a new function SFO(h) as the switching field distribution without interaction between magnetic particles. This function is the switching probability density of magnetic particles, measured individually, as a function of magnetic field h given by h=H/H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, where H and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> are externally applied magnetic field and coercive field, respectively. Magnetization is described by a integral of SFO(h).

articleTitle: Field of magnetic recording head with arbitrary core/pole shapes
abstract: This work describes a general method of rigorous solutions for the fields of two-dimensional magnetic recording head models of finite size and arbitrary shape. It is based on mixed boundary conditions, and employs a succession of conformal mappings. The method is a major generalization of the procedure presented in the previous work. Key improvement is the fast iterative computer routine for the determination of constants in the Schwarz-Christoffel (S-C) transformation applied to a polygonal contour of an infinitely permeable core wrapped with an idealized winding. After constants are found, calculation of a head field is performed by the method of navigated integration.

articleTitle: The computer-aided design of magnetizing fixtures for the post-assembly magnetization of rare-earth permanent brushless DC motors
abstract: The post-assembly magnetization of permanent magnet machines is an attractive production route since it eliminates the hazards associated with handling pre-magnetized magnets, when the magnetic forces can lead to contamination by ferrous debris and prevent accurate and rapid assembly. However, it requires the design of magnetizing fixtures which produce higher magnetizing fields than those for the pre-magnetization of magnets. To aid the design of such fixtures, a CAD methodology has been developed and applied to design studies of post-assembly magnetizing fixtures for the brushless dc motors of Fig 1, which are based on radially anisotropic sintered NdFeB magnet rings.

articleTitle: Axially tapered fields in cylindrical spaces
abstract: Devices that employ electron-beam tubes require magnetic fields for beam focussing and guidance. Sometimes the required field is one which varies either in magnitude or direction along the principle beam axis. For certain micro/mm wave sources, an axial field variation of an longitudinal field is required. In applications where transverse fields are required, as in storage rings and particle accelators, field tapering in the axial direction is sometimes necesaray to compensate for changes in the axial beam velocity. The paper shows how variation of the field along the beam axis is effected for both longitudinal and transverse orientation. Field profiles in cylindrical structures of both orientations and various cross sections (square, octagonal and circular) are compared with each other and with a spherical shell source with a tapered longitudinal field.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of the magnetization of nanocrystalline Fe/sub 68.5/Co/sub 5/Nb/sub 3/Cu/sub 1/Si/sub 13.5/B/sub 9/ alloy
abstract: Increasing attention has been given to nanocrystalline Fe-Nb-Cu-Si-B alloy system. Substitution of Co in the Fe-Nb-Cu-Si-B alloy have a influence on the magnetic properties. To understand the magnetic properties of nanocrystalline Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">68.5</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13.5</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sub> alloy, several physical parameters to the annealing temperature were obtained from the temperature-dependent saturation magnetization curves.

articleTitle: Studies of wear damage in RF sputtered carbon-nitrogen protective layer for rigid magnetic storage disks
abstract: In practice, the tribological interactions between a magnetic head slider and a disk can result in signal degradation and cause failure of a disk drive. Although recently used as a protective overcoat, sputtered diamondlike carbon films still have wear failure problems. Therefore, observations of the wear failure mechanism can give us information on how to improve the performance of sputtered carbon coatings. Several investigations and explanations of the failure mechanism involving crack propagation and fatigue have been reported. In addition to those studies, a microscopic SEM investigation of the initiation of slideing wear damage at the head/disk interface at very low rotational velocities has been reported for conventional sputtered carbon-coated unlubricated standard rigid disks. This earlier study showed that significant wear features were found after the first pass. These wear features gradually became larger during several successive passes.

articleTitle: A new technique for passive millimeter wave devices
abstract: An image guide loaded with self biasing ferrite was designed and tested from 26.5 to 40 GHz (Fig. 1). M - type ferrite was used with its C - axis transverse to the direction of propagation, but parallel to the ground plane. Electromagnetic scattering parameters of the device were measured for the magnetic field applied along the C - axis. Our data showed that the nonreciprocal effects was due to a nonuniform external DC magnetic field (H) applied to the ferrite slab. Millimeter wave devices like isolators, filters, modulators, switches etc. can be realized from our design.

articleTitle: A numerical investigation of stript chopping in thin films with prependicular anisotropy
abstract: The detailed dynamic structure of two interacting magnetic domain walls in a thin film with a large anisotropy perpendicular to the plane of the material has been determined by numerical integration of the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation in two dimensions. This configuration permits the simulation of domain wall motion, horizontal Bloch line (HBL) formation and motion, and the collision of the domain walls during stripe chopping. The dynamic structure of the domain walls and final magnetization of the sample has been obtained for a range of initial conditions and externally applied fields. External fields that are spatially uniform as well as those field due to a pair of conductors above the surface of the material have been used in these simulations. We have observed an infinite chopping margin for a pair of domain walls that are initially held together at small separation (by a large bias field) before a spatially uniform chopping pulse is applied. In this case, an unwinding pair of walls will annihilate above a critical field resulting in a uniformly magnetized sample. The corresponding winding pair of walls never annihilates. The infinite margin is due to the fact that the initially winding pair of domain walls always remains, even locally, a winding pair and are therefore held apart by exchange.

articleTitle: High permeability of Fe-Ni-Cr with ultra-high purity
abstract: As is well known, Fe-Ni alloys, particurarly Fe-80%Ni, are used in a wide range of practical applications. Recently, great efforts have been made to decrease the Ni content to reduce production costs. We have found that the magnetic properties of Fe-Ni alloys with 34-46%Ni are dramatically improved by the addition of Cr, as well as the reduction of 0 and S impurities. The purpose of the present paper is to demonstrate the effects of some elements, particularly 0 and S impurities on the magnetic properties of Fe-Ni-Cr soft magnetic alloys.

articleTitle: On the depostion of Y/sub 3/Fe/sub 5/O/sub 12/ by molecular beam epitaxy
abstract: On the application of magnetic thin-film at a microwave and mm-wave regions, it is interesting of to use a periodic structure obtaining by distributing the saturation magnetization on the occasion of the crystal growth. The thin-film devices having non-uniform magnetization might be easily expected to take place an energy localization of magnetostatic wave (MSW) and lightwave propagating in the structure. Previously, we have tried to grow separately Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> by MBE. In this paper we show some results obtained in the thin-film growth experiment of yittrium iron garnet, YIG (Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>) by depositing Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> simultaneously by MBE, and also we indicate a result on quantitative analysis of the film by ESCA.

articleTitle: The oxidation of a NdFeB permanent magnet at 400°C: A sem microhardness and Mösserbauer study
abstract: Permanent magnet samples of composition Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">76</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub> supplied by Philips Components Ltd were heated in an open furnace at 400<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">/slp deg/</sup>C for times up to 29 days. The lightly polished surface of the oxidised magnet was investigated using a JEOL 840A SEM equipped with EDX and WDX. The latter allows the determination of oxygen and boron levels within the sample. High resolution micrographs were taken using a Hitachi 4000 SEM. Microhardness measurements were carried out on different regions of the sample to determine the relative hardness of these regions with respect to a sample of unoxidised Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">76</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub>. Identical samples were studied using Conversion Electron Mössbauer Spectroscopy (CEMS) both prior to polishing, and after polishing to identify the iron containing corrosion products at increasing depths in the sample.

articleTitle: An ultimate high frequency transformer
abstract: In order to realize the ultimate compact size power supplies, it is essential to reduce the size of transformers. One of the ways to reduce the size of transformers is to apply the high frequency excitations. However, such a high frequency exciting condition, we confront a serious difficulty that major performance of the transformer is limited by the high frequency characteristics of core materials. To overcome this difficulty, we have previously developed a new type careless high frequency transformer and reported its basic characteristics. This paper reports that the frequency characteristics of our new type transformer have been dramatically improved and its efficiency readly takes over 90 percent in MHz range even though no magnetic mateial is used for flux paths. This suggests that the transformer may become an ultimate high frequency transformer.

articleTitle: Optical and magnetic measurements of the dependence effects in magneto-optic thin films
abstract: Recent advances in magneto-optic storage media have centred around rare earth - transition metal (RE-TM) alloys of Tb - Fe/Co. I n this paper we compare the results of measuring the magnetic properties of these materials by two different methods. In the first method measurements were performed using a polar kerr magnetometer, that is the surface magnetisation was probed. In the second method bulk magnetisation was measured by means of an alternating gradient force magnetometer (AGFM). Comparison between the two methods above is important as material parameters are frequently determined by bulk magnetic measurement techniques such as VSM or AGFM whereas in real applications it is the polar kerr effect that is used to store information. The materials examined were Tb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub>-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">72</sub>-Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub> single layer alloys 485Å thick, protected by under and overlayers of Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>. Samples 1 and 2 were produced under identical conditions, sample 1 was as sputtered, and sample 2 was laser annealed.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Co-M-C (M = Zr, Hf, Ta) films
Mossbauer spectroscopy and magneto-optical studies of Tb-Fe films
abstract: Magneto-optical (MO) amorphous rare earth – transition metal (RE-TM) films are considered to be good candidates for high-density laser information recording systems. The study of magnetic microstructure and it's connection with MO parameters is of great interest to increase MO efficiency of the media. MO effects in RE-TM amorphous film in the visible wavelength region are known to be associated mostly with the magnetic state of the TM-subsystem. Mossbauer spectroscopy (MS) is one of the most efficient methods to obtain data on the magnitude and direction of TM magnetic moments. The aim of this work is to find a correlation between MO effects and Mossbauer spectrum parameters, as well as to clarify the details of the TM-subsystem microstructure.

articleTitle: Long spin disk lube migration
abstract: The open literature on surface lubricant depletion of magnetic data storage hard disks has generally examined non-porous media having no inner diameter hole and short spin times (e.g., a few hours to a few weeks). Applied surface lubricant was usually thick (above 10 nm) and subject to inertially driven migration. Here we report the depletion of thin surface lubricant (h < 5 nm) on commercially used particulate porous media with radial migration driven by air shear stress over a six year spin period. The radial profile of the outer disk pack assembly surface lubricant thickness after long spin time is characterized by nearly complete depletion near the inner diameter followed by a ramp up to a semi-stable outer dimeter plateau. ID depletion does not occur on interior pack corotating surfaces because of solid body air rotation near the hub and the associated lack of air shear stresses there. Elementary modeling is done for the development of the outer pack surface profile. One such model includes surface lubricant replenishment from subsurface porosity, surface air shear stress, and effective interface slippage of the surface lubricant.

articleTitle: Comparison of effective linewidth and FMR linewidth at 10 GHz in Ho substituted YIG
abstract: The standard technique to study microwave losses in ferrites is ferromagnetic resonance (FMR). The analysis of losses by FMR techniques at a given frequency strictly applies only to the positive external static field that satisfies the FMR condition. The "effective" linewidth technique, however, can be used to study intrinsic losses in materials for fields well above the resonance field. The high field effective linewidth provides a good measure of these "intrinsic" losses, with minimal influence due to two magnon scattering loss contributions related to sample inhomogeneities, etc. In many cases, these intrinsic losses are much lower than the FMR losses and the high field effective linewidth, ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub>, is much smaller than the FMR linewidth, ΔH. This work, however, focuses on rare earth substituted yttrium iron garnet (YIG) for which rapid relaxation losses dominate. In this case, the high field effective linewidth and FMR linewidth are expected to be the same. In this study, measurements of both ΔH and ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> at 10 GHz are used to test the effective linewidth technique for polished spheres of (Ho<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1-x)</sub><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> single crystals. It is found that the linewidths track closely. The high field effective linewidth agrees with the measured FMR linewidth for all but the smallest Ho substitution.

articleTitle: Superconducting propulsion system design for the U.S. baseline Maglev vehicle
abstract: Linear synchronous motor (LSM) design for the baseline U. S. maglev vehicle is detailed for a 480 km/hr. operating speed and a 50 kN nominal thrust rating, 27,000 kg vehicle weight. The basis for selection of the lightweight NbaSn magnet array is given in view of other superconducting wire options and higher field strengths. The specific system proposed is a dual air-core LSM with two independent and identical stator windings embedded in the active guideway of total width 2.8 m. Roll and heave compensation by LSM inverter angle regulation is incorporated for adjustment of the nominal airgap 0.205 m. The vehicle contains 40 magnet pairs all identical in construction arranged in an array of overall length 25.4 m and 16 discrete pods, each constituting one LHe circuit. The magnet design is special due to high shock loading requirements of 1.2 G longitudinal, 0.6 G lateral and 0.3 G vertical that the units must withstand. This necessitates that the superconductor be encapsulated in a stainless steel laminated core assembly. Each magnet operates at a field strength of 600 kAT and 4.2° K.

articleTitle: Synthesis and propeties of T1BaCaCuO films prepared by spray pyrolysis method
abstract: We report the fabrication, characterization and transport properties of TlBaCaCuO (TBCCO) high-T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> superconducting films using a low cost spray pyrolysis technique. This technique is applicable to the fabrication of large-area films for the design and fabrication of manetic suspension balances and microwave devices at low frequencies (1GHz). In the fabrication of these TBCCO superconducting films, two different process stages were involved: a) deposition of precursor BaCaCuO films by spray technique, and b) formation of a superconducting phase by incorporating thallium into the films from the vapor phase (thalliation).

articleTitle: Uniform remanent state noise and its relation to microstructure
abstract: The noise generated in a magnetic tape or disc is closely related to the magnetic microstructure. Even when the medium is in a uniform remanent state, as the head passes over the surface, fluctuations in the stray field from local non-uniformities in the magnetic state will be observed as noise. Furthermore, it would be expected that the different microstructures associated with particulate and thin film media will result in different noise characteristics and that noise from media of the same type will be indicative of subtle differences between their microstructures. In order to examine the effects of microstructure on noise, we have examined the noise associated with the remanent states of a number of media, both commercial and experimental systems which included particulate and thin film types.

articleTitle: Effect of tensile, torsional and compressive stresses in amorphous wires
abstract: Amorphous wires with a circular cross section have a disordered atomic structure and exhibit excellent physical properties such as large Barkhausen jump and the Matteucci effect. The unique characteristics of the wire include robust geometry, ability to be twisted, bundled, torsioned and arrayed. These advantages, together with excellent magnetic characteristics, are quite attractive in novel sensors for measurement of acceleration, torque, in rotary encoders, non-contact switches and security devices. In this investigation, the effect of tensile, compressive and torsional stresses on the magnetic properties of high and low magnetostrictive wires produced by Unitika Ltd., Japan were studided. They include SENCY AF-10, Fe- Si-B, highly magnetostrictive as-quenced wire and its as-drawn version, DF10- 50; AC-20, Co-Fe-Si-B as-quenched low magnetostriction wire and its as-drawn and annealed version, DC2T-100, and Co-Si-B as-quenched negative magnetostriction wire.

articleTitle: The analysis of the magnetostatic fields surrounding a twisted-pair transmission line using integral methods
abstract: In aerospace applications related to the Space Station Freedom (SSF), one of the potential problems is that of the electromagnetic fields surrounding helical twisted-pair transmission lines with infinite boundaries. In order to study these-fields in various situations posed by shieldings, conducting plasma environment, and v x B effects effects due to the ambient geomagnetic fields, the first step one must take is knowledge of the essential nature of the fields associated with such helical conductors. In this paper, only the magnetostatic case for the two-wire twisted-pair transmission line in free space is considered, so that an integral formulation derived from Biot Savart Law associated with Gaussian numerical integral methods [1,2] were employed, as will be detailed in the paper, to deal with this possible three dimensional (3D) problem. A simple example which was tested here is shown in Figure (1), where the DC current flowing in each conductor with opposite direction is equal to 500 A. The detailed geometries of the helical twisted-pair transmission line, which consists of many pitchs, will be given in the paper. The flux density comparisons between twisted-pair and parallel-pair cases were carried out and the effects of the length of the pitch of the helical twisted-pair line on the magnetic field profiles were obtained.

articleTitle: Theory of nonlinearites and pulse asymmetry in high density tape recording
The stress of k/sub 33/, d/sub 33/, d1/1 and u in Tb/sub 0.3/Dy/sub 0.7/Fe/sub 1.95/
abstract: Measurements of k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</sub>, d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</sub>, λ and μ under prestresses of 0-20MPa in a 152mm long and 6mn diameter grain orientated Tb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</sub> Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.95</sub> rod, prepared by a free float zone technique, have shown that the k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</sub> peaks at pre-loads of about 2MPa. Simultaneously the static differential permeability drops by a factor of 2.5. The λ vs. H curve shows a negative dip at low fields with strains of around -100ppm that vary with prestress. This initial negative strain has been explained by Thoelke et. al. [1] using an anisotropic rotational model for magnetization and magnetostriction. According to this model, only rotations of the magnetic moments from the [111], [111] or/and [111] axes to the [112] direction lead to initial negative strains before the sample elongates at higher fields.

articleTitle: Magnetic recording analysis taking into account of hysteresis and eddy current
abstract: To realize a high recording density of the magnetic recording products such as FDD, it is important to clarify the phenomenal mechanism of the magnetization in a thin-film medium and the flux density in a MIG (Metal In Gap) head. The conventional methods have carried out the analysis taking into account of the hysteresis using the curling mode. However, the analysis taking into account of eddy current in the MIG head has not developed. In this paper, we describe a two-dimensional magnetic recording analysis based on the FEM, which take into account of the hysteresis in the medium and the eddy current in the head. In addition, this method is applied to the high density FDD, numerical results obtained by the analysis with and without the eddy current are compared with the measured ones.

articleTitle: Modeling of a passive //sup dl/sub dt// limiter
abstract: The complete paper introduces a composite magnetic device which can be used as a rate of current change (dI/dt) limiter. A simplified model of this device is presented along with performance equations. The results obtained from the simple model are compared to simulations performed using a finite element package, and to a simpler analytical hyperbolic model. The models are in good agreement if the number of segments becomes large.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of magnetic moment of epitaxially grown single crystal Fe/sub 10/Ne/sub 2/
abstract: Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is a very attractive substance from both physics and application sides. This is because its Bs was predicted to be 2.8T by Kim and Takahashi. Recently, we have grown single crystal Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1a</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> films epitaxially on ln<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0 * z</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0 * z</sub> As (001) substrates by using N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas and the mixed gas of NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Bs of these Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> films was as high as 3.0 T. In this study, we investigate the temperature dependence of Bs for Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1a</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> compared with that of Fe in order to obtain fundamental properties of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>.

articleTitle: In-plane anisotropy studies in amorphous FeBSi films
abstract: The presence of an in-plane anisotropy in amorphous films has been the object of study in several laboratoires. In fact such studies have been carried out also in crystalline permalloy films in the 1960s. It is known that the preparation conditions affect not only the magnitude of this anisotropy but also the degree of dispersion. Even in crystalline films such as permalloy, several authors have invoked the presence of local variation in the magnitude of the anisotropy to explain the flux reversal by noncoherent rotation. It is assumed that isotropic stress on a macroscopic scale is the result of randomly distributed uniaxial stresses on microscopic scale. These uniaxial stresses produce local strains and if the film is magnetostrictive it will lead to strain induced anisotropy. It is also known that the dispersion is minimum for zero magnetostriction. We have chosen intentionally for our present study amorphous Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">76</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>, films where the magnetostriction is very large. We have prepared the films at a wide range of argon pressures which is known to give rise to varying amount of stresses in the film. These samples have been investigated and the results discussed.

articleTitle: Generation of winding VBLs and their effect on wall dynamics
abstract: Domain wall structure and its effect on wall mobility have ben studied in a thin, single crystal garnet film of (YBiLu)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (FeGa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>. This sample has saturation magnetization 4 ΠM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> = 186 G; thickness h = 4.63 μm; gyromagnetic ratio γ = 1.78 Oe-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>; anisotropy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> = 1.6 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> Erg cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>; exchange constant A = 1.06 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> erg cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>; and damping constant α = 0.0184. The steady state method of bubble translation in a Rotating Gradient Experiment (RGE) has been used for this study. An isolated magnetic bubble, nucleated at the center of the conductor pattern, was circulated in the clockwise direction using a drive frequency of ω/2π = 90 kHz in this RGE. The trajectory radius R and the phase lag ϕ of the bubble are functions of the wall state and the wall mobility and these observables are related to the tangential and radial drive fields h<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> and h<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>, to obtain the winding number S, the dimensionless momentum p, and the mobility μ of the wall.

articleTitle: Anisotropy influence on the rotational and alternating behaviour of soft magnetic matetial
abstract: Local analysis of the magnetic circuits of electrical machines is more and more performed nowadays. It points out complicated distributions of the magnetic field. Working conditions of the magnetic material and their properties consequently are far from the standard characterization ones: sinusoidal induction at 50 or 60 Hz applied in the rolling or transverse directions. The quality of the electrical steel used and especially its anisotropy modify the flux distributions in the sheet plane and its magnetic properties when it is subjected to an external solicitation. In these investigation, magnetic properties of magnetic materials in rotational and unidirectional field are studied in order to analyse the magnetrocrystalline anisotropy influence.

articleTitle: Higher-order mode waveguide circulators for MM-wavelenghts
abstract: Waveguide circulators are being widely used in mm-wave microwave systems. Their principal disadvantages are the low reproducibility and the narrow frequency bandwidth. The former is due mainly to the uncertainty in the dimensions of the very small ferrite insert. One possible way to overcome this shortcoming is to design the circulator for operation at higher-order mode which leads to greater dimensions of the ferrite insert. Since an upper limit of saturation magnetization exists, the operation frequency bandwidth of these devices decreases at higher frequencies. The bandwidth could be substantially enlarged if two circulaton modes with merging operation regions are used. The purpose of this paper is to investigate higher-order circulation modes both numerically and experimentally and to outline the design procedure for reproducible and broadband mm-wave ferrite circulators.

articleTitle: Hardness and etching studies of flux grown YFeO/sub 3/ crystals
Magnetic properties of multilayered GdDyFeCo thin films
abstract: We have already reported that GdDyFeco film is one of the candidates as a Magneto-optical recording medium under lower applied magnetic fields. An alternating GdDy-FeCo multilayer structure of a short period using two-source sputtering yielded excellent recording characteristics, as shown in Fig. 1. We have conducted research to discover a mechanism for reducing the magnetic field required for recording on GdDyFeCo film with a multilayer structure.

articleTitle: The magnetic properties of pulsed laser deposited single crystal MnZn-ferrite thin films
abstract: The magnetic properties of pulsed laser deposited MnZn-ferrite single crystal thin films have been characterized by static and microwave techniques. Because of their large resistivity and high permeability, ferrites are very important in the design of many static and microwave devices such as isolators, circulators, and phase shifters. Since modern technology is shifting towards miniaturization, it is highly desirable to explore techniques to synthesize thin film ferrite components for these and other device applications. Several synthesis processes for thin film ferrites have already been successfully demonstrated. These include: sol-gel, rf- and dc-sputtering, and ferrite plating. In 1989 Ogale et al. demonstrated that ferrite film could be synthesized by pulsed laser ablation. In this paper we examine the dependence of the magnetocrystalline anisotropy energy and ferrimagnetic resonance on oxygen partial pressure and substrate temperature for a series of pulsed laser deposited MnZn-ferrite films. These results are correlated with the structural analysis obtained by x-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy.

articleTitle: Enhanced tribological performance of rigid disk by using chemically bonded lubricant
abstract: Recent trends in magnetic recordings show higher recording density and faster data transfer rates through lower flying height (less than 4 u") and higher spindle rotation (up to 5400 rpm). Satisfying this technical demand of lower flying height means that the surface of the rigid magnetic disk using Al/NiP substrate must become smoother. Also, the use of alternative substrates such as glass or ceramics should be considered because of their smoothness. The trade-offs is to manufacture a disk that is smooth enough to have good magnetic performance but does not sacrifice the stiction performance. Several types of perfluoropolyether lubricants have been successfully used in thin film magnetic media applications. It is believed that disk lubricants on either smooth disk surfaces or higher inertia disk surfaces should be bonded to some degree to the overcoat materials throughout the lifetime operation of a drive. Lack of lubricant on the disk surface during a drive operation leads to early catastrophic head/disk crashes. The use of "Z-Disoc" reactive lubricant as bonded lubricant on particulate disks shows a tremendous benefit in preventing lubricant spin off from relatively smooth surfaces, which demonstrated long-term head/disk durability.

articleTitle: Thurst derating due to stability requirements of the zig-zag linear synchronous motor-pair integrating lift and thurst for mag-lev vehicles
abstract: The Zig-Zag Linear Synchronous Motor Pair, ZZLSMP is composed of two magnets of which one is shown in Figure 1. These are attached to the mag-lev vehicle boggie as shown in Figure 2, and are reacting against the Zig-Zag shaped rail shown in Figure 3. The coils of each magnet are connected as shown in Figure 4, with dc coils fed from a chopper power amplifier controlling field current to provide lift ct constant gap, Z. The feed back loops involved in field control are shown in Figures 5. The ac coils are, on the other hand, fed from a two phase inverter providing armature currents such that field is distorted among the four sub poles of each magnet and hence propulsion is obtained.

articleTitle: Experimental and theoretical studies of transverse susceptibility in recording media
abstract: An experimental study of the transverse susceptibility X<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> has been undertaken. Measurements have been performed on various types of samples. In parallel with the experimental work a model has been set up with a system of Stoner Wohlfarth (S-W) particles. Good agreement is found between the experimental and theoretical characteristics of the X<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> response.

articleTitle: Micromagnetic Barkhausen emission analysis of Tb/sub 0.3/Dy/sub 0.7/Fe/sub 2/ under the action of an alternating field excitation
abstract: Recent work on the magnetostriction of Tb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</sub>Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> has shown that it can change discontinuously with magnetic field H under certain conditions. Theoretical studies have enabled us to develop a model for the magnetization process in this material and this has indicated that the sharp changes in magnetostriction are caused by discontinuous rotation of domain magnetizations. These rotations, which occur between directions of easy magnetization along the <111> crystallographic axes, also give rise to Barkhausen effect emissions. The Barkhausen emissions occur at different field strengths because they arise from domains having different orientations with respect to the field axis. These domains have different critical field strengths for rotation which we have calculated previously. It appears that all domains with a particular orientation will switch directions discontinuously at the same field strength.

articleTitle: Analytical calculations of flux induction and forces of thick coils with finite length
abstract: In many applications of superconducting thick coils, a good accuracy is needed for the computation of flux densities, forces and stored energies. On the other hand, the determination of the accurate geometry (M.R.I., Homopolar electrical machines ....) is obtained after many tests. Because of the problem of open boundaries, purely numerical methods are not really suitable, especially for air cored devices.

articleTitle: Magnetostrictive properties in laves phase (Ce/sub x/ R/sub 1-x/)Fe/sub 2/
abstract: It is well known that the cubic Laves phase of rare earth-Fez compounds exhibit large magnetostrictive properties. The calculated results, summarized in Table 1, indicate that CeFez possesses highest mygnetostriction of all rare earth-Fez compounds at the temperature of 0 K'. A lot of research was conducted to synthesize CeFez but satisfactory results have not yet been obtained. Although PrFez exhibits huge magnetostrictive properties, it was synthesized only under high pressure. Up to now, most of the investigation and measurement of the magnetostrictive properties of RFez had been carried out by Clark. McMaster et al'. Table 1 shows the values for elements which are possible to synthesize but a dash represents the elements for which synthesis is not possible. The resulting ternary alloy, having composition around Tb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">.3</sub> Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">.7</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.95</sub>, shows high magnetostrictive strain with reduced magnetic crystal anistropic energy. We are the first to achieve the synthesis of the Laves phase (Ce<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>, R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Fez with eutectics by the powder metallogy method. Here, we would explain about the magnetostrictive properties of the above mentioned compound.

articleTitle: Application of a stress-dependent magnetic Preisach hysteresis model on a simulation model for Terfenol-D
abstract: The highly magnetostrictive material Terfenol-D has opened new possibilities to develop novel magnetomechanical devices. In many potential applications it is necessary to take higher order effects into account, such as nonlinearity, eddy currents and hysteresis. Methods of predicting the influence of nonlinearity and eddy currents in Terfenol-D have previously been implemented into a model for transient simulation of Terfenol-D rods. The recently developed stress-dependent magnetic Preisach hysteresis model has given an opportunity to a further extension of the model.

articleTitle: Weak field NMR and EPR spectrometers and magnetometers
abstract: This paper presents the characteristics of different NMR and EPR sensors developed at LETI in the area of earth field magnetometry and spectrometry (see tables 1 and 2). The magnetometers are field-frequency transducers. The nuclear or electronic spins precess around the magnetic field at the Larmor frequency proportional to the field modulus B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> : 2 γ = B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>, where γ is the gyromagnetic ratio of a nucleus (NMR) or an electron (EPR). For some sensors, the resonance signal is amplified using electronic or optical Pumping, leading to very high sensitivities. All the described sensors present different features corresponding to several applications : antisubmarine warfare, borehole logging, current sensing, scientific instrumentation, etc...

articleTitle: Using squids for AC measurements
abstract: With a bandwidth of dc to tens of megahertz and the capability to measure currents at the picoampore level, Superconducting Quantum Interference Devices (SQUIDs) find application in a variety of experimental measurements. While SQUIDs have historically been used primarily for measurement applications at frequencies below a few hundred hertz, the inherent bandwidth and extreme sensitivity of the devices can also make them attractive for use at much higher frequencies. Different feedback schemes and input circuit configurations allow SQUID sensors to be adapted to a variety of experiments. In the most common implementation, a modulation signal of several hundred kilohertz applied to the SQUID produces a periodic output signal which is used as an input to a phase-detection circuit. The phase-detector output is then fed back to the SQUID, locking the device into a specific flux state. This “locked-loop” configuration, which can provide a system linearity of a few parts per million over a dynamic range spanning eight orders of magnitude, has a frequency response starting at dc and is limited at high frequencies by the bandwidth of the phase-detection circuit. Measurements at higher frequencies, well above the roll-off frequency of the phase detector, can be made by detecting the high frequency signal ahead of the phase detector.

articleTitle: Effects of cation distribution on the magnetic and electrical properties of cobalt ferrite
abstract: Cobalt ferrite has the so-called inverse spinel structure, with one-half of Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions on A sites and the rest, together with Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions, on B sites at room temperature. The cation distribution of the cobalt ferrite, however, has been reported to change through heat treatments. During the head-treatment, magnetic and electrical properties of the cobalt ferrite also change due to the cation redistribution. In this study, changes in the magnetic properties and Hall parameters of Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> (X=0.94, 0.97, 1, 1.03) were measured at differnet heating conditions and these results were related to the cation distribution changes.

articleTitle: On the performance of a rate 8/10 matched spectral null code for class-4 partial response
abstract: Class-4 partial response signalling with maximum-likelihood (PRML) detection has been experimentally shown to provide a substantial performance improvement on magnetic recording channels relative to the peak detection method. The performance of the PRML method can be significantly enhanced with coding techniques that impose additional structure in the readback waveform. In this paper, we describe one such technique based on the use or a Matched Spectral Null (MSN) code with Class-4 partial response signalling. The MSN codes are a class of trellis codes for partial response channels, designed to enhance the minimum distance between allowed sequences of channel symbols relative to that for the uncoded system. The relative increase in minimum distance defines the coding gain, which is a measure of the extra immunity to additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). The key idea underlying the design or MSN codes is to match the nulls in the code power spectrum with those of the channel transfer function. The coding gain then depends upon the relative order of the nulls in the code power spectrum and the channel transfer function. Unlike other trellis coding schemes for partial response channels, MSN codes exploit the memory of the the partial response channel and allow reduced-complexity, near maximum-likelihood Viterbi detectors that achieve the theoretical coding gains.

articleTitle: New verticle bloch line memory materials for large operating temperature range
Magnetic field around and iron torus
abstract: The paper presents a semi analytical solution of the magnetic field excited by an infinitely long current filament passing through the hole of an iron torus. To the best knowledge of the authors, this is the first 3D analytical solution for a bounded multiply connected iron region. The solution can be of use when testing 3D magnetostatic software.

articleTitle: Magneto-optic characterization of iron garnet crystals using photoelastic modulation
abstract: The photoelastic modulator (PEM) is now a standard tool for polarimetric measurements. However, existing PEM techniques for characterizing magneto-optic materials are strictly valid only when the degree of polarization is unchanged by the material being characterized. Although this restriction is satisfied by diamagnetic and paramagnetic materials, it is not always satisfied by unsaturated ferromagnetic and ferrimagnetic materials which exhibit domain structure and can produce significant spatial depolarization. This distinction is particularly important in ferrimagnetic materials used for optical sensing of magnetic fields, which exhibit the highest sensitivity in the unsaturated (polydomain) state. In this paper we present a PEM technique for simultaneously measuring Faraday rotation and depolarization. Other features of this technique are the absence of any moving parts (permitting rapid data acquisition), and insensitivity to source (laser) power fluctuations.

articleTitle: High-speed (10-20ns) non-volatile MRAM with folded storage elements
abstract: In magneto-resistive memories (MRAMs), a write can be completed within a few nanoseconds. In the case of reading, access time is a function of cell size. The modest signal level of densely packed small cells require a long read time in the order of several hundred nanoseconds to maintain adequate signal to noise ratio. Larger cells with larger outputs can be read in a much shorter time. Therefore, speed-density trade-offs influence the cell size selection for a MRAM design. This paper presents a high speed sensing scheme which uses folded storage cells and two-turn word lines, together with simulation results.

articleTitle: Application of magnetooptical spectroscopy for investigation of spin fluctuations in Fe/sub 2/P above its curie temperature
abstract: We studied magnetooptical and magnetic properties of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>P films to show applicability of magnetooptical method for investigation of spin fluctuations in weak itinerant electron ferromagnets in the paramagnetic region. The Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>P films were obtained by flash evaporation method onto glass substrate at 623 Κ with 3 nm/s rate in vacuum about 5*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> torr. The thicknesses of films were 150 - 200 nm. The spectral-and temperature dependences of Equatorial Kerr Effect (EKE) in Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>P films were measured at angle of incident to be 70° in the range 300 - 1200 nm (4.0 - 1.0 eV) and temperature region 100 - 650 Κ. Measuring value (δ) has been defined as the ratio of intensitiy change of p – polyrized monochromatic light, caused by magnetic field, to the light intensity without magnetic field: δ = xx I/I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>. The temperature dependence of magnetization of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>P films has been obtained in magnetic field 4*10<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> A/m by Faraday balance technique in argon medium in the range 100 - 700 K. Structure of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>P films has been studied on the sumples of 50 nm thickness by electron diffraction method. In temperature range 100 - 300 Κ magnetization of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>P films films decreases according to the law for typical ferromagnets. The Curie temperature to be T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 290 Κ have been defined as maximum of dM/dT.

articleTitle: Analysis of energy make-up requirements for resonant-type ring magnet power supply
Large Kerr rotation angle and magnetic characteristics of Co-Cr/Al multilayers prepared by palsma-free sputtering
Friction and wear of zirconia overcoated disks
abstract: In order to improve the performance of the head-disk interface, various types of protective overcoats are used on magnetic media. The overcoats arc typically on the order of 25-30 nm thick. Sputtered carbon is the most widely used overcoat, but zirconia (Yamashita et al., 1988). SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and silver have also been used. This paper examines the friction and wear properties of zirconia overcoated disks.

articleTitle: Magneto-optic spectra of EuS-Gd and EuS-Tb films
abstract: Thin films were prepared by coevaporating EuS and Gd metal by abeam onto cooled substrates as previously described for EuS-Tb films. The mole percent Gd was varied from 0 to 80. The films have the f.c.c., NaCI structure, the same as EuS, at least up to 50% Od es determined by x-ray diffraction. The Iattice constant decreases more rapidly than Vegard's law when plotted against the nominal Gd mole fraction indicating possibly a high concentration of sulfur site vacancies. We suggest the general formula for these materials: Eu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-y</sub> □<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub> where y can be less than x if some of the Eu is displaced from the EuS lattice by Gd and rejected to the grain boundaries as Eu metal. The latter process could also contribute to the more rapid decrease in lattice constant than expected based on the nominal Gd mole fraction. The Gd substituted films show increased T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and squareness with increasing Gd concentration es previously observed in the EuS-Tb system. However, in the EuS-Gd system the coercivity increases monotonically to about 1 kOe at 50% Gd whereas in the EuS-Tb system the coercivity is over 4 kOe at 30% Tb. The lower coercivity in the EuSGd system is expected because Gd is nearly an e-state ion depending on how much d character it retains. The resistivity generally decreases with Gd concentration. The 50% Gd has a ρ of about 800 μΩcm and ρH/ ρ = 0.3 %. The effect of Gd on the resistivity suggests that it is contributing electrons to the conduction band as it does in the well known EuS-GdS solid solutions. In our films, however, there is no sulfur to take up some of the electrons donated by the Gd so more electrons are available.

articleTitle: Contactless position sensing in linear reluctance motors
abstract: In a segmental-secondary linear reluctance motor (LRM), the secondary consists of ferromagnetic segments separated by nonmagnetic gaps; the primary has a standard 3- phase distributed winding. There is a tractive force on the secondary which depends on the current-density load-angle δ - defined as the angle between the peak of the primary current-density wave and the Centre of a segment. If -45° < δ < 45°, the secondary will remain synchronised with the primary travelling field. The LRM can then be used for position control by manipulating the vector angle ϕ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> of the primary current density; from the definition of the load-angle δ, the absolute position xxx<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> of the secondary is given by ϕ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> = ϕ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> - δ A new method of measuring δ has been developed, based on magnetic field measurements, which allows contactless position sensing and control of the LRM secondary.

articleTitle: Finite element analysis of nonlinear magnetic devices combined with circuit equations by tableau approach
abstract: The consideration of the magnetizing circuit in the field analysis often suppresses the flexibility of the FEM analysis. Because the implementation of the circuit equation does not entirely become familiar with the formulation of the FEM. This paper describes a new generalized approach for considering the complicated external circuits in the harmonic balance FEM (HBFEM).

articleTitle: Digital recording as a communication channel
abstract: This paper is concerned with describing a digital recording as a digital communication channel. It is assumed that the reciprocity principle is applicable and that the received signal is corrupted with additive white Gaussian noise. The influence of the physical parameters of the channel, such as the gap length, on the matched filter bound and on the loss due to intersymbol interference (ISI) are studied based on the maximum likelihood sequence estimator (MLSE).

articleTitle: Micromagnetic studies of interacting permalloy particles
abstract: We have reported successfully modeling experiments on isolated permalloy particles of sub-micron sizes by numerical micromagnetics. Here we report further studies on interacting pairs of such particles with various placements. We use a new finite element method which gives superior results for single particles. The magnetization is linearly interpolated within each tetrahedral element and the magnetostatic interaction is accurately obtained by integration. The magnetization at the nodal points is found by solution of the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equations. The details of the method will be given elsewhere. The individual particles are those we have previously studied: they are 1.47 μm x 0.18 μm x 0.05 μm, the exchange constant is 1 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> erg/cm, their saturation magnetization is 800 emu, and the crystalline anisotropy is zero. A pair is made by displacing one particle from the other. Three placements are studied: one on top of the other, ride by side and end to end.

articleTitle: Experimental testing of the average Preisach model
A double sided metal-in-gap composite head for 150 Mb/in/sup 2/ recording
abstract: The performance of metal-in-gap (MIG) composite heads have been improved by using a single crystal Mn-Zn ferrite and a double sided metal film in the gap. In this paper, we will discuss the recoding characteristics of MIG heads evaluated precisely with thin film media of various coercive forces. The recording density of the MIG heads were examined in relation with O/W and S/N.

articleTitle: Local magnetoresistive response in thin-film Ni-Fe read elements: a sub-micrometer-resolution measurement system
abstract: Domain wall formation and irreversible processes have long been a problem in magnetoresistive (MR) heads. As the size of the MR sensors becomes smaller (less than 10 μm) for hard-disk storage applications, the magnetoresistive response becomes increasingly characterized by irreversible jumps (Barkhausen noise). The presence of a longitudinal field that opposes the magnetization of the single-domain state destablizes the element.
