Such fields could result from magnetic poles at the ends of the MR element' or misalignment of the applied field. In this work, we describe a sub-micrometer-resolution system that is capable of measuring local MR responses in thin-film MR elements. By mapping the local responses, we can study where domain reversals, where affect the bulk response, occur. We measured both the bulk and local MR responses of a 6 X 6 X 0.035 μm (active area size) NI-Fe film in different field orientations. Our experimental resuIts qualitatively agree with the theoretical calculations of Smith.

articleTitle: Effect of sintering parameters on Zn loss for preparation of high permeability MnZn ferrites
abstract: It is well known that minimizing Zn loss is of paramount importance for high permeability maganese zinc ferrites. Beer and Schwarz have shown that internal stress from Zn loss limits the permeability when growing large grains at high temperatures or for long times. Even though high oxygen content during sintering reduces Zn vaporization, there are still other sources of Zn loss. For example, low partial pressure of oxygen during cooling is the major source of Zn loss. The interaction between saggers and samples is a nther important source of Zn loss. We have stressed the effects of oxygen partial pressure, temperature and saggers on Zn loss in this study.

articleTitle: Low-complexity viterbi detection for a family of partial response systems
abstract: The family of the partial response (PR) systems of the form (1 - D) (1 + D)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> where D is the delay operator and n is a non-negative integer is of particular interest in digital magnetic recording since such models posses the spectral nulls that match the type of bandpass characteristics observed in practice. When n = 1, the result is the well-known class IV PR system (PR4) which has been extensively studied in recent years. An experimental system which couples Viterbi decoding with PR4 modeling has been developed. In this work, we are concerned with cases where n > 1. Although Viterbi detection based on such models results in even better performance than PR4, (assuming perfect equalization is possible), the use of such models is hindered by the computational complexity and storage requirements of the corresponding Viterbi algorithms. In this work, a sub-optimal reduced complexity decoding method is developed which is suitable for the PR systems of the form given above.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of K/sub 2/O-Fe/sub 2/O/sub 3/-Bi/sub 2/O/sub 3/ films fabricated by SOL-GEL processing
abstract: Owing to the merits such as molecular homogeneity and lower processing temperatures, sol-gel processing has been paid attention to fabricate electronic materials in recent years. We have already succeeded in producing various kinds of ferromagnetic oxide powders and/or films such as transparent γ-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> and Bi-substituted YIG<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> by using the sol-gel reaction of a solution of iron (III) nitrate dissolved in ethylene glycol. As an extension of these studies, we have examined K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> films formed on glass plates by coating a gel solution of potassium nitrate and bismuth nitrate added in the solution above. It was found that films of this ternary oxide system have magnetization 4 ΠM=1.8kG which is comparable with that of YIG.

articleTitle: Magnetic and magneto-otpical proerties of EuGaG single crystals
abstract: Europium based garnets constitute interesting compounds both for applications (magneto-optical (MO) devices) and fundamental studies. This is due to a ground state of J=0 and low separation between ground and excited states of Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>. We present here the results concerning the magnetic and MO properties (Faraday rotation (FR)) of Eu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> (EuGaG) single crystals.

articleTitle: Design sensitivity for skin effect and minimum volume optimization of magnetic shields
abstract: Provides an abstract of the presentation and a brief professional biography of the presenter. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Faraday rotation in Fe-based semimagnetic semiconductors
abstract: The principal feature of Fe-based semimagnetic semiconductors is that the main state of magnetic ion is a spin singlet and the magnetization origin is accounted by adding of high level states in magnetic field presence. Such rather new materials knom as Van Vleck paramagnetics are of great fundamental interest now. They differs from well known Mn-based semimagnetic semiconductors which are Curie -Veis paramagnetics. This paper is devoted to investigation of Faraday rotation of CdTe and CdSe crystals doped by Fe fulfilled to study a behavior of exchange interaction and differences in magnetooptic effects of two type paramagnetics mentioned above.

articleTitle: Detection of secondary current and torque squirrel-cage induction motor using amorphous magnetic sensor
A study of wiggle in metal-in-gap heads
abstract: Previous work has shown that a poorly formed interface between Sendust and ferrite in metal-in-gap heads acts effectively as a secondary gap, which produces secondary pulses on the read-back signal. However, in addition to this secondary pulse, wiggles that are not related to the Sendust-ferrite interface have also been observed on the read-back pulses of some heads. In this work, a DSA 602 Digitizing Signal Analyzer and a Scanning Magneto-optic Photometer were used to show that the wiggles can be caused by defects in the ferrite or the Sendust itself. The DSA 602 Digitizing Signal Analyzer was used to analyse the read-back signals of several MIG heads. The results measured on two heads are shown in Figs. 1a and 2a. The signal in Fig. 1a shows wiggle on the left side of the main pulse. The wiggle is not caused by the interface between the Sendust and ferrite because the wiggle appears 0.4 μs earlier than the main pulse whereas the Sendust-ferrite interface corresponds to 0.4 μs after the main pulse. In Fig. 2a, a small pulse can be seen on the right hand side of the main pulse. This small pulse lags the main pulse by 0.34 μs and also does not correspond with the Sendust-ferrite interface.

articleTitle: Applications of magnetic garnet films in integrated optics
abstract: Magnetic garnet films can be used as optical waveguides in the near infrared region where optical communication via glass fiber is developed. Their low optical absorption combined with large Faraday rotation highly qualifies them for integrated optical devices. In this paper applications as optical isolators, modulators, and deflectors are discussed. Problems of adjusting material parameters by controlling chemical compositions and preparation conditions are also addressed.

articleTitle: Thin film head characteristics studied by inductance change from bias current control
Interferometric spacing measurements of the Bernoulli head/disk interface
abstract: Bernoulli flexible disk storage devices feature removable cartridges with flexible magnetic medium in 130 mm (5.25 inch) format. At present. the technology allows storage densities on the order of 6x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> bits/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> resulting in a capacity of 90 MB per cartridge. The rigidly mounted Bernoulli head provides a negative pressure airbearing that releases the flexible medium whenever vibrations become excessive. During operation, the Bernoulli head is in very close proximity to the flexible disk. White light interferometry measurements indicate that the spacing in the area of closest approach is less than 100nm (4 μin). However, white-light interferometry is limited in its resolution since the measurements are based on the identification of fringe colors, and this procedure becomes increasingly more difficult for spacings below 150nm (6μin).

articleTitle: An inverse method in electromagnetism applied to the optimization of inductors
abstract: All linear induction machines use a travelling magnetic field wave created by polyphase currents. The most classical device working on this principle is the Linear Induction Motor (LIM) such as those developped for ground transportation. There are also two other types of linear inductors whose applications belongs to the field of MagnetoHydroDynamics (MHD). First of all, the electromagnetic pumps are used for liquid metals such as the cooling sodium of fast breeder nuclear reactors or cast iron for metallurgical applications. Secondly, some of the various concepts of seawater MHD thrusters for ship propulsion are also linear inductors. We propose an inverse method to find the best primary current spatial distribution leading to the maximum efficiency for any sort of these induction machines. Then, this method is applied to the optimisation of an annular electromagnetic pump whose simple geometry allows to derive an analytical solution of the ideal primary current distribution. This solution is compared to that of a finite element modelling of the pump.

articleTitle: Model of magnetization viscosity in Stoner-Wohlfarth particles
abstract: It is well known that hysteresis has its physical origin in the multiplicity of metastable states. Random perturbations of thermal or other nature may cause a gradual motion of the hysteretic system from one metasable state to others resulting in slow changes of the output variables (such as magnetization). This phenomenon is referred to as "viscosity" or "creep". Recently, Preisach's hysteresis model with stochastic input has been proposed as a model of viscosity in hysteretic systems. Later, this model was generalized to include materials which can be described by hysteresis loops of the Stoner-Wohlfarth particles (or their assembly). In this paper, a model of magnetization viscosity in the Stoner-Wohlfarth particles is obtained for the most general case of vector valued magnetic field and magnetization.

articleTitle: Side writing phenomena in narrow track recording
abstract: Understanding of side writing phenomena is of critical importance for narrow track recording. For typical planar isotropic films, it has been found that significant noise arises from track edges. Electron microscopy studies have shown that track edge patterns in planar isotropic films are significantly different from that in oriented film media. However, effects in the read back voltage and impacts on different detection mechanisms remain unclear. In this paper, computer simulation study of recording properties and noise behavior due to side writing for recoding media with various orientation ratio along the recoding track are presented. The recording media are chosen to be longitudinal thin films and an earlier developed micromagnetic model is utilized in the study. The film is represented by an array which contains 128x128 grains, corresponding to approximately 4μm x 3.6 μm with grain diameter D = 30nm. To resemble oriented film media, a Gaussian distribution of the angles between grain crystalline easy axes and the recording track direction is assumed with an angular dispersion Δ θ (standard deviation). In addition, the easy axes are constrained in the film plane. Films with Δ θ varied from 10° to 90° and with the easy axes randomly oriented in the film plane studied. Recording processes of di-bit transition pairs arc simulated using the Lindhom formula for a finite width ring head of 1.5μ wide. Reproduce voltage pulses are calculated using reciprocity theorem. The initial magnetization state before recording is a previously saturated state. The maximum head field inside the medium is approximately 3.5 times of the medium coercivity in a recording simulation.

articleTitle: Properties of single-domain ferromagnetic particles with distorted external shapes
Exponential series statistical modeling of track misregistration in magnetic storage channels
abstract: The ability to predict off-track performance and to assess the efficiency of signal processing and coding schemes depends on having a good analytic representation of the track misregistration (TMR) noise. We apply the analytical method of exponential series expansion to empirical frequency distributions obtained from measurements of this noise in magnetic storage head-disk-assembly (I IDA) devices. Traditionally, the analytic model used in the industry has been the Gaussian distribution. The use of such a model reduces a huge mass of measurement data to a single number, the dispersion or variance, provided the origin is shifted to the mean value. The argument that is used to justify this procedure is the central limit theorem, which is an asymptotic result.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties and substructure of Ni nanocrystals
abstract: Investigated in the present study, with the use of the Ferromagnetic resonance method (FMR), are magnetic properties of Ni nanocrystals which have been prepared by compacting ultradisperse particles using axial loading. The starting powder was produced by evaporation-condensation technology in inert atmosphere. Its particle site distribution being 7∅ nm. The use of the FHR method was caused by specific interest to surface magnetic properties of nanocrystals.

articleTitle: Magnetization process and recording simulation in bicrystal thin film media
abstract: A recent experimental study shows that bicrystal CoCrPt magnetic films exhibit very interesting micromagnetic behavior during magnetization processes. CoCrPt films with a <1120> texture epitaxially grown on (100) planes of Cr single-crystal films results in the c -axis of the magnetic crystallites oriented along two orthogonal directions (<110>) in a random fashion. In the wok presented here, the bicrystal films are modeled with utilization of an earlier developed micromagnetic model. The film is represented by an array of hexagons closely packed on a triangular lattice. Each hexagon represent a single crystal with uniaxial anisotropy. The crystalline easy axes are only allowed to be in two given orthogonal directions randomly. The simulation study is performed on a Connection Machine CM-2 and the array contains 256x256 grains, which corresponds to approximately 8μmx8μm in area, assuming grain diameter D = 300 Å Fast Fourier Transformation method is implemented to calculate the long-range magnetostatic interaction fields. Magnetization process and hysteresis properties are studied and recorded di-bit transition pattern are investigated. The Lindholm head field formula is used in recording simulation.

articleTitle: Effect of PbO-B/sub 2/O/sub 3/-SiO/sub 2/ glass on preparation of low loss Mn-Zn ferrite
abstract: In a high frequency range of 0.5 to 1MHz, the proportion of eddy current loss in the total core loss of ferrtie increase with the highening of frequency. It has been shown in the literature that addition of CaO, or CaO-SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> can improve the iron loss of Mn-Zn ferrite due to increasing the resistivity of grain boundaries. But the ferrites added with CaO or CaO-SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> alone can not be sintered very well at low temperature, which results in low saturation magnetization. The additives with low melting point does lower the sintering temperature, but only a few effective liquid phase additives to Mn-Zn ferrites are known, and they often make the loss factor worse by about an exaggerated grain growth. Glasses with low melting point (-1000° C) were chosen as liquid phase sintering aid in this study. We will conclude the influence of addition amount of different glasses combined with CaO addition on magnetic properties, and microstructure.

articleTitle: Comparative performance between drop-out detection and viterbi reliability metric erasure flagging
abstract: It is well known that reIiable byte erasure flags can significantly enhance the decoded performance of an interleaved Reed-Solomon (RS) code on a digital magnetic recording channel. This paper compares the improvement afforded by a drop-out detector erasure flagger to the improvement provided by an erasure flagger based on a Class IV partial response (PR4) Viterbi detector. It is shown that, in addition to being less complex, the drop-out detector is the superior erasure flagger when decoded performance is burst-error limited and burst errors are a result of signal level drops. Although the proposed Viterbi erasure flagger is derived heuristically, it performs as well as the optimum method discussed in the references and, hence, the drop-out detector can be claimed to be superior to all such Viterbi flaggers under the assumptions of this paper. The focus is on interleaved Reed-Solomon codes over GF(2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>8), that is, codes whose codewords consist of 8-bit symbols. Hence, we would like to flag byte errors rather than bit errors (although a bit error flagger trivially extends to a byte error flagger). Furthermore, we assume that the recorder decoded performance is limited by burst errors due to drop-outs, tenting, etc., rather than by additive white Gaussian noise as in the references. This is the environment typical of a magnetic tape recorder.

articleTitle: A method permeability measurement of magnetic thin film in the GHz region
abstract: One of the important parameters to evaluate a magnetic material is permeability. But permeability is not easy to measure in thin films at high frequencies up to a few GHz. We have developed a method of permeability measurement of magnetic thin film at high frequency using the S-parameter of a stripline. Various ways to improve the measurement accuracy were investigated by using sensitivity analysis. Effectiveness of this method has been confirmed by measurements of several magnetic materials from 100MHz to 3GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of the degradation of a spaceflight tape recorder
abstract: Beginning shortly after launch, and continuing from orbital insertion around Venus through the prime science mission, one of the two magnetic tape recorders aboard the Magellan spacecraft experienced an increasing bit-error rate. As depicted in Figure 1, the bit errors from the recorder eventually caused the percentage of Venusian radar data frames experiencing errors to exceed 5%, and caused the recorder to be deemed unusable. The bit errors were manifested not as single-bit errors nor as burst errors, which are common errors that may be expected from tape recorders. Instead, as shown in Table 1, the errors were usually characterized by occurrences of slipped bits associated with flipped bits. For example, "1001" radar data patterns were recovered from the recorder as "111" patterns.

articleTitle: Dispersion quality of metal particle inks measured by a magnetic probing technique and its relation to tape quality
abstract: It is a well recognized fact that the dispersion quality of a magnetic ink has a direct bearing on the performance characteristics of the finished particulate media products. Many methods based on optical, flow and magnetic techniques have been described in literature for the characterization of dispersion quality of inks. A magnetic probing method known as DIMAG (DIspersion by MAGnetic measurement) has been claimed to be successful in identifying the presence of single particles, doublets and agglomerates in γ-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> based magnetic inks. In this method, a sample of magnetic ink initially subjected to an alternating magnetic field (<60 Oe) is exposed to a DC magnetic field of much higher intensity (up to 600 Oe) for a short duration (- 10 sec) and the response (amplitude and phase) of the ink to this perturbation is measured. Details of the DIMAG set up have been described in a patent. A study was undertaken to relate the dispersion quality of metal particle inks measured by DIMAG technique to the magnetic characteristics of the tapes. Since the metal particles have higher coercivities (near 1500 Oe), the DIMAG instrument was modified so as to obtain a DC field up to 1000 Oe. Inks were made from passivated metal particles of 1500 Oe coercivity, using a commercially available wetting binder based on a vinyl acetate-vinyl chloride copolymer. This binder was also used as a dispersant. Milling of the ink was carried out in an attritor with alumina balls using a solvent containing 75% THF and 25% cyclohexanone. In the experiments aimed at the elucidation of the effect of milling time on dispersion quality, 10 ml samples of ink were periodically withdrawn from the attritor and were characterized using the DIMAG instrument.

articleTitle: A new approach for calculating rectangular winding parameters
abstract: In order to reduce the calculation complexity of the rectangular winding parameters and to find an accurate method for that, a new method is developed. The proposed method is based on Conformal Transformation of the type w = K exp ((Π / b) z) that transforms a rectangular region into a circular one. Consequently, the electrostatic energy, and surface charges are conserved after application of the method. The method uses two Conformal Transformation (C.T.) according to K and b parameter calculations: the first, T.C. 1, retains the exterior surface and gives the external radius, and the second, T.C. 2, retains the interior surface and gives the internal radius.

articleTitle: Magneto-optical visualizer of magnetic field topology
abstract: Bismuth substituted rare-earth ferrite-garnet films (Bi-REFG) grown by means of liquid phase epitaxy technique (LPE) on gallium-gadolinium garnet (GGGl substrate with (111) orientation were used as magneto-optical (MO) visualizers. The films had the following features: Chemical formula (BiLuPr)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (FeGa)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> thickness, pro /spm mu/m 2 saturation field in (1111 plane, Oe 5 coercivity in (111) plane, Oe 0.5 The magneto-optical head is shown on Fig. 1. MO film by the substrate side was glued by immersion liquid to the widest plane of the glass prism. The prism was a film holder and radiation input, simultaneously. Linearly polarized laser beam was focused through the prism and substrate on the MO layer in the contact place of the latter with current structure. Further, laser beam was undergone total inner reflection on the interface MO film - current structure, was reconstructed by objective and fallen on the photoreceiver. The optical system as a whole was designed like a laser scanning polarimeter.

articleTitle: On the practicability of permanent magnets in the system Sm - Fe - Ti: A constitutional argumentation
abstract: Permanent magnets based on the SmFe11Ti (1/12) compound were considered to compete with Nd2Fe14B based magnets. However, maximum coercivity values reached so far by mechanical alloying or rapid quenching were rather disappointing (≈ 5 kOe). On the other hand, extremely high coercivity values at a low remanence were found in mechanically alloyed Sm-rich samples based on the hexagonal Sm5(Fe,Ti)17 (5/17) compound. As coercivity strongly depends on the microstructure of a magnet, detailed knowledge of the phase relations is indispensable. The yet published papers dealing with this question disagree in several points, and in both the 5/17 compound was not confirmed to exist. Therefore, comprehensive constitutional investigations based on microstructural examinations, X-ray diffraction, EDX and thermal analyses were carried out to clear up the points at issue of the phase diagram and to clarify the question, whether or not magnets in this system could become feasible.

articleTitle: Mechanical sensors based on re-entrant flux reversal
abstract: In this paper we report results of new mechanical sensors, which are based on the domain wall nucleation process. These sensors can detect position and force. It is shown that the position sensor has a linear characteristic with a submicron sensitivity and the force sensor has an almost linear behaviour for measuring force up to 3 N. Low mobility and easy shape of domain walls, allows us to use low cost of electronics, for high sensor sensitivity and linearity.

articleTitle: Domain studies in single-crystal ferrite MIG heads with image-enhanced, wide-field, Kerr microscopy
abstract: Ferrite metal-in-gap (MIG) heads are being extended beyond audio/video to digital storage applications. Pulse distortions and inabilities sometimes observed in read-after-write cycles, can become pronounced with diminished track-widths. When a similar situation arose in thin film heads, magnetic domain instabilities were shown to be responsible through extensive studies, including Kerr-effect microscopy observations. Scanning Kerr microscopy has been used on ferrite MIG heads to evaluate leakage flux from a secondary air gap caused by the ferrite/Sendust interface. As a consequence, this leakage problem has now be minimized with improvements in the processing methods. However, other read-back distortions may still occur and persist even in single-crystal ferrite MIG heads. From a micromagnetic point of view, pulse distortions can be related to the domains, particularly in the critical region close to the media and to the pole tips. This is because the resulting distribution of local permeabilities can cause the air-flux return there to be inhomogeneous. A strong influence of processing conditions on domain complexity is to be expected. Yet little work has been reported investigating possible connections between pulse distortions and the domain configurations themselves. This may be due in part to the Kerr effect being quite small in ferrite, providing domain contrast several times weaker even than in permalloy. None the less, we obtain suitable images to study the new single-crystal MnZn-ferrite MIG heads and show domain orientations and responses depending on surface treatments, geometry, and magnetic history.

articleTitle: Simultaneous fly-height, pitch and crown measurements of RIE sliders by capacitance stripe
abstract: Since the dawn of the industry, the measurement of slider static flying height, pitch, roll and crown have been critical measurements throughout the slider development and manufacturing process. The continued drive toward "contact" recording has already strained some of the older methods based on interferometry. Thus a group from IBM Yorktown Research Laboratory developed a measurement scheme based on capacitance, which has the advantage of growing sensitivity for small head-disk gaps. The capacitance stripe technique allows the characterization of any standard N58 slider. One or several "thin" radial metallic stripes are deposited on an insulating substrate (e.g. glass) to form a spoke-like pattern. The stripes are electrically connected to ground at the disk hub. As a slider flies over a single stripe, the slider-stripe capacitance as a function of time directly profiles the gap between the ABS and the stripe.

articleTitle: Effective Faraday rotation for broad spectrum polychromatic mlight in garnet
abstract: In magneto-optical (MO) current field sensors utilizing Faraday rotation, monochromatic lights of laser diodes (LD) or light emitting diodes (LED) are used in general. However, we have been trying to use in the MO sensors broad-spectrum polychromatic lights of electric lamps (which we call "polychromatic lights" for convenience): The polychromatic lights are free from intensity fluctuation due to reflected light, which is advantageous for attaining a high signal to noise ratio in sensors as compared with the monochromatic lights of LD and LED. We have shown that Faraday rotation for polychromatic light is expressed in terms of "effective Faraday rotation" which is defined operationally. In this paper we summarize the theory on the effective Faraday rotation, and report the results of the measurements on effective Faraday rotation <θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>> for polychromatic lights in a Bi-substituted iron garnet. The Faraday rotation θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> in this garnet changes sign in visible range (see Fig.1). Therefore, we will be able to clearly show that <θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>> calculated from our theory agrees the observation not only in magnitude but also in sign.

articleTitle: Thin film magnetic head composed of inorganic materials
abstract: Today, Hc(coercivity) of magnetic recording mediums is becoming higher as high density recordings are strongly demanded to the mediums, this requires a magnetic head having higher Bs(saturation flux density) for its core material. On the other hand, currently utilized thin film magnetic heads developed for such high density recordings, employ an organic insulation film which is naturally not heat-resistant. This limits the flexibility of selecting magnetic core materials for the heads. This paper discusses a thin film magnetic head which employs a heat-resistant inorganic insulation film and a cobalt family amorphous alloy for its core.

articleTitle: Optimum magnetic-head shape for high-density recording
abstract: This report on the result of experiments are conducted to determine the optimum shape of magnetic-head suitable for high-density recording. The head/tape contacts under various conditions are observed by means of an optical interference fringe method made at a wavelength of 526nm.

articleTitle: Effects of ferrite magnetic wedge on characteristics of capacitor motor controlled by triac
abstract: Revolving electric motors are generally installed with slots and teeth (iron portion between slots) to embed electric conductors. The presence of the slots and the teeth introduces the variation of magnetic reluctances through the magnetic circuit to produce pulsation of the flux distribution in the air gap. As the result, the voltage, current and torque of the motor becomes oscillative to increase electric power losses and at last to decrease motor efficiency. The authors have found that the rectangular hysteresis loop of ferrite materials as the magnetic wedge into motor slot openings are very effective to reduce the pulsation of flux density distribution in the air gap. If the motor is drived in accordance with the loaded conditions, more economical operation is expected. In this study, the capacitor motor has been controlled by the triac. However the voltage wave controlled by the triac is an asymmetric sinusoidal wave and so the flus density distribution in the air gap is disturbed to increase motor power losses and to produce oscillative torque. Thus the ferrite materials were wedged into the slot openings of the capacitor motor controlled by the triac and some experimental discussions have been developed.

articleTitle: Preparation of soft magnetic Fe-N films by ion beam deposition method with strict control of plasma potental
abstract: Ion beam deposition (IBD) method is very attractive to deposit the ionized particles such as metal and reactive gas ions themselves on substrates with direct controllability of the kinetic energy and to form thin films of metallic nitride and boride. It is well known that Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>-N exhibits very different magnetic properties with its degree of nitridation. The crystallographic and magnetic characteristics of Fe -N films formed by using IBD system were investigated in detail, because it can strictly control the degree of nitridation and kinetic energy of depositing particles.

articleTitle: Contact start-stop studies with silicon planer head sliders against thin-film disks
abstract: The horizontal heads can be mass produced inexpensively by using integrated circuit (IC) technology. All horizontal head-slider process steps can be done at the full wafer level, eliminating the precision lapping of rows (which is very labor intensive) presently required in making conventional thin-film heads (CTFH). Cross section of a head slider produced using IC technology referred to as silicon planer head (SPH) slider, is shown in Fig. 1. This head slider (head and ABS) is fabricated on a single-crystal (100) silicon wafer using semiconductor technology. The silicon wafer is coated with SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> coating applied by plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) which ranges in thickness from 5 to 6 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μm</sup>. The SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> film is very dense and provide good friction and wear performance. In this paper, we present contact-start-stop (CSS) data and magnetic performance data on SPH sliders against thin-film disks. The CSS data is compared with that for CTFH sliders made of Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Ti-C material.

articleTitle: Magnetic centers for excess oxygen in YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 6+x/ (x << 1)
abstract: A model is proposed for magnetic centers produced in YBa<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6+x</sub>O by the chains from n oxygens at successive O (1) sites in the basal plane. In the simplest case of n = 1 the center obviously represents a magnetic "dumbbell" of two adjacent Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions (spin ½) with strong AFM exchange ≅ 1200 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> between them. Its singlet ground state is separated by J from the excited triplet state, so dumbbell center is magnetically inert for all the temperatures T < T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> ≪ J. The same behaviour follows also for all 1 ≤ n < 4 in the recently proposed model of electronic structure for insulating phase in this compound, where each chain of n oxygens is presumed to generate magnetic structure of successive (n + 1) Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> spins and (n – 1) O spins with strong AFM coupling between them.

articleTitle: Fluctuation fields of recording particles; the role of anisotropy dispersion
abstract: The fluctuation field H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⨍</sub> has recently been studied because of its relation to the magnetization reversal phenomenon. El-Hilo et al found that H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⨍</sub> is a non-monotonic function of field having a broad minimum. A good fit can be obtained with a model assuming particles with a distribution of volume and anisotropy. Jachow et al have also measured H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⨍</sub> experimentally, finding a similar variation of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⨍</sub> with field. In this paper we show that the minimum in the calculation arises from two competing effects; a decrease in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⨍</sub> with field arising from the volume distribution and an increase arising from the anisotropy dispersion. The results of further calculations are compared with experiment.

articleTitle: Switching mechanism and domain structure of bistable amorphous wires
abstract: A number of works have been recently reported about the outstanding magnetic properties of amorphous wires exhibiting re-entrant flux reversal. This is mainly because such behaviour is useful for technological aplications. The magnetization process of large magnetostriction amorphous wires is characterised by a single large Barkhausen jump at a critical switching field, while for larger applied fields magnetization increases almost reversible up to reach saturation. This magnetization process has been interpreted considering the existence of a core whithin the wire with spontaneous axial easy axis and of an external shell where magnetization is roughly transversely oriented. Then, the switching field has been ascribed to the field necessary to nucleate one or several small domains with reversed magnetization. Being this field larger than the propagating field, once the small domains are nucleated they propagate very quickly along the core of the wire.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Fe formed by H/sub 2/ reduction of lepidocrocite in the presence of exfoliated MoS/sub 2/
abstract: Recently some attention has been directed toward the possibility of harnessing interfacial or surface anisotropies for new particulate materials. These anisotropies should be uniaxial and large, reflecting the reduced symmetry at an interface. A possible embodiment would be some combination of monomolecular flakes of exfoliated MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> to provide interfaces and metallic Fe to provide a large magnetization. In pursuing this possibility we continually encountered lepidocrocite, γ-FeOOH, one of the popular starting points for producing maghemite, γ-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. The usual practice is to decompose lepidocrocite to maghemite, allowing the maghemite to inherit the needle-like morphology of the lepidocrocite. As it also inherits a porous structure, it is sometimes the practice to reduce the maghemite to magnetite (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) and then reoxidize it to maghemite. A major industry is founded on this sort of magic.

articleTitle: Experimental and computational analysis of flux and force in a D.C. linear stepping motor
abstract: One of the advantages in using d.c. linear motors for low speed linear drives is that the position and speed of these motors can be precisely controlled with the help of a feedback circuit. Also linear motors get rid of the rotary-to-linear conversion mechanism, hence reducing the weight, cost, backlash and dynamic complexity which produces friction, and eventually reduce the space required by the drive. Again the NdFeB permanent magnet which has a high energy product can be used as the field source in these motors thus reducing the size and weight of the motors further. This paper describes the experimental and computational analysis of flux and force in a d.c. linear stepping motor. The armature in this motor is stationary and the field is the moving part. The armature is made of a 1 inch square steel core with sections of single turn copper wire wound on it. The field system is mounted inside a cylindrical carriage made from Tufnol material. The flux from a permanent magnet pole crosses the air gap, passes along the armature core and returns through an oppositely magnetised magnet pole and the yoke. The magnetic flux reacts with the current flowing in the armature winding and develops a force which enables the carriage to move relative to the armature.

articleTitle: Modelizaton of ferrometric materials in 2D finite element problems using Preisach's model
abstract: Ferromagnetic materials are widely used in electrotechnical applications. Their essential features are non-linearity and irreversibility. The both of them are important but, while the way to deal with the first is quite clear, the second is often overlooked. This paper aims to report of a method allowing to involve that kind of materials in finite element problems, considering irreversibility as well as non-linearity. When dealing with a two-dimensional problem, it is convenient to choose the vector potential A (defined by (1)) as an unknown because the equation (2) is by the way automatically verified and only a scalar field has to be discretized. Thus, the only equation remaining is (3) where H depends on A through B. B = rot A div B = 0 rot H = J

articleTitle: Permanent magnet structures for XUV image sensors
abstract: In space astronomy there has been considerable recent interest in the spectral region of wavelengths below 1200 Å. The investigation of such radiation is often carried out by means of a windowless detector placed on a Rowland-circle together with a collimating slit and grating as in figure 1. After the to-be-investigated beam passes through the rectangular opening in the detector it impinges upon a photocathode from which it ejects electrons. The electrons are subsequently accelerated toward a collecting anode by an electric field between the electrodes. The rectangular, slab-like electron beam thus formed requires a magnetic field of several hundred Oersteds to keep it focused on the anode. This paper discusses several suitable permanent magnet structures designed to optimize the balance among field uniformity, light weight, small bulk, simple, rugged design and minimum magnetic flux leakage to the detector exterior. The latter is important to allow tight packing of field-sensitive instruments in the space vehicle.

articleTitle: Microstructural investigations of FeN and FeAlN thin films for recording head applications
abstract: FeN thin films have been proposed for use in recording heads. For this application a material should have a high saturation magnetisation (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> > 20kG), a low coercivity (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> < 1Oe), low magnetostiction (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> < 1 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>), a high permeability (μ>4000) and good thermal stability. In previous work, we employed macroscopic studies to investigate how the magnetic properties of FeN films depend on growth parameters. We then presented work on FeAlN thin films and on lamination, both of which gave improved magnetic properties. In this paper we present results, of TEM investigations of the microstructure, on a series of single and multilayer FeN and FeAlN films with systematically adjusted growth parameters. We then discuss how these results relate to the magnetic properties.

articleTitle: Low constant flying height on silicon planar heads
abstract: Silicon planar heads (SPH) was recently described. The complete device (head slider and ABS) is fabricated on silicon wafer, with microelectronic processes. Si02 coats the rails and the head and is used by etching to shape and design ABS. ABS gives essentially flying height and a peripheral secondary surface (PSS) gives essentially flying parameters like pitch, roll etc... Fig. 1 PSS is 7000 XXXX (27 μ") down to the ABS. Compared to White concept 2, the PSS surrounds ABS including loading and trailing edges. Then we can play with many parameters: ABS shape, PSS step height, PSS area etc...ABS and PSS are fabricated full water using reactive ion etching.

articleTitle: Dynamics of magnetic domain wall and bloch line motion using 3D simulations
abstract: The dynamics of a magnetic domain wall containing vertical Bloch lines (VBL) has been numerically investigated. The wall is the kind found in thin film materials with a large anisotropy perpendicular to the plane of the film. The VBL's are all of the same chirality and are periodically repeated along the wall. The wall is driven by an applied field perpendicular to the film plane and the VBL’s are gyrotropically driven by wall motion. This simulation was performed for a wide range of applied fields. At all fields, both the wall and the VBLs distort from their equilibrium shape and finally attain a constant velicity. As show below, neither the wall velocity or the VBL velocity is a linear function of the respective drive so that the ratio of VBL velocity to wall velocity decreases, presumably, because of the observed distortion. For an applied field extrapolated to zero, the ratio agrees with the value predicted by the analytical rigid wall model. We will show the dynamic distortion by observing contours of the magnetization in-plane angle for various applied fields, the wall velocity as a function of field, the VBL velocity as a function of wall velocity and the various energies of the moving wall as a function of field.

articleTitle: Frequency dependence of the FMR linewidth in single crystal barium ferrite platelets
New design of current access bubble memory device
abstract: Current access memories are characterized by high speed, simple assembly and may be alternative to field access memories. Earlier it was shown that there are some problems in these devices, which should be overcome. In this paper a new design of current access magnetic bubble memory, based on combination of two-conductor meander in the input-output domain channel with three layer perforated informational array.

articleTitle: A self-cascaded induction generator system with DC chopper, PWM inverter and LPF
abstract: Since the oil shock of the 1970's, induction generators have been regarded as energy-saving, small scale energy-producing devices. In this paper we deal with a induction generator system for energy-producing devices. In this paper describes analytical and experimental studies of self-cascaded induction generator system. This generator system have the self-cascaded induction machine for the generator, and Rectifier, DC Chopper, PWM Inverter, and LPF (low path filter) for the Frequency converter.

articleTitle: Activation volumes of reversal in Tb-Fe-Co thin films
abstract: The first generation of magneto-optic (M-O) data storage systems use rare earth - transition metal (RE-TM) alloys as the storage media. The materials typically used are Tb - Fe/Co thin film alloys protected by passivating dielectric layers on either side of the M-O layer. In this paper we present measurements of the activation volumes of reversal in such materials, obtained from magnetic time dependence measurements. Activation volumes are of interest as they set the fundamental limits to the maximum storage density obtainable from any media, being the volume of material that nucleates the generation of a reversed domain. The wavelength of laser light available and the quality of optical systems currently set the technological limits of storage density.

articleTitle: Microstructural origin of the magnetic degraded layer in sendust metal-in-gap recording heads
abstract: A magnetic degraded layer at the interface between the Sendust film and the ferrite core Often forms in Sendust metal-In-gap heads, which gives rise to undesired secondary output in playback spectra. Mechanisms proposed to explain the origin of the magnetic degraded layer can generally be divided into two categories: one which attributes it to the formation of AI and Si oxides at the interface due to oxygen diffusion caused by the high temperature manufacturing process, and the other which attributes it to the initial Sendust metal film layer with poor magnetic properties. However, both mechanisms fail to explain the dependence of the secondary output on crystallographic orientations of single crystal ferrite cores. We report results from studies of Sendust films on ferrite cores using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). A mechanism will be proposed to explain the microstructural origin of the magnetic degraded layer.

articleTitle: Numerical solutions of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation for microwave solitons in magnetic thin films
abstract: Nonlinear dipole-exchange spin wave pulses in single crystal yttrium-iron-garnet (YIG) thin films are observed to have soliton characteristics which can be modeled by the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE). In this work, a detailed study of the numerical solutions for the NLSE has been done to better understand the profiles of such nonlinear waves in magnetic thin films.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of electromagnetic system in magnetically levitated vehicle, KOMAG-01
abstract: An electromagnetically levitated vehicle, KOMAG-01, has been developed with 8 axial flux type electromagnets for levitation and 2 single-sided linear induction motors (SLIM) for propulsion. The magnet is designed using analytical calculation and analysed by Finite Element Method to find out an optimum configuration. The SLM is also analysed using a 2-D FEM with current and magnetic vector potential to investigate end/edge effects in 3 different analysing planes.

articleTitle: Surface power distribution in cross field heating of thin nonmagnetic plates
abstract: Cross field heating is widely used in metal industry for heating of thin plates. In these systems the distribution of induced currents over the surface of the plate or the workpiece is of interest because it determines the distribution of heat over its surface. This is a three dimensional problem. Existing methods for three dimensional problems need large computer memories and are very time consuming. In the absence of boundary conditions, use of methods based on the differential equations requires that the field equations need be solved both in the region of the workpiece as well in the region outside the workpiece. In integral equation methods the field equations need be solved only in the region of interest. In this paper we use a circuit approach to obtain the induced current density and the power.

articleTitle: Influence of crystallite size and shape on the viscous magnetization of /spl gamma/-Fe/sub 2/O/sub 3/ particles
Longitudinal and perpendicular Matteucci effects of amorphous wires
abstract: The Matteucci effect (found by Matteucci in 1847) is originally a phenomenon of induction of a pluse-shape ac voltage which is generated between both ends of a torsional-stressed magnetostrictive bar magnetized with a longitudinal ac magnetic field. This unique electro-magnetic effect has not connected to any engineering applications up to now due to its low sensitivity in crystalline bars. The Matteucci voltage e <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</sub> is simply expressed in the equation of e <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</sub> = -d ϕ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</sub>/d t, where ϕ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</sub> shows a circular flux in the specimen considering the Maxwell equation of rot E = - ∂B/∂t. Therefore, any magnetizing methods giving rise to d ϕ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</sub> /d t are valid to utilize the Matteucci effect. From this point of view, we found a sensitive perpendicular Matteucci effect in negative magnetostrictive amorphous wires having circular magnetic anisotropy and constituted a new data tablet as an inputting apparatus of hand-written characters and figures for personal computers (Pen- PC). In this paper, mechanisms of the longitudinal and perpendicular Matteucci effects in various amorphous wires are investigated using a BH measuring circuit.

articleTitle: Overlapping finite elements for problems with movement
abstract: It is often not easy to match two different meshes, especially for the problems with movement. Good quality of a mesh may be hard to maintain, fixed displacement of the rotor may be required, or filled nonsymmetric and even singular stiffness matrices may be obtained. The proposed finite element model allows overlapped elements and thus avoids geometric matching of two meshes. The rotor and stator meshes of an electric machine can be generated independently and may overlap in the airgap.

articleTitle: Nonlinear distortion in helical-scan tape recorders
abstract: Parallel channel recording with single channel data rate of at least 150 Mbps is required in digital HDTV and high performance data recorders. Linear densities of these recorders usually lie between 60 and 100 kbpi. Previous studies indicate that nonlinear distortion is dominated by transition shifts arising from one and two bit interactions in thin film disk recording using a thin film head. Our investigation is focused on metal particle tape recording which is characterized by a finite recording depth and a non-uniform transition depth profile. We found that the distortion at high linear densities is mostly transition sharpening as well as transition shift from one bit interaction.

articleTitle: Variations in strain amplitude and phase ina a cylindrical specimen of Tb/sub 0.3/Dy/sub 0.7/Fe/sub 1.95/ in an AC magnetic field
abstract: In recent work it has been shown that the alloy Tb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</sub> Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.95</sub> has very high differential magnetostriction dλ / dH [1], and that this property can be utilized for the development of an AC magnetometer for detecting magnetic field strengths down to the range of a few tenths of an A/m [2,3]. It was also found that the surface deformation of a disk or cylinder of this material did not give rise to a uniform displacement across the surface of the disk. The present paper explores in detail the surface displacements of a [112] orientated disk of Tb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</sub> Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.95</sub> resulting from an alternating magnetic field applied normal to the plane of the disk.

articleTitle: Eddy currents and displacement currents in multi-layer soft magnetic films for recording heads
abstract: Eddy current loss has become a significant problem in the development of soft magnetic films as the signal frequency has become higher. In thick soft magnetic films, it has been proposed that layering of the film reduces the eddy current loss. However, there was a hypothesis that displacement current flows through the insulator such as a capacitor sandwiched by two metal films and that multi-layered films are not so efficient at a high frequency. By using a 3D-FEM (Finite Element Method), we found that the displacement current is smaller than the eddy current by a factor of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> for 0.5 μm thick insulator. In this study the insulator thickness was changed from 0.05μm to 1μm and the effects of pin holes and the passage of eddy currents through metal on the edge of insulator was investigated precisely. The computation results was confirmed by using large scale models.

articleTitle: Profile analysis of magnetic encoders
abstract: Magnetic encoders have been widely used for controlling the position and speed of a brushless motor. The speed fluctuation of a motor can be measured and compensated by using a magnetic encoder with pulse-width-modulation. The purpose of our research is to investigate the effect of pole pitch on the magnetic field distribution of magnetic encoders.

articleTitle: MÖssbauer effect study of ordering behaviors for Fe-Al-Si and Fe-Al-Si-Ni magnetic thin films
abstract: Recently, the development of magnetic thin films having not only excellent soft magnetic properties at high frequencies but also sufficient saturation magnetic flux densities are hastened for recording-head materials of MIG (Metal in Gap) type. In this paper, we prepared Fe-AI-Si sendust films which have been widely used for head materials and Fe-AI-Si-Ni supersendust films which have high potential for new head materials by a sputtering method and examined the structural changes in these films due to the annealing with a conversion electron Mossbauer spectroscopy (CEMS). Furthermore, we clarified the differences in ordering behaviors between Fe-AI-Si and Fe-AI-Si-Ni films.

articleTitle: Collisions of VBL clusters
abstract: Vertical Bloch lines separate regions of domain wall of ferromagnets in which magnetization rotates in opposite directions. The domain wall and VBL are topological solitons or kinks. But its behavior is very different. After collision of two neighboring domain wall it is possible obtain only collapse the domain between them. The annihilation kink-antikink process is possible in this cast. After collision of two VBL clusters in domain wall garnet film with perpendicular anisotropy it is possible obtain many different results including complete and partial restoration of colliding VBL clusters and its annihilation. For this investigations it is elaborated methods of triple high-speed photography. Two possibility of this methods are shown on fig. 1 and fig. 2. On fig. 1 the region traversed by the domain wall with VBL clusters moving along it during time interval between first and triple laser pulses is dark band. Inside this band it is possible to see DW in phase contrast. Fig. 2 represents three position moving DW with VBL clusters moving along it in phase contrast. The solitary flexural waves of asymmetric profile, which accompany the VBL cluster move along D W. From the distances between the first and second positions of the VBL clusters one can determine their velocities before collision. From the distances between the second and third positions - the velocity after collision. The decrease in the amplitude of solitary flexural wave and increase its velocities after collision are clear noticeable on fig.1. The time evolution of the positions of moving VBL clusters is represent on fig. 3 for a DW velocity of 17 m/s. Fig. 3 shows the phase shift in the course of collision. Before the collision the velocity of each of the colliding clusters was 30 m/s, after collision 45 m/s. At the domain wall velocity below 17 m/s one observe an annihilation at higher velocities - a complete restoration of the clusters.

articleTitle: Comparison of rotational power loss in non-oriented 6.5% silicon iron with other sheet materials at power frequency
abstract: Rotational power loss in electrical machines is a major cause of energy loss. Recently Nippon Steel Corporation has developed a non-oriented 6.5% silicon steel with very low A.C. losses which is a strong candidate for use in energy efficient machines. Rotational losses in thin gauge 6.5% silicon iron tape have been measured previously but data was limited and difficult to compare with competing materials. This paper compares the rotational losses of the new material with those occurring in existing materials and relates its magnitude to the A.C. losses and degree of anisotropy of the materials. Strips of material 170mmx70mm, 0.1mm thick were magnetised in a computer controlled magnetisation system and the losses were measured with the aid of orthogonal B and H coils, a four channel data acquisition system and analysing software mounted on an IBM P.C. The apparatus, previously described, was capable of measuring losses under controlled magnetisation conditions with an error of less than ±2%.

articleTitle: A high output mode for submicron M-R memory cells
abstract: Two new discoveries allow a two to three times increase in outputs of M-R elements and allows small cells to be made with the current material with a nominal anisotropy constant of 20 Oe. First, a new operating mode has been demonstrated in which the information is stored by the direction of the edge magnetization and the body of the element serves as the sensor. Secondly, a technique has been developed by which a demagnetizing field in the long dimension of the element can be tailored to give the required effective anisotropy needed for proper operation of very small elements. With these techniques submicron dimensioned cell can be made in which the read access time is not compromised.

articleTitle: A methoc of computing electro-mechanical transfer functions for magnetorestrictive functional units
abstract: In a magnetostrictive device the active material is magnetized by a current in a driving coil. During magnetization ohmic losses and flux leakage occur in the coil system. The influence of losses and flux leakage on the performance is of special interest when the magnetostrictive device is to be adopted into an external system. An earlier developed model for magnetostrictive rods gives together with a mathematical formulation of the electric and magnetic circuits an opportunity to compute electro-mechanical transfer functions for magnetostrictive functional units.

articleTitle: Surface induced magnetic and magneto-optical properties in amorphous Ni/sub x/Y/sub 1-x/ films
abstract: Recently, some experimental magneto-optic properties on Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub> amorphous films were reported. This paper is a continuation of our earlier study. Films were prepared by sputtering onto substrates held at room temperature. The concentration range investigated is 0.60≤x≤0.91. Magneto-optic measurements were performed in both film/air (f/a) and glass/film (g/f) interfaces for both as prepared and air annealed (373K, 8h 30m) Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub> amorphous films (Table 1). The dependence of the magneto-optical properties upon the concentration was studied using two compositions Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.95</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</sub> and N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.91</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.09</sub>. Evidence of the existence of two magnetic phases in Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.91</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.09</sub> amorphous films air annealed was obtained from transverse initial magneto-optic Kerr effect at room temperature. Here we discuss the physical origin of this behaviour. In figures 1, 2, 3 we show χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x/2</sub> vs. H curves for Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.91</sub> Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.09</sub> and air annealed. The occurrence of the downwards curvature of χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> in the range of low magnetic fields, together with the multiple minima in χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x/2</sub> (regions A,B), can be explained by two magnetic phases weakly coupled. The two regions shows two different H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">κ</sub> and δ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">κ values. (δ<sub>κ</sub> : transverse Kerr effect parameter related with the magnetization).</sub>

articleTitle: Comparison of power supplied for magnet load applications
abstract: The performance of power supplies used in magnet load applications is compared in this paper. Load output specifications and requirements are described. Conventional linear and phase-controlled power supplies are discussed, and a new type of magnet power supplies (switchmode) is introduced. Their advantages and disadvantages are evaluated. In high-energy physics research and medical institutions, power supplies are used to drive magnets of accelerators for particle beam excitation and control. In order to accurately control particle beam positions and energy levels, magnet power supplies often require to provide load regulation with extremely low current ripple and fast response speed. A typical output current ripple specification ranges from several ppm to several hundred ppm, while the control loop bandwidth is in the region of several kilohertz. Traditionally, linear and phase-controlled power supplies have been used for this type of applications.

articleTitle: A study of push-pull parametric transformer
abstract: The parametric transformer is expected as a power stabilizer because the transformer exhibits various desirable features including voltage regulation, noise rejection and overload protection. However, the parametric transformer had a problem of distortion of its input current. In this paper, the authors present a method for improvement of the problem and propose a new application of the parametric transformer to a power supply for suppressing the harmonic currents produced by nonlinear loads.

articleTitle: Observation technique and formation mechanism of columnar microstructure in TbFeCo films
abstract: The crystalline and amorphous films produced by vapour deposition commonly exibit approximately parallel columnar microstructure regions, there is few situations in homogeneous glass state like SIO2. The columnar microstructure has long been known in crystalline films and semiconductor materials, but it has been only discoveried in amorphous metallic thin films in 1977, this partially due to that the research and development of amorphous materials is later then crystalline materials. On the other hand the structure dimension (about 200 A) in amorphous materials is less than that in crystalline materials, which makes the observation more difficulty. Magneto-optical recording media demands to have excellent perpendicular anisotropy to form stable recording domain, this is to say, Q=Ku/2 Ms > 1. Because the columnar microstructure in RE-TM films affects the anisotropy and diffusion of oxygen a great deal of work in observation technique has been carried out. It is noticeable that the formation mechanism has never been directly verified by TEM or other methods. The understanding of the physical origin of column formation is limited to computer simulation.

articleTitle: Structural origins of magnetic anisotropy in amorphous Fe-Tb films and multilayers
abstract: Many amorphous rare earth - transition metal (RE-TM) alloy films exhibit magnetic anisotropy favoring the direction perpendicular to the film plane. This phenomenon makes these alloys useful for magneto-optical applications and potentially important for perpendicular recording applications. Although perpendicular magnetic anisotropy was first observed in Co-Gd alloys nearly two decades ago by Chaudhari, Cuomo, and Gambino the origins remain unclear. Several theories have been applied to explain this phenomenon, including pair-ordering anisotropy, bond-orientational anisotropy, surface dipole effects, and film morphology, however, little experimental evidence has been provided to support any one theory.

articleTitle: Noise in thin-film inductive heads
Effect of relative humidity on friction behavior of the head/disk interface
abstract: The effect of humidity on tribological behavior of the head/disk interface has received considerable attention in merit years as smoother surfaces are required to obtain ultra high recording densities at a ultra low flying height. The effect of relative humidity depends on a lot of factors such as surface roughness, lubricant thickness, water thickness, head materials and so on. The purpose of this paper is to make an effort to correlate water adsorption data on both head and disk surfaces with frictional behavior at the head/disk interface. Glass disks with carbon overcoating were used for this study. Surface roughness of the disks is about 35Å peak-to-valley. Alumina titanium carbide was used as slider materials with surface roughness of about 80Å peak-to-valley. Thickness of adsorbed water was measured using an ellipsometer. A friction apparatus was placed in a humidity-controlled chamber. At each controlled relative humidity, the head was in contact with the disk for about twenty minutes before testing.

articleTitle: Infrared Kerr rotation and magnetic properties of amorphous U-Sb films
abstract: Thin films of amorphous U-Sb have been prepared by magnetron sputtering by sequentially depositing layers of U (1.8 Å) and Sb (6.7 Å) at sputtering rates of 3.5 and 6.7 Å/s, respectively, to give a total thickness of 3000 Å. As previously reported, these films show large Hall effect and magneto-optical effects. We extended the photon energy range of the polar Kerr measurement down to 0.65 eV, in order to get more information on the U5f→6d transition. The resulting polar Kerr spectra for an amorphous U-Sb film with 43 at. % U are shown in Fig. 1 for the remanence state and in a field of 3 T. An increase of the negative Kerr rotation toward lower photon energies is clearly visible. This is a different result than in amorphous U-As where the Kerr rotation peaks in the vicinity of 1 eV due to an U5f→6d transition. The Kerr rotation of U-Sb looks in fact more like the Kerr spectra observed in the crystalline compounds U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> and U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> which crystallize in the Th<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> structure. These spectra are dominated by spin-polarized charge carrier behavior rather than by an U5f→6d interband transition.

articleTitle: Coaxial railgun experiment results
abstract: Electromagnetic launchers are attractive to the defense community because they have the capability to impart projectile velocities which are higher (in excess of 3 kilometers per second) than can be obtained with conventional cannon systems. This technology has only recently been considered for earth-to-space and space-ID-space launch applications in support of scientific and commercial space pograms. This paper describes the experimental test results of a coaxial railgun, and elaborates on the interior electromagnetic and ballistics environment imposed upon a small space probe launched from a large-scale coaxial railgun in space.

articleTitle: Magnetomechanical properties of single crystal Tb/sub x/Dy/sub 1-x/ under compressive stress
abstract: Large magnetostriction/anisotropy ratios (λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">γ,2</sup>K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>) have been recently found in Tb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub> alloys (0<x<1) for temperatures below ˜150 K. In this paper we report the magnetomechanical properties (permeability, piezomagnetic d-constant, and compliance) of the anisotropy compensating alloys (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> ≡ 0) near 77 K. A-axis and b-axis single crystal rods (˜3.1 cm long x ˜0.65 cm x -0.6 cm) for x = .5 and x = .6 were prepared by strain annealing techniques. Magnetization, strain vs magnetic field, and elastic modulus measurements were made by conventional inductive and strain gage methods on a specially designed apparatus which subjects the sample to fixed compressive stresses up to 18 MPa. Representative magnetization and magnetostriction curves are shown in Figs. 1 and 2, Magnetomechanical properties are given in Tables I and II. Particularly interesting are the huge strains and the large mechanical work done at relatively low applied magnetic fields. In these alloys, both λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">γ,2</sup> and the saturation, M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>, are large. Figs. 1 and 2 contrast the magnetic behavior for K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> ≡ 0 (x = 0.6) and for K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> ≡ 7 kOe (x = 0.5). In Fig. 1, the easy direction is perpendicular to the rod axis. Discontinuities in the magnetization and in λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> γ,2</sup> are observed as the magnetic moments change from the perpendicular easy direction to the easy direction 30° from the rod axis. Small triggering fields yield large magnetization "jumps". As the magnetic field is increased further, slow magnetic rotation to the hard b (rod) axis occurs. The sample shown in Fig. 2 is nearly magnetically isotropic. Here the full λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">γ,2</sup> (6.3 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>) is attained by a 90° magnetization rotation process.

articleTitle: The inductance calculation of magnetic rods by using complementary finite element methods
abstract: The finite element method is widely used for the magnetic field calculations of magnetic circuits, but it is difficult to evaluate the calculation errors for the models which are not known the exact solutions. In this paper, the inductance calculation method of magnetic rods by using complementary finite element methods is proposed to obtain good solution. The upper bound and the lower bound for the inductance of ellipsoid magnetic rod are calculated by using the calculation method, and presented the exact solution exists in the middle of the upper bound and the lower bound.

articleTitle: Media noise improvement through head-disk spacing reduction
abstract: Improvements in the noise performance of heads, disks, and channels have allowed the demonstration of recording densities greater than l Gbit/in<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The use of low noise thin-film media, low noise magnetoresistive (MR) heads, and very low flying heights is critical to achieve the required error rate performance.
