Reducing the flying height improves signal strength at high linear densities by shortening the transition length and miminizing the spacing loss. What is less clear as the head-disk spacing is reduced is the behavior of the media noise. Belk et al examined media noise as a function of write separation with a constant read separation and noted that the noise maximum moved to lower linear densities with increasing head-disk separation. We have measured media noise as a function of head-disk separation on disks prepared with different overcoat spacer layers and compared the results to theoretical calculations.

articleTitle: Magnetoelasticity for large stresses
abstract: Recent interest in the theory and modeling of magnetoelastic processes has drawn upon the Preisach model of hysteresis and the anhysteretic model. We have extended our past work with the differential susceptibility model to stresses much larger than residual stress, reaching the local anhysteretic curve and the Villari reversal. Progress in this nonlinear differential magnetoelastic theory arises from the concept of local demagnetization, that is positive and negative stress-sensitive domain walls and stress-insensitive walls are attributed average local magnetization, M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub>, rather than global magnetization, an experimentally determined nonlinear demagnetization factor, D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>, that replaces a function by Spano, and an improved approach to modeling hysteresis.

articleTitle: Magnetic imaging based on tunneling-stabilized, scanned-probe microscopies
abstract: We have modified the scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) method to do magnetic force microscopy (MFM) using a compliant, magnetic tunneling tip in place of the usual rigid STM tip. This method, referred to as tunneling-stabilized, magnetic force microscopy or TSMFM, is different from conventional MFM based on atomic-force-microscopy (AFM). Conventional MFM employs a displacement detector to measure the motion of the magnetic cantilever (see Fig. 1). TSMFM, on the other hand, operates in the usual STM sense with a flexible tunneling tip. This means that the TSMFM images show magnetic forces on the tip as well as topography. TSMFM images compare favorably with conventional MFM images as well as other types of magnetic imaging techniques including Bitter patterns, Lorentz microscopy, electron holography, or scanning electron microscopy with polarization analysis (SEMPA). Depending on the instrumentation, these methods can resolve magnetic features with sub-micrometer resolution, whereas methods based on STM or AFM have resolutions as good as 20 nm with the prospect of breaking the nanometer barrier.

articleTitle: Hexafferite tape casting and hyperfrequency characteristics
abstract: The tape casting technic were used to realize an hyperfrequency absorbing screen with continuous change in characteristics. Different hexaferrite compositions were stacked and co-sintered.

articleTitle: Viterbi detection of matched spectral null codes for PR4 channels
abstract: Partial response systems [1] have the potential for increasing the storage density of magnetic recording systems employing Viterbi detection [2]. Class-IV partial response (PR4) is an appropriate target for magnetic channels at moderate densities. In [3], it is shown that use of a modulation code which has spectral nulls matching the nulls of the channel transfer polynomial can result in significant coding gains over the baseline partial response channel. In this study, the performance of three Dc and Nyquist free codes for the PR4 channel is determined by simulation. The three codes under consideration are all of rate 3/4, and are contained in [3][4][5]. Baseline channel performance is established using interleaved detectors for the PR4 channel. The channel is modeled as an ideal PR4 channel corrupted by colored noise, as would be produced by a zero forcing equalizer applied to a Lorentzian channel at various values of S = pw<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub>/T. In Figure 1, the injected noise spectrum is shown as a function of normalized frequency for various values of S. In Figure 2, theoretical curves are shown for the byte error rates of the baseline and matched spectral null detectors of ideal PR4 with white noise, while simulated byte error rates are shown as scatter points for various values of S, for the code of [3]. Generally, these codes are employed in systems with an outer error correcting code operating on decoded bytes. As an alternative to the detector of [3], an enhanced baseline detector which flags detected code violations for erasure correction in a Reed Solomon code is considered. In Figure 3, a theoretical curve is shown for the ratio of undetectable to detectable errors for ideal PR4 with white noise, while simulated ratios of undetected byte errors to detected byte errors are shown as scatter points for various values of S for the code of [5].

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of amorphous films of Bi/sub 2/O/sub 3/-Fe/sub 2/O/sub 3/-Fe/sub 2/O/sub 3/-CaO
abstract: Amorphous samples of Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> - Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-MO, where M is a divalent ion such as Zn, Cu, and Ca, are reported to show a spontaneous magnetic moment at room temperature. Techniques including rapid quenching and rf sputtering are used for the preparation of such magnetically ordered amorphous compounds. One observes a ferromagnetic character in as-quenched samples whereas high temperature annealing is essential for the onset of a long range magnetic order in rf sputtered film. This study is concerned with the magnetic characterization of annealed amorphous compounds of (Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>)0.5 – x (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>)0.5 (CaO)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> prepared by the rf sputtering technique.

articleTitle: A new algorithm for calculating HVDC corona in the presence of wind
abstract: A new algorithm for calculating HVDC corona based on Boundary Element Method (BEM) is presented. The new algorithm takes a different approach to the process of updating the space charge density during the iteration. The iteration process is convergent even for a uniform initial space charge distribution. It takes into account the effect of wind.

articleTitle: Magnetic and magneto-otpical properties of Ca-doped Bi-YiG sputtered films
abstract: Bismuth substituted iron garnet (Bi-YIG) is very attractive material for magneto-optical media and has been applied in magneto-optical devices working in the infrared wavelength region. However, in the visible wavelength region, Bi-YIG shows large absorption because of Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>, then the figure of merit is considerably smaller than that in the infrared wavelength region. We have investigated Ca-doped Bi-YIG to improve the optical absorption in this system for the use in the visible wavelength region. In this paper, we describe annealing properties of highly Ca-doped Bi-YIG sputtered films. The films are examined with regard to microstructural, magnetic and optical characteristics.

articleTitle: A detailed study of the environmental stability of metal particle tapes
abstract: The overall stability of metal particle (MP) tape media is the sum of synergistic contributions of the metal particles, binder system, and the substrate used in the tape fabrication. The components used will dictate the stability of the various physical, magnetic, mechanical, and chemical properties of the tape. This study was undertaken to examine selected properties of MP tapes as a function of accelerated aging and the results obtained are summarized in this paper.

articleTitle: Avoiding surface impedance modification in be methods by singularity-free representations
abstract: The minimum-order boundary element method for conducting media makes use of surface impedance to represent eddy current effects. It has teen shown that in two-dimensional problems and for the TM situation in three-dimensional problems, the surface impedance is modified near edges and comers and an expression which significantly improves computed field distributions has been derived for 90° corners.

articleTitle: Nonlinear theory for polar kerr effect in ferromagnetics
abstract: It has been proven that, in ferromagnetics, magneto-optical effects stem not only from the splitting of the excited state resulting from L-S interaction but also from the splitting of the ground state caused by the exchange interaction and applied field. In this paper, on the basis of this theory. further calculations have shown that the polar Kerr effect is not completely unreciprocal. In normal temperature regime, the polar Kerr rotation θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> has a complicate nonlinear dependence un magnetization M and temperature T.

articleTitle: An improved technique of impedance measurement for thin film inductors over 10MHz
abstract: Thin film inductor is one of the key element to develop small distributed power supplies and intelligent sensors over 10MHz. We need a new technique to measure the impedance of the inductors because their feature is different from that of the conventional bulk inductors; Thin film inductors have flat and small profile without any copper wiring and they are used at very high frequency. We have already proposed to measure the impedance of thin film inductors from reflection coefficient by using microstrip line. However, its accuracy has not been discussed in detail especially over 100MHz where the measured impedance can he influenced by impedance matching, undesirable signal reflection, and etc. In this paper we examined both the mismatch of the characteristic impedance and the error of the electrical length. Furthermore we discuss the frequency characteristics of the inductor up to 1.3GHz based on the improved measurement.

articleTitle: The high Bs sputtered amorphous MIG head with a minimized contour effect
The effect of track width and topography on composition uniformity of electroplated permalloy in thin film heads
abstract: Thin Film recording heads are fabricated either by "dry" process, or " wet " process. In the dry process, sputtering and ion etching are used. In the case of wet processing, a combination of dry process, phololithography patterning and electrochemical deposition are employed. For most manufacturers, Permalloy layers in the thin film inductive heads are deposited by electroplating. The composition uniformity of the Permalloy over the flat and stepped portion of the head plays an important role in the read/write characteristics and magnetic performance of thin film heads. To increase magnetic recording density, one requires the reduction or the track width or a magnetic head. How narrow one can plate Permalloy and still obtain uniform composition? In this paper we have studied the composition variation or the electroplated Permalloy films with electron microprobe, (EPMA/WDS). The electroplating was carried out in the system similar to the one described in reference 6. The composition variation of the upper magnetic layer from pole tip to yoke was studied as a function of both track width and topography. The track width was varied from 5 to 26 microns and the topography was varied up to 20 microns. Keeping the topography constant at 17 microns and varying the pole tip track width of plated Permalloy from 6 to 26 microns, the apparent composition difference between pole lip and yoke decreased from 1% to 0.4%.

articleTitle: Development of a new sub-sub micron flying ramp loading head with emphasis on slider roll control capability
abstract: Much smaller flying height of the air bearing slider is a strong requirement for higher areal recording in magnetic disk drives. However, ultra-smooth finish of the disk surface attempting lower flying height often causes head/medium stiction, so surface roughness control is a critical issue for higher recording density limitations. This paper proposes a new head/medium interface mechanism, which puts into practical use ulna-smooth, no-textured disks. The newly developed ramp loading head shows excellent reliability in recording interface suitable for sub-sub micron head/medium spacing.

articleTitle: Poincare sphere interpretation of Kerr-effect measurements by using a photoelastic modulator
abstract: There is a growing popularity in the use of photoelastic modulators (PEM’s) to measure Kerr loops of magnetic materials. This technique offers several advantages over the other main method, differential detection with a Wollaston prism, but is somewhat obscure in terms of visualizing how the measure signal actually appears. The Poincare sphere has proved useful in interpreting many polarimetric experiments, but has not seen applied in the recent poliferation of PEM-based detection. In this talk, I describe a highly visual application of the Poincare sphere to magneto-optic detection with a PEM that clarifies how such a large modulation can yield a sensitive measure of an extremely small change in polarization. A computer program is demonstrated that provides a graphical view of the polarization modulation on the Poincare sphere in time, showing direct agreement with the output from a detector used in a magneto-optic experiment.

articleTitle: Dynamic field distribution of thin film inductive heads
abstract: Magnetic poles used in thin film inductive disc drive heads have a complex structure. It is therefore very difficult to recognize the actual field distributions. However, precise understanding of the field profiles, especially in high frequency regions, is very important for designing high density and high speed data storage systems. In this study, dynamic field distributions of thin film heads were investigated using electron beam tomography. Their relation to the pole materials and configurations are discussed.

articleTitle: High-speed and high-thrust linear induction motor designed by using Eigenvalue analysis method
abstract: The purpose of the investigation to be described was to examine the effectiveness of the novel design technique (called EVA method) for electromagnetic force maximization problem. EVA, an acronym for Eigenvalue Analysis, is a new approach to elucidate the essential characteristics of an electromagnetic apparatus. In the researchers on linear induction motor, for example, it has become a common brief that there hardly exists a direct way to prevent entry-end and exit-end effect. However, the EVA method has possibility to give a practical and effective solution to this problem. The present work reveals for the first time the improvement simulation of thrust characteristics of acutual high-speed linear induction motor.

articleTitle: 3D eddy current analysis by the hybrid Fe-Be method using magnetic field intensity H
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to provide a useful method for numerical calculation of the 3D eddy current problem with open boundary. The finite element method (FEM) and the boundary element method (BEM), which have entirely different features from each other, are useful for numerical analysis. In this paper we describe the hybrid finite element and boundary element method, and adopt the magnetic field intensity H as much as possible as the physical quantity. The conductive region is analyzed by the FEM, on the other hand, the free space having a supply current in it by the BEM. We also propose a new boundary element discretization scheme in H formulation, which makes it entirely easy to couple the BE region with the FE region by introducing the edge element. Some numerical results obtained by the proposed method are compared with measured ones.

articleTitle: Reciprocity in computer simulation of magnetic reproduction process
abstract: Conventionally the reciprocity is widely used for calculation of reproduced output in the magnetic recording theory. On the other hand, we have performed the reproduction simulation taking the head-medium magnetic interaction into account by the magnetic recording simulation program based upon FEM and the curling magnetization reversal model. In this paper, the reproduced voltage waveform and amplitude calculated by the reciprocity will be compared with those obtained by the simulation and validity of the reciprocity will be discussed.

articleTitle: Size effects of switching fields of thin permalloy particles
abstract: Measurements of hysteresis loops were performed on thin permalloy rectangular platelets with various dimensions prepared by nanolithography. The particle coecivity, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, exhibits a sensitive size dependence. The measured H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> are compared with micromagnetic predictions utilizing two-dimensional models without magnetization variation through the thickness. Excellent overall agreement is found, indicating that a simplified two-dimensional approach is sufficient for characterizing reversal mechanisms for particles with thicknesses smaller than or comparable to the exchange length.

articleTitle: Investigation of the torque calculation of a DC PM motor
Side reading study of recording heads
abstract: The side reading of recording heads from adjacent tracks becomes increasingly important in high track-density environments. Often trackwidths are reduced without properly sealing head geometries and written transition spacings. The resultant side reading can increase the noise-to-signal ratio, thus degrading the error-rate performance. Traditionally, track profiles have been used to evaluate the side reading behavior of ferrite heads, thin-film inductive (TFI) and magnetoresistive (MR) heads, where the fundamental frequency component of the readback signal was measured in the frequency domain and plotted against the offtrack displacement. In this work. a time-domain method for characterizing the side reading of various recording heads is described. It provides information such as the side-reading amplitude and its data-pattern dependence as well as readback-signal distortions. not obtainable from frequency domain measurements. The results on MlG, TFI and shielded MR heads will be presented.

articleTitle: Extraction magnetometry in an SC susceptometer
abstract: Our efforts over the last several years have been focused primarily on ac susceptibility and the development of cryogenic ac susceptometers. However, the study of the magnetic properties of materials often requires the capability to perform both ac and dc measurements. The strong scientific interest shown in performing both of these measurements led to efforts for incorporating a dc moment measurement scheme into an ac susceptometer. The goal was to develop a dc capability which could be simply implemented, which could provide sensitivity adequate for most measurement needs, and me which would not sacrifice any of the performance characteristics of the ac measurement.

articleTitle: Thin-film media with a radial composition gradient and dual-layer structure
abstract: The capacity of rigid-disk file can be increased considerably using the technology of zone recording to achieve same linear density at inner and outer diameters of the disk. This results in a lower signal output at the inner diameter region (ID) because of small linear velocity, whereas overwrite (OW) performance tends to suffer at the outer diameter region (OD) because head is flying higher due to the greater velocity at OD. The greater flying height at OD reduces the ability of the head flux to saturate the medium and thus degrades the OW Unfortunately, a reduction of intergranular magnetic coupling, which is necessary for better noise performance, inevitably leads to a drop in S* value. One consequence of reduced S* of low-noise media is the degradation in OW. To overcome this fundamental difficulty and achieve a simultaneous improvement in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at ID and overwrite at OD, a scheme of sputtering using a composite target was proposed and preliminary results are reponed here.

articleTitle: Magnetic ferromagnetic resonance and MÖssbauer study of Zr-substituted Li-Zn-Cu-Ti ferrite system
abstract: Owing to the applications of radar, remote-sensing and satellite- communication in new and high techniques, it is required that the gyromagnetic materials might satisfy the requirements in performance in various frequency bands and understand the mechanism of frequency dependence of gyromagnetic properties. On the basis of rather systematic investigation of the effect of ion substitution on the magnetic properties and ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) in 3 cm band of Li ferrite system in past, it has been found that the Li-Mg ferrite systems with better gyromagnetic characters have been obtained, and small amount of Cu ion-substitution may reduce the porosity and FMR line-width, and on the consideration that Zr ion-substitution may reduce the magnetocrystalline anisotropy in rare-earth iron garnets. The effect of substitution of Zr for Ti in Li-Zn-Ti-Cu spinel system on the magnetic properties and FMR was studied in this paper.

articleTitle: Modified viterbi algorithm for a jitter-dominant 1-D/sup 2/ channel
abstract: As transitions are packed closer at high recording densities, transition noise becomes significant, and the detection performance of the Viterbi algorithm (VA) is substantially degraded. The random jitter of the written transition position is an important contribution to the transition noise. Because of its data-dependency, jitter cannot be modeled as an additive noise. In this paper, we propose a practical detection scheme based on the maximum likelihood (ML) criterion under the assumption of Gaussian jitter. This detection scheme is very similar to the VA except that a modified branch error metric is used to incorporate the data-dependent nature of jitter noise. Error rate simulations are performed for channels dominated by either Gaussian jitter or truncated Gaussian jitter. The results show that the proposed detection scheme yields lower error rates than the VA.

articleTitle: Electron holography of magnetic microstructures
abstract: The phase shift of an electron wave relative to a reference wave assumed to proceed through field free space is given by δ φ = e (V . t – Φ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>)/ ħ where V is the electrostatic potential, t the transit time of the electrons through the field and Φ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> is the magnetic flux enclosed between the object wave and the reference wave. δ φ can readily be measured by means of electron interferometry and holography (Fig. 2). In a hologram the phase shift δ φ is recorded as a corresponding displacement of the interference fringes whereas an amplitude modulation leads to a modulation of the fringe contrast (Fig. 3). Using an Elmiskop IA we built a specially designed electron microscope for the holographic investigation of magnetic microstructures. It is equipped with a highly coherent field emission gun and an electron biprism; the magnetic objective lens is replaced by an electrostatic one to prevent any magnetic influence on the specimen. Using this instrument we are studying the limits of electron holography for the detectability of magnetic structures found for very small object sizes.

articleTitle: A technique for decoding two frequency coherent phase recorded data using a digital decoder circuit
abstract: Two-frequency coherent phase (F2F) recording is a technique used for encoding data on magnetic stripe cards. In this method, a series of binary bits representing the data are encoded in terms of magnetised areas of different polarities along the tracks. The conventional method for decoding F2F is by using software. A purpose built digital decoder circuit can however greatly enhance the systems performance, such as speed. This paper describes a computerised security lock and access system using the digital decoder circuits to decode data retrieved from a hand held magnetic stripe card reader, and send it to the central computer via a parallel I/O converter.

articleTitle: Magnetic and magneto-photoellipsometric evaluation of corrosion in metal-particle media
abstract: Considerable current interest centers around the question of the viability of metal-particle tape as a mass data storage medium for archival systems. Much of the concern relates to the possibility that the sub-microscopic metal (i.e. iron) particles will be somewhat sensitive to ambient moisture and will, ultimately, corrode. The problem is therefore one of considerable importance since it can call into question the security of data bases of national agencies. As one would expect, much of the current experimental evidence concerning MP tape is contradictory. Recent experimental studies by Djalali et al<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> have concentrated on degradation of surface layers of MP tape by evaluation of dropouts and read errors at high linear write densities. Current studies in these laboratories indicate clearly that volumetric methods of measurement such as a vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) are of little value in the detection of the onset of metal particle corrosion. Fig.1 indicates the changes, as indicated by the VSM, in M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>. H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> and squareness ratio in commercial D2 tape exposed for several weeks in a humidity chamber at 60°C, 90% relative humidity. Evidently, no significant changes in bulk magnetic properties can be detected.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: No-load induction motor core losses using a combined finite element-state space model
abstract: The majority of previous electric machinery design and analysis work was done with the aid of mathematical transformations, such as Park's transformation. When using such transforms the winding mmfs and flux density waveforms implicitly exclude any harmonics beyond the fundamental. In this paper a Combined Finite Element-State Space (CFE-SS) modeling approach is used. The CFE-SS environment is totally within the embrace of the ABC frame of reference. Consequently the currents, flux linkages, winding mmfs and flux density waveforms include as many space harmonic terms as necessary. The number of included harmonics depends only on the spatial resolution of the computed series of magnetostatic finite element solutions, a parameter that can be varied by the analyst. The resulting harmonically rich flux density waveforms are used to calculate hysteresis and eddy current losses. In addition, the above results arc compared with conventionally computed core losses obtained using only the fundamental of the flux density waveform.

articleTitle: Polarization magnetooptic bistability in films
abstract: Optic bistability (OB) means the presence of two steady States of the output intensity of the wave that passed through an optic device with the same input intensity of the wave. Polarization magnetooptic bistability (PMOB of Faraday effect) is meant here as two steady states of polarization of electromagnetic wave (EMW) that passed through a magnetooptic device (easy plane ferro- and antiferromagnetic (EPF and EPAF) films are considered here) with constant output intensity and polarization.

articleTitle: Characteristics of level and two-axis attitude detector a using magnetic fluid
abstract: The usual angle detector can detect an angle in one axis only, and cannot detect the level alone. The detector described in this paper is able to detect angles of orientation with respect to horizontal and vertical planes. In addition, the new detector can detect level by itself for using fluids, such as water levels.

articleTitle: Ferrite head instability
abstract: Narrow-track ferrite heads for digital data recording can exhibit undesirable isolated transition responses. Investigated here were polycrystalline MnZn MIG ferrite heads (Fig. (a)) with single Sendust films (thickness 1.4 μm) having trackwidths of 9 μm and gaps of 0.45 μm. In response to isolated transitions written on a thin-film disk (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 9.5 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> A/m, M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>t = 37 mA) some of these heads showed distorted readback waveforms such as the one in (b). This waveform is the trace-average of 64 waveforms, each taken after a write operation (measured transitions not rewritten). The isolated impulse shows on the leading edge a precursory phenomenon (foot), while the trailing edge is not different from a normal impulse as shown in (c). The "foot" in (b) causes left-right asymmetry of the Isolated impulse which shins the VCO timing for closely written transitions, Introducing errors. This foot is believed to be caused by one or more high-reluctance crystallites adjacent to the gap. In (d) it is shown that if such a crystallite has a magnetic orientation in approximately the same direction as the flux lines emanating from a transition under the gap, it exhibits a low, local permeability, and therefore effectively widens the head gap. Since this orientation is determined by the shape, crystalline orientation, scratches, stresses and effects of segregation at crystallite boundaries, this effect is write-excitation independent; the micro-magnetic behavior is "frozen in" at the time of manufacturing. If the magnetic orientation is as in (d) at the right. i.e. at right angles with the flux lines, the respective crystallite can show a high, rotational /spl mu, and produce a sharp magnetic gap-edge definition, leading to isolated impulse responses as in (c).

articleTitle: Evaluation of capacitance displacement sensors used for slider-disk spacing measurements in magnetic disk drives
abstract: Capacitance probe (CP) sliders have been used in recent years for evaluating relative slider-disk spacing and dynamics during various processes. In Suk et al. the CP and multi-channel laser interferometer (MCLI) flying height measurements made during contact-start-stop (CSS) were found to agree when the calibration factor for the CP was derived on the basis of the capacitance-spacing relationship given in Best. However, when using this relationship with the CP to measure spacing variation over one disk revolution, and then comparing that result with what was obtained from the MCLI, we obtained the results in Fig. 1. Here we see that the waveforms are very similar, but the amplitudes are quite different, the CP result having a much smaller amplitude. The cause is related to the CP pad size, but it is somewhat more subtle than wavelength averaging. It results from the fact that spacing variation is a function of position along the slider, as explained in Zhu and Bogy.

articleTitle: Theoretical consideration of Faraday rotation spectra in bismuth substituted yttrium iron garnet films
abstract: It is well known that bismuth substituted rare earth iron garnet (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</sub>Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>, Bi:RIG, where R denotes rare earth element) exhibit large magneto-optical Faraday rotation in wavelengths ranging from the visible to infrared regions. The origin of Faraday rotation of Bi:YIG (i.e. yttrium is used for R in the above chemical formula) films was investigated theoretically by Scott et al. and Shinagawa. Simsa et al. also attempted to interpret their Faraday rotation spectra (FRS) data of LPE grown Bi:YIG films with the bismuth content X < 0.3 theoretically. However, no theoretical studies of FRS for heavy substituted Bi:YIG films have been done. Thus we attempted to explain FRS of Bi:YIG films with the bismuth content x < 2.0 by making a modification of the theories.

articleTitle: Thermal stability and corrosion resistance of Fe based high moment magnetic materials for thin film recording heads
abstract: Recently Fe based materials such as FeN, FeAlN and their multilayers have been shown very promising for high magnetization head applications. However, the thermal stability and corrosion resistance of these materials, which are extremely important to the fabrication process and product life of thin film recording heads, have not previously been thoroughly reported. This paper will present our investigations of the thermal stability and corrosion resistance of these films.

articleTitle: Simulation of wear of tape head contours
abstract: Sub-micron changes to head geometries can drastically affect the head/tape interface. For example, in the processing of head contours, a final lapping operation with abrasive tape is often required to obtain proper head/tape contact. Although this final lapping process may only remove a small amount of material, it generally results in a significant improvement in head/tape performance. Although many studies have been performed on the bulk wear properties of head materials, few investigations of head geometry changes due to wear have been made. In the existing papers, head geometry changes due to wear are calculated based on the assumption of a constant pressure between the head and tape. These papers indicate that the predicted wear profile is very close to the actual shape of a head after a large amount of wear. However, in order to predict changes of the head contour due to small amounts of wear immediately after manufacturing, these models can not be used.

articleTitle: Comparison of the mesh and the toroidal shaking coil from residual noise
abstract: The necessary condition for realizing magnetic shielding mom with well suppressed residual fields is to be not only a large shielding factor but also low emission of magnetic noise from the shielding walls. We have already shown that comparing to conventional Permalloy shield, a 20 - 30 times better shielding factor can be obtained by applying magnetic shaking (MS) to the square-loop material. We have also proposed mesh shaking coils which, compared to a toroidal shaking coil, substantially reduce the shaking field leaking out of the shielding walls. In this paper, we will further discuss the characteristics of those shaking coils from the view point of residual noise. Two kinds of noises are measured by a fluxgate magnetometer at the center of the cylindrical shielding case with both shaking coils on it. Those two noises are background noise resulting from Barkhausen noise in the magnetic material and demodulated noise caused by nonlinear effect of the material under the external disturbing fields and the shaking field. The shielding case was prepared using a plastic pipe of 20 cm in diameter and 40 cm in length, on which Metglas 2705M amorphous ribbons were wound helically in four layers. A 10-turn toroidal coil and a mesh coil with 2cm square-mesh were placed after winding two layers and two more layers were wound over the coils.

articleTitle: Single-sided linear induction motor controlling the surface shape of molten tin
abstract: We apply a Single-sided Linear Induction Motor (SLIM) to control the surface shape of molten metal. There is no precedent for such use of a SLIM in the applications of controlling molten metal. In the float process of producing flat glass it is required for a glass ribbon to leave the molten tin bath horizontally to improve the quality and the operation. Our new technique using a SLIM allows one to keep the level of molten tin higher than the fence and to withdraw the glass ribbon horizontally from molten tin bath without the interference of the outlet fence. We already verified the basic principle by using a 0.3m-wide SLIM and a molten metal. This paper presents theoretical and experimental analyses to demonstrate the surface shape control of molten tin, which can be used in the practical float process, by a 1.5m-wide SLIM. In addition, two types of SLIM mechanisms are compared from the stand point of the location of SLIM.

articleTitle: Side reading study of recording heads
abstract: The side reading of recording heads from adjacent tracks becomes increasingly important in high track-density environments. Often trackwidths are reduced without properly scaling head geometries and written transition spacings. The resultant side reading can increase the noise-to-signal ratio, thus degrading the error-rate performance. Traditionally, track profiles have been used to evaluate the side reading behavior of ferrite heads, thin-film inductive (TFI) and magnetoresistive (MR) heads, where the fundamental frequency component of the readback signal was measured in the frequency domain and plotted against the offtrack displacement. In this work, a time-domain method for characterizing the side reading of various recording heads is described. It provides information such as the side-reading amplitude and its data-pattern dependence as well as readback-signal distortions, not obtainable from frequency domain measurements. The results on MlG, TFI and shielded MR heads will he presented.

articleTitle: Magnetic Behavior of clusters of transition metals
abstract: The developments in molecular beam techniques have permitted studies on clusters of atoms in an interaction free environment. The recent interest has focused on magnetic behavior. Stern- Garlach experiments on clusters of Fe, Co, and Cr have revealed several startling results. Contrary to the case of individual atoms, all the clusters underwent deflection in the same direction. For Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> and Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> clusters, the magnetic moment per atom deduced from the Stern Garlech deflections were substantially below the bulk values. This is opposite to theoretical expectations which had predicted enhanced moments in reduced sizes and dimensions. The magnetic moment per atom for Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> and Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> clusters was found to increase linearly with cluster size and with magnetic field. The size dependence again defies the expectation of increased moments at smaller sizes. For Cr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> clusters the measured moments were less than 0.01 μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>.

articleTitle: Static magnetic field deformation by a ferromagnetic body
abstract: The deformation of a static magnetic field by a soft nonlinear magnetic material using the boundary element method was recently discussed. That analysis was not able to handle magnetic materials that supported remanent magnetizations. A model that can accurately handle both reversible and irreversible magnetic processes has been introduced. Although this model, referred to as VD-3, in quite sophisticated, by appropriate choices of the seven parameters reduces to other similar models. This paper addresses the use of this model to the deformation problem. Due to the complexity of the inclusion of this model into a field calculation, the finite difference method is used. It is expected that after all of the implementation problems have been solved, a boundary element analysis will be used to permit the handling of complex boundaries.

articleTitle: Synthesis and characterization of stable colloidal De/sub 3/O/sub 4/ particles in water-in-oil microemulsions
abstract: Inverted micelles have been shown to be useful versatile systems for forming stable small (5 Å radius) particles of CDS. In this work we prepared nano-scaled magnetite particles using a micellar reaction technique. The micellar system used was the Aerosol OT (AOT)/water/isooctane water-in-oil (w/o) microemulsion. In this technique water droplets in the microemulsion interact and exchange their contents. Magnetite particles can be easily prepared by a precipitation reaction of aqueous Fe (III)/Fe (II) and NaOH solutions.

articleTitle: A new maximum likelihood detection for DAT system
abstract: In as earlier paper, the application of Viterbi algorithm to partial response on magnetic recording channel was discussed. We bare developed a new maximum likelihood detection (MLD) with the trellis path limited by channel coding. This new MLD is possible to be parallel decoding of byte datas and has an effect to decreasing error detections. Employing this new method, a transfer rate of 22.2Mbps and in areal recording density of 419Mbpi were achieved on DAT system. (Digital Audio Taperecorder). We have investigated symbol error rate and recorded video signal of Digital S.N.G.

articleTitle: Novel technique for ferrimagnetic resonance measurement
abstract: The ferrimagnetic resonance (FMR) linewidth (ΔH) and resonant magnetic field of single crystal (Mn-Doped) Ba<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Zn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sub> were measured as a function of frequency from 2 to 20 GHz. These measurements were performed utilizing an improved coupling scheme between the measurement device and ferrite specimen. Previous measurements with respect to the linewidth had been inconclusive.

articleTitle: A compensation scheme for head-to-tape misregistration in multiple track tape systems
abstract: The reduction in track widths and spacings used to increase the areal packing densities of storage devices compounds the problem of maintaining alignment between the replay head and the recorded information. Such misalignment reduces the amplitude of the replayed signal and can cause interference from an adjacent track, reducing the SNR and increasing the probability of errors. Rather than investigate coding schemes that are passively robust or resilient to such effects, a technique has been developed (similar to the linear processor' developed by Barbosa) that actively compensates for the effects of Lateral Head Displacement (LHD), reducing errors.

articleTitle: Magnetic characterisation of metal particle pigment dispersions
abstract: Metal particle tapes are currently of considerable commercial interest because of their suitability for high density storage applications. The high remanent moment and small particle volume associated with metal particles do however introduce considerably higher demands on their method of dispersion, compared to the traditional acicular, low coercivity, particles. Similarly, the requirement for effective dispersion characterisation, prior to final coating, becomes critical. Recent studies on characterisation have used a variety of techniques including rheomagnetometry, light scattering, small angle x-ray scattering, and rheological measurements. In this study we have investigated the behaviour of 'wet' metal particle dispersions, as a function of milling time, using a variety of magnetic characterisation techniques.

articleTitle: Study on cause of quench at joint between multifilamentary superconducting cable and copper plate using 3-D FEM
abstract: In the ac superconducting electrical machine, the superconducting cable is connected with the normal conducting copper wire through a copper plate. If the ac current is increased, the quench occurs at the joint. As a resulut, the rated current of the superconducting electrical machine is limited to a smaller value than that of ac superconducting cable itself. Since the superconducting cable is multifilamentary, it is difficult to analyze 3-D current distribution at the joint. Therefore, the cause of quench was not clear. Since 3-D numerical method for analyzing the twisted multifilamentary conductor has been developed by us [1], the current distribution is calculated taking into account of eddy current. It is found out that the cause of the quench is the extreme concentration of current at the joint due to the remarkable skin effect in the copper plate under liquid helium temperature.

articleTitle: A new method of Te-Tm mode conversion in thin magneto-optical film
Systhesis and properties of magnetically hard two element Sm/sub 6/Fe/sub 17/ phase in sputtered films
abstract: Magnetically hard two element Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> phase has now been obtained in sputtered films. The films were crystallized from amorphous sputter deposits. Film composition was determined to be Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21.9</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">78.1</sub>. The films were found to be nearly single phase with only traces of α-Fe present, consistent with the measured Sm concentration of the film which is slightly less than the 5-17 stoichiometry of 22.7 atomic percent. All the observed lines in the x-ray diffraction pattern of these polycrystalline films could be fitted to a hexagonal cell of a=20.06±0.01 A, c= 12.28±0.01 A. A nearly random distribution for the easy magnetic axes of the crystallites is seen on comparison of the observed diffraction line intensities o these films with the calculated powder diffraction pattern of the 5-17 phase.

articleTitle: A new magnetic sensor utilizing separated drift field
abstract: Magnetotransistors may be the most promising magnetic sensor. Magnetotransistors are based on the bipolar junction transistor. The widely used operating principles of magnetotransistors are emitter injection modulation and carrier deflection. The large increase of sensitivity of magnetotransistors can be achieved using emitter injection modulation. However, there were some experimental and numerical results that emitter injection modulation can be ruled out as an operating principle. On the contrary, recent study shows that emitter injection modulation is related to the drift carrier transport and it is necessary to separate the electric field with the junction behavior in order to utilize the emitter injection modulation as an operating principle of the magnetotransistor.

articleTitle: A study of MiG head readout waveform asymmetry with magnetic force and Kerr Microscopy
abstract: In ferrite MlG heads used in bard disk drives, bit shift caused by asymmetry distortion in readback waveforms becomes more pronounced at higher recording densities. The origin of asymmetry has been said to be mainly Barkhausen transient phenomena. However, little work has been done to verify the connection between magnetic domain distributions and readback waveform asymmetry in narrow track MIG heads. In this paper, we attempt to clarify the cause of the readback waveform distortion in ferrite MlG heads using a magnetic force microscope (MFM) and also an optical microscope capable of micro-ellipsometry for grain contrast and Kerr contrast for domain microscopy. Use of a specialized MFM tip enables us to measure the fringing field near the surface. Domain distributions at the surface are observed for comparison using wide-field Kerr microscopy. Results from both experiments in the critical region near the gap are described for heads exhibiting low and high asymmetry in their readback waveforms.

articleTitle: A torque transducer utilizing a circularly polarized ring
abstract: Recent efforts to develop suitable torque transducers for automotive and industrial applications have focused on two measurement technologies: elastic systems based on the relationship between torque and torsional strain, and magnetoelastic systems based on relationships between magnetic properties and the torsional stress by which torque is transmitted. Elastic systems commonly employ magnetic encoders or differential inductors/transformers to measure the torque associated strain in a dedicated shaft segment (i.e., twist angle of a "torsion bar"). Since sensitivity of this measurement increases directly with mechanical compliance, elastic systems are often undesirably large and soft for an intended application. While allowing for much stiffer systems and shorter shaft segments, conventional magnetoelastic torque transducers derive their output signals from stress induced variations in permeability, a property generally more highly dependent on excitation and environmental conditions than on stress. To attain acceptable zero and sensitivity stability, elaborate compensation method. are often required in the associated excitation/signal conditioning electronics thereby increasing costs.

articleTitle: Thin film thermocouple sensors for measurement of contact temperatures during slider asperity interaction on magnetic recording disks
abstract: In magnetic hard disks drives, increased recording densities may be achieved by flying the slider carrying the magnetic transducer closer to the disk surface. This decreased spacing increases the probability of contact between the slider and disk asperities. Measurement of temperature increase during such contacts is critical for determining the nature and damage of these events. We report here a novel thin film thermocouple/ resistive temperature sensor which has been used to detect in real time the temperature increase of slider and asperity contacts and to measure the average temperature of the head-disk interface during flying.

articleTitle: Spin reorientation in Tm/sub 2.14/Bi/sub 0.08/Pb/sub 0.06/Fe/sub 3.1/Ga/sub 1.9/O/sub 12/ thin films
abstract: Bi doped garnet materials are currently of interest for their application as a magneto-optic material. Stability of the spin orientation is an important factor in this application. The present work reports the study of the spin orientation by magnetization and ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) measurements in a garnet thin film having the composition Tm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.14</sub>Bi0.80Pb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.06</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.1</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.9</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> grown on [lll] oriented GGG substrate by the LPE method. From 25 K to 160 K, the in-plane component of the magnetization decreases from 4 πM = 590 Gauss to zero. From 80 K, the normal component increases from zero to a maximum value of 4 πM = 150 Gauss at 100 K and then decreases to 4 πM = 52 Gauss at 300 K. This data is shown in Figure 1 and suggests that a continuous spin reorientation occurs from easy plane to easy axis over this temperature range.

articleTitle: High frequency characteristics of multilayered thin film heads
abstract: It is well known that the permeability in multilayered films remains to be large in the high frequency range. This is probably because the domain structure is almost single except in the region close to the edge. In this study, we investigate the advantages of multilayered heads compared with single layered heads.
